knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Equivalence of Separation and Linear Optimization over Rational Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded bidirectional polynomial-time reduction for rational-polyhedron families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P=\{P(n,T)\}\) be a family of rational polyhedra whose input length is at least polynomial in \(n\) and \(\log T\). Linear optimization over \(\mathcal P\) is polynomial-time reducible to separation over \(\mathcal P\), and separation over \(\mathcal P\) is polynomial-time reducible to linear optimization over \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For rational-polyhedron families satisfying the stated input-length condition, linear optimization and separation reduce to one another in polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: P(n,T)\text{ is a rational polyhedron for every member of }\mathcal P
\operatorname{len}(P(n,T))\geq \operatorname{poly}(n,\log T)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}(\mathcal P)\leq_p\operatorname{SEP}(\mathcal P)\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{SEP}(\mathcal P)\leq_p\operatorname{OPT}(\mathcal P)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial-Time Equivalence of Separation and Optimization for Polytopes and Their 1-Polars
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded oracle equivalence under full-dimensionality, interior-origin, and input-length hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P=\{P(n,T)\}\) be a family of full-dimensional polytopes such that \(0\in\operatorname{int}P(n,T)\) and the input length is at least polynomial in \(n\) and \(\log T\). The following are equivalent: polynomial-time separation over \(\mathcal P\), polynomial-time linear optimization over \(\mathcal P\), polynomial-time separation over the family of 1-polars \(\mathcal P^{\circ_1}\), and polynomial-time linear optimization over \(\mathcal P^{\circ_1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For full-dimensional polytopes containing the origin in their interiors and satisfying the stated input-length condition, polynomial-time separation and linear optimization are equivalent for both the original family and its family of 1-polars.
assumptions_latex: P(n,T)\text{ is full-dimensional for every member of }\mathcal P
0\in\operatorname{int}P(n,T)
\operatorname{len}(P(n,T))\geq \operatorname{poly}(n,\log T)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SEP}(\mathcal P)\in\mathbf P\iff\operatorname{OPT}(\mathcal P)\in\mathbf P\iff\operatorname{SEP}(\mathcal P^{\circ_1})\in\mathbf P\iff\operatorname{OPT}(\mathcal P^{\circ_1})\in\mathbf P

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separation Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership testing and separation relative to the convex hull of a feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the separation problem asks whether \(x^*\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\). If not, it asks for an inequality \(\pi x\leq\pi_0\) satisfied by every \(x\in X\) but violated by \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Determine whether a given point belongs to the convex hull of the feasible set; if it does not, find an inequality valid for every feasible point and violated by the given point.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n
x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\quad\text{or}\quad\exists\pi,\pi_0:\ (\forall x\in X,\ \pi x\leq\pi_0)\ \land\ \pi x^*>\pi_0.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\text{ for all }i\in I\}\), where each listed inequality is valid for \(C\).
The query point is \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a violated valid inequality or the declaration \(\bar x\in C\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set described by the indexed inequalities
Violation of inequality i at the query point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact search over a specified valid-inequality family.

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar x\), compute or optimize the violations \(v_i(\bar x)=a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_i\) over \(i\in I\). If some \(i^*\in I\) satisfies \(v_{i^*}(\bar x)>0\), return \((a_{i^*},b_{i^*})\); a most-violated rule chooses \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in I}v_i(\bar x)\). If \(v_i(\bar x)\le0\) for every \(i\in I\), return \(\bar x\in C\). For infinite \(I\), the final declaration requires attainment or a certified upper bound on \(\sup_{i\in I}v_i(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search the defining valid inequalities for positive violation; return a violated inequality, preferably a maximizer, or certify membership when every violation is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.title: Violated-Inequality Search

children.title: Membership Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates supporting membership conclusions for a queried point.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{Q}^n:Ax\le b\}\), with rational \(A\) and \(b\) explicitly encoded.
The query point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) is explicitly encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed slack vector certifies whether \(\bar x\) satisfies every displayed inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct membership certificates for explicitly represented rational polyhedra.

source_refs.locator: 8.1 Implicit equalities and redundant constraints p. 99
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A membership certificate for \(\bar x\in P\) is the rational vector \(s=b-A\bar x\) together with the assertion \(s\ge0\) componentwise. Verification recomputes \(A\bar x+s=b\) and checks every component of \(s\) is nonnegative. If a component \(s_i<0\), the corresponding row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) instead certifies nonmembership. With binary rational encoding, these arithmetic and sign checks require time polynomial in the encoded sizes of \(A\), \(b\), and \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an explicit rational inequality system, the nonnegative slack vector is a directly checkable membership certificate; a negative slack identifies a violated row.
knowledge_statements.title: Membership Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 8.1 Implicit equalities and redundant constraints p. 99
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The slack certificate is mathematically correct and the certificate kind fits, but the cited section on implicit equalities and redundant constraints does not clearly support the certificate interpretation or polynomial bit-complexity claim. A specific supporting locator is required.

children.title: Nonseparation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates supporting the absence of a qualifying separating inequality.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\text{ for all }i\in I\}\).
A separation subproblem computes \(V(\bar x)=\sup_{i\in I}(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A verifiable upper bound \(V(\bar x)\le0\) certifies that no inequality in the family separates \(\bar x\) from \(C\).

notation.meaning: Set represented by the inequality family

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonseparation requires a checkable upper bound on maximum violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonseparation relative to a fixed complete inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonseparation certificate is finite data from which a verifier can establish \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_i\le0\) for every \(i\in I\), equivalently \(V(\bar x)\le0\). For finite explicit \(I\), the complete slack vector suffices. For an implicitly indexed family, an admissible certificate may instead be a verifiable optimality certificate for the maximization defining \(V(\bar x)\), provided its bound is valid for every index. Such a certificate proves \(\bar x\in C\) only when the family represents all defining inequalities of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonseparation is certified by a checkable upper bound showing that the maximum violation over the complete inequality family is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparation Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly distinguishes finite slack evidence from a global optimality certificate for an implicit family, but no source supports the admissibility and verification conditions for such nonseparation certificates.

children.title: Certificate Verification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Verification scope, access requirements, and inconclusive-certificate regimes.

assumptions_latex: The set is given by an inequality family indexed by \(I\).
Certificates are required to have polynomial encoded length and polynomial-time verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive separation answer has a short certificate only when the returned inequality is efficiently validated; a negative answer does so only when universal nonviolation is efficiently certified.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: existential and universal oracle answers have different verification requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between oracle answers and independently checkable certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Returning \((a,b)\) with \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b\) is not by itself a certificate unless the verifier can also establish that \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid for the represented set. Conversely, reporting that no member of an implicit family is violated asserts \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x\le b_i\) for all \(i\in I\); checking sampled indices cannot verify this universal claim. Thus oracle solvability does not imply polynomial certificate verification unless validity and global nonviolation admit polynomial-size, polynomially checkable witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle answer becomes a certificate only when inequality validity or universal nonviolation can be independently checked with a suitably short witness.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Verification Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits and the existential-versus-universal verification distinction is plausible, but the polynomial witness and verification claims require an authoritative complexity-theoretic source.

children.title: Strong Separation
children.top_down_role: The strong separation regime and its attainable certificates.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The query point is \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle either confirms membership or returns a hyperplane strictly separating \(\bar x\) from all of \(C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard strong separation predicate for closed convex sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact strong separation for a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strong separation oracle for \(C\) maps each \(\bar x\) either to the declaration \(\bar x\in C\), or to \((a,\beta)\in(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\})\times\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>\beta\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in C\). Equivalently, its separating output satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>\sup_{x\in C}a^{\mathsf T}x\). The returned inequality is therefore valid for the entire target set and strictly violated by the query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong separation either recognizes membership or returns an inequality valid for the whole closed convex set and strictly violated by the query point.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent exact strong-separation definition for a nonempty closed convex set, but no inspectable citation establishes the chosen oracle convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oracle-polynomial strong separation for a recession cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A derived strong-separation guarantee for the recession cone of a well-described polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((P;n,\varphi)\) be a well-described polyhedron given by a strong separation oracle. Then the strong separation problem for \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\) can be solved in oracle-polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a strong separation oracle for a well-described polyhedron, strong separation for its recession cone can be solved in oracle-polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: (P;n,\varphi)\text{ is a well-described polyhedron}
P\text{ is given by a strong separation oracle}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{StrongSeparation}(\operatorname{rec}(P))\text{ is solvable in oracle-polynomial time.}

children.title: Weak Separation
children.top_down_role: The weak separation regime and its relaxed outcomes.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex, and \(\varepsilon>0\).
Define \(C^{+\varepsilon}=\{z:\operatorname{dist}(z,C)\le\varepsilon\}\) and \(C^{-\varepsilon}=\{z:B(z,\varepsilon)\subseteq C\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle may accept points in the outer thickening and otherwise separates the query point from the inner core.

notation.meaning: Outer and inner Euclidean offsets of C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weak separation uses inner and outer tolerance sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean weak separation using inner and outer offsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An \(\varepsilon\)-weak separation oracle, on input \(\bar x\), returns either the declaration \(\bar x\in C^{+\varepsilon}\), or a nonzero \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x\ge a^{\mathsf T}y\) for every \(y\in C^{-\varepsilon}\). When \(C^{-\varepsilon}=\varnothing\), the separating alternative is vacuous, so a useful oracle specification must additionally assume a nonempty inner core or prescribe behavior in that case. Acceptance need not prove exact membership, and the cut need not separate \(\bar x\) from boundary points excluded from the inner core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak separation tolerates an outer membership error and may require separation only from an eroded inner core of the target set.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Weak-separation conventions vary in their offset sets, normalization, margin, and empty-inner-core behavior. The stated convention is internally coherent but requires a specific authoritative source before acceptance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Separation Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines separation with a membership tolerance and an additive inequality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $y\in\mathbb{Q}^n$ and $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, the weak separation problem is to either determine that $y\in S(K,\delta)$, or find $c\in\mathbb{Q}^n$ with $\lVert c\rVert_\infty=1$ such that $c^\top x\leq c^\top y+\delta$ for every $x\in K$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a rational point y and a positive rational tolerance δ, either determine that y belongs to S(K,δ), or return a rational vector c of infinity norm one such that cᵀx ≤ cᵀy+δ for every x in K.
assumptions_latex: y\in\mathbb{Q}^n
\delta\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\in S(K,\delta)\quad\text{or}\quad \exists c\in\mathbb{Q}^n:\ \lVert c\rVert_\infty=1\ \land\ \forall x\in K,\ c^\top x\leq c^\top y+\delta.

children.title: Strength-Gap Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem classes and access conditions separating the two regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex.
Weak separation is interpreted through \(C^{+\varepsilon}\) and \(C^{-\varepsilon}\) for \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak separation does not imply exact strong separation without quantitative geometry and controlled limiting precision.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tolerance regions prevent unconditional recovery of exact separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric boundary between strong and weak separation guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in C\), strong separation must accept \(x\), whereas weak separation may accept every \(x\in C^{+\varepsilon}\), including exterior points. A weak cut is required to dominate only \(C^{-\varepsilon}\), which may omit boundary points or be empty, while a strong cut must be valid for all of \(C\). Consequently, a fixed positive \(\varepsilon\) cannot resolve membership or separation inside the boundary layer \(C^{+\varepsilon}\setminus C^{-\varepsilon}\). Passing from weak to strong separation requires additional geometric bounds and arbitrarily controlled precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tolerance boundary layer hides exact membership and full-set cut validity, so fixed-accuracy weak separation cannot generally recover strong separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Strength-Gap Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the boundary-layer distinction follows from the selected weak-separation convention, but neither that convention nor the claimed requirements for recovering strong separation are sourced.

children.title: Exact Separation
children.top_down_role: Exact violated-inequality search and exact nonseparation outcomes.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is represented by a complete family \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), indexed by \(I\).
The query point \(\bar x\) and all returned coefficients are represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle decides exact membership in the represented set or returns an actually violated valid inequality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: zero-tolerance separation over a complete inequality representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-tolerance separation over a complete inequality representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact separation oracle returns \(\bar x\in C\) if and only if \(V(\bar x)\le0\). Otherwise it returns an index \(i\in I\) satisfying \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b_i\). Thus neither a positive feasibility tolerance nor an approximate comparison may convert a strictly positive violation into membership. Exact separation does not require the most violated inequality, but every separating output must be exactly valid for \(C\) and exactly violated by \(\bar x\) under the chosen arithmetic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact separation uses zero tolerance: it certifies true membership or returns a valid inequality with strictly positive violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-tolerance definition is precise for a complete inequality family and correctly does not require a most-violated row, but it has no authoritative locator.

children.title: Approximate Separation
children.top_down_role: Approximation regimes for violation detection or cut quality.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\text{ for all }i\in I\}\) and \(\delta\ge0\).
The query point is \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle either finds violation exceeding \(\delta\) or certifies that every family violation is at most \(\delta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive approximation is expressed through maximum family violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive approximate separation for a normalized inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(\delta\)-additive separation oracle returns either an index \(i\in I\) with \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_i>\delta\), or the certificate \(V(\bar x)\le\delta\). The latter places \(\bar x\) in the relaxed intersection \(C_\delta=\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i+\delta\text{ for all }i\in I\}\), not necessarily in \(C\). Because rescaling an inequality rescales its violation, this guarantee is representation-dependent unless a normalization such as \(\lVert a_i\rVert_2=1\) is imposed for every nonzero row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive approximate separation detects violations above a tolerance or certifies membership in a relaxed inequality system; row normalization is essential.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive formulation is internally consistent and correctly identifies its representation dependence, but approximate-separation conventions vary and no source supports this particular guarantee.

children.title: Approximation Guarantee Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Accuracy measures, admissible losses, and excluded guarantees.

assumptions_latex: Approximate separation is stated through raw additive violations \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_i\).
Equivalent inequalities may be multiplied by arbitrary scalars \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without normalization, an additive violation guarantee is not invariant under equivalent representations and has no intrinsic geometric meaning.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive algebraic violation changes under positive row scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation dependence of additive separation guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequalities \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) and \((\lambda a)^{\mathsf T}x\le\lambda b\) define the same halfspace for every \(\lambda>0\), but their violations at \(\bar x\) are respectively \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b\) and \(\lambda(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b)\). Hence the predicate that violation is at most \(\delta\) can be made true or false by rescaling when \(\delta>0\). A representation-invariant guarantee therefore requires fixed normalization, a geometric distance convention, or another scale rule; it still does not certify exact membership when \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves the feasible set but changes additive violation, so approximate guarantees require normalization or a geometric error convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Guarantee Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaling calculation correctly identifies the failure of representation invariance for positive additive violations, and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the record lacks a supporting source.

children.title: Separation Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Oracle abstractions distinguished by the representation exposed to the separator and the strength of the returned result.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Separation Oracle Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines weak-separation access together with a polynomial output-encoding requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A circumscribed convex set $(K;n,R)$ is given by a weak separation oracle if, for every $y\in\mathbb{Q}^n$ and $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, the oracle solves the weak separation problem, and the encoding size of any separator $c$ it returns is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ and the encoding sizes of $R$, $y$, and $\delta$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A circumscribed convex set is given by a weak separation oracle when the oracle solves weak separation for every rational query point and positive rational tolerance, with every returned separator having encoding length polynomial in the dimension and the encoding lengths of R, y, and δ.
assumptions_latex: (K;n,R)\text{ is a circumscribed convex set}
y\in\mathbb{Q}^n
\delta\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall y\in\mathbb{Q}^n\;\forall\delta\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0},\ \mathcal O(y,\delta)\text{ solves weak separation, and each returned }c\text{ satisfies }\operatorname{size}(c)\leq\operatorname{poly}\bigl(n,\operatorname{size}(R),\operatorname{size}(y),\operatorname{size}(\delta)\bigr).

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{Q}^n:Ax\le b\}\), where the rational matrix \(A\) and vector \(b\) are explicit.
The query point is \(\bar x\in\mathbb{Q}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scanning the displayed rows gives an exact separation oracle whose arithmetic cost is polynomial in the explicit input size.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-scanning oracle for an explicit rational inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(s=b-A\bar x\). If every component satisfies \(s_i\ge0\), output \(\bar x\in P\). Otherwise choose any \(i\) with \(s_i<0\) and return the displayed valid inequality \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), which satisfies \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b_i\). Choosing a minimum-slack row returns a most violated row under the given scaling. For \(m\) rows, the oracle uses \(O(mn)\) rational arithmetic operations under dense storage, with bit complexity polynomial in the encoded input and intermediate arithmetic sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an explicit rational system, evaluate every row; accept if all slacks are nonnegative, otherwise return a row having negative slack.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-Inequality-Family Oracles

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex set specified without enumerating all of its valid inequalities.
An auxiliary routine can optimize a prescribed violation function over the implicit inequality index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the auxiliary problem implements separation when its optimum exactly characterizes membership and yields a valid inequality from any positive optimizer.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: implicit separation is represented by optimization over an indexed valid-inequality family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation through optimization over an implicit inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(P=\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\text{ for every }i\in I\}\), while \(I\) or the corresponding rows are not explicitly listed. On input \(\bar x\), solve the auxiliary problem defining \(V(\bar x)\). If an optimizer \(i^*\) has positive value, return \(a_{i^*}^{\mathsf T}x\le b_{i^*}\); if a certified upper bound gives \(V(\bar x)\le0\), return \(\bar x\in P\). The oracle is computationally effective only when optimization, inequality recovery, validity checking, and the nonpositive bound meet the required complexity model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit-polyhedron oracle separates by optimizing violation over an unlisted inequality family and recovering either a violated row or a global nonpositive bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit-Polyhedron Oracles

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation by a discrete combinatorial subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rational query point \(x\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) and an implicitly indexed valid-inequality family \(a_s^{\mathsf T}z\le b_s\), \(s\in S\), compute an index \(s^*\in\arg\max_{s\in S}\{a_s^{\mathsf T}x-b_s\}\) using a combinatorial algorithm. If \(a_{s^*}^{\mathsf T}x-b_{s^*}>0\), return the violated inequality \(a_{s^*}^{\mathsf T}z\le b_{s^*}\); otherwise certify that no inequality in the family is violated. The oracle is polynomial-time when the combinatorial maximization and output encoding require time polynomial in the encoding length of \(x\) and the instance.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Optimization Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation reduced to optimization over an auxiliary feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathbb{Q}^n\), an auxiliary feasible set \(Y(x)\), and rational functions \(a:Y(x)\to\mathbb{Q}^n\) and \(b:Y(x)\to\mathbb{Q}\) such that every \(a(y)^{\mathsf T}z\le b(y)\) is valid for the target relaxation, solve \(v(x)=\max_{y\in Y(x)}\{a(y)^{\mathsf T}x-b(y)\}\). If \(v(x)>0\), output an optimizer \(y^*\) and its violated inequality. If \(v(x)\le0\), certify that no inequality represented by the auxiliary model is violated. Polynomial-time auxiliary optimization yields polynomial-time separation, provided coefficients and optimizers have polynomial encoding length.

The auxiliary optimum is attained or infeasibility is detectable.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Polyhedral Equivalence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong optimization–separation equivalence for well-described rational polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of nonempty rational polyhedra \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) whose defining inequalities have encoding length bounded polynomially by the instance encoding. In the rational Turing model, a polynomial-time strong separation oracle for \(P\) yields a polynomial-time algorithm that, for rational \(c\), decides whether \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in P\}\) is unbounded and otherwise returns an exact optimum. Conversely, polynomial-time exact linear optimization over \(P\), together with the same well-describedness bounds, yields polynomial-time strong separation. Thus optimization and separation are polynomial-time oracle reducible in this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For well-described rational polyhedra, exact linear optimization and strong separation can each be implemented with polynomially many polynomial-bit oracle operations.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty, well-described rational polyhedron.
All inputs and oracle outputs use binary rational encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact linear optimization and strong separation over \(P\) are polynomial-time oracle equivalent.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Oracle Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A tolerance-gap convention for weak separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and tolerance \(\delta>0\), a weak separation oracle receives \(x\in\mathbb{Q}^n\). It may certify \(x\in K+\delta B_2\), or return rational \((a,\beta)\) with \(\lVert a\rVert_2=1\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}y\le\beta\) for every \(y\in K\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta+\delta\). When \(x\) lies in the unresolved boundary band, either admissible response may be permitted. Complexity is measured jointly in the instance length, query length, and \(\log(1/\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak separation distinguishes points safely outside a convex set from points within a prescribed tolerance, leaving a boundary band unresolved.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(B_2\) is the Euclidean unit ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle supplies separation only when the query has margin at least \(\delta\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean outer offset of the target set

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Oracle Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive approximation of maximum inequality violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V(x)=\sup_{s\in S}\{a_s^{\mathsf T}x-b_s\}\) for a valid-inequality family \(a_s^{\mathsf T}z\le b_s\). An additive \(\varepsilon\)-approximate separation oracle returns an index \(\hat s\in S\) satisfying \(a_{\hat s}^{\mathsf T}x-b_{\hat s}\ge V(x)-\varepsilon\), or certifies \(V(x)\le\varepsilon\). Consequently, a returned inequality with positive violation is valid and violated, whereas a certificate establishes membership only in the relaxed set \(\{x:V(x)\le\varepsilon\}\). The running time is polynomial in the instance length, query length, and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) when the regime is fully polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive approximate oracle finds a cut within epsilon of maximum violation or certifies that every represented violation is at most epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
The supremum \(V(x)\) is finite and the requested approximate index is representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle certifies only \(V(x)\le\varepsilon\), not exact membership when \(\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: maximum violation at the query point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Approximate-Oracle Regimes leaf and consistently describes additive error in maximum violation. Because approximation models and their complexity dependence vary, the selected convention and certificate semantics require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Guarantee Degradation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of conclusions obtainable from inexact separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V(x)=\sup_{s\in S}(a_s^{\mathsf T}x-b_s)\) and suppose an oracle can certify only \(V(x)\le\varepsilon\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), this certificate need not imply \(V(x)\le0\): with target set \(K=(-\infty,0]\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) and query \(x=\varepsilon/2\), the sole inequality \(z\le0\) has violation \(V(x)=\varepsilon/2\). Hence exact membership, exact feasibility, and exact optimization–separation equivalence cannot generally be inferred from a fixed positive additive tolerance without additional margin, error-bound, or rounding assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive oracle tolerance can accept infeasible points, so exact feasibility and exact equivalence require additional margins, error bounds, or recovery assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The oracle uses an additive violation tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certificate \(V(x)\le\varepsilon\) does not generally imply \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Input Encoding Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary length convention for rational optimization data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(p\), define \(\langle p\rangle=1+\lceil\log_2(|p|+1)\rceil\). For a reduced rational \(r=p/q\) with \(q>0\), define \(\langle r\rangle=\langle p\rangle+\langle q\rangle\). The encoding size of a rational vector or matrix is the sum of its entries' encoding sizes plus dimensions and structural indices. For an optimization-or-separation instance \(I\), \(\langle I\rangle\) includes every explicitly supplied coefficient, dimension, combinatorial datum, and requested rational tolerance. Polynomial time means polynomial in \(\langle I\rangle\), not polynomial in coefficient magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Input size is the total binary length of rational coefficients, dimensions, structural data, and tolerances, rather than the numerical magnitude of coefficients.
assumptions_latex: Rational numbers are stored as reduced signed numerator and positive denominator in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantity \(\langle I\rangle\) is the bit-length parameter used for polynomial-time analysis.

notation.meaning: binary encoding length of an object

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shallow separation oracle for quasiconvex polynomial regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A continuous ellipsoid-method primitive; its use in integer algorithms is a specialization rather than its primary ownership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_0,\ldots,g_{m+1}\in\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]\) be quasiconvex polynomials of degree at most \(d\), with coefficient encoding sizes at most \(r\). Suppose \(F=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(\mathbf x)<0\}\subseteq\mathcal E(A,\widehat{\mathbf x})\), where \(A\) and \(\widehat{\mathbf x}\) have binary encoding size at most \(\ell\). In time \(m(\ln r)^{\mathrm O(1)}d^{\mathrm O(n)}\), an algorithm either certifies \(\mathcal E((n+1)^{-3}A,\widehat{\mathbf x})\subseteq F\subseteq\mathcal E(A,\widehat{\mathbf x})\), or returns \(\mathbf c\in\mathbb Q^n\setminus\{0\}\), of encoding length \((\ell+r)(dn)^{\mathrm O(1)}\), such that \(F\subseteq\mathcal E(A,\widehat{\mathbf x})\cap\{\mathbf x:\mathbf c^\top(\mathbf x-\widehat{\mathbf x})\le(n+1)^{-1}(\mathbf c^\top A\mathbf c)^{1/2}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quasiconvex polynomial region contained in an ellipsoid, the algorithm either certifies a fixed concentric inner ellipsoid or returns a rational shallow cut containing the entire feasible region.
assumptions_latex: g_0,\ldots,g_{m+1}\in\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]\text{ are quasiconvex}
\deg g_i\le d
\text{coefficient binary encoding size}\le r
F=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(\mathbf x)<0\}\subseteq\mathcal E(A,\widehat{\mathbf x})
\operatorname{size}(A),\operatorname{size}(\widehat{\mathbf x})\le\ell
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{In time }m(\ln r)^{\mathrm O(1)}d^{\mathrm O(n)},\text{ the algorithm returns either the stated inner-ellipsoid certificate or the stated rational shallow cut.}

knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Complexity Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial bit bounds for rational-polyhedral oracle reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a well-described rational polyhedron with facet complexity at most \(\varphi\), and let the rational query or objective data have encoding length \(L\). In an exact optimization–separation reduction, polynomial bit complexity requires that the number of oracle calls, rational arithmetic operations, and maximum encoding length of every generated query, cut, and intermediate rational number be bounded by a polynomial in \(n\), \(\varphi\), and \(L\). Under these bounds and a polynomial-time oracle, the complete reduction runs in polynomial Turing time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial oracle-call counts suffice for polynomial Turing time only when every query, cut, and intermediate rational also has polynomially bounded bit length.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) has a rational description with facet complexity bounded by \(\varphi\).
Oracle outputs use exact binary rational encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomial bounds on operation count and operand length imply polynomial total bit complexity.

children.title: Arithmetic Precision Effects
children.top_down_role: Precision sensitivity and finite-arithmetic limitations.

knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic Precision Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precision requirements for reliable cut and membership decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a valid inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le b\) is evaluated at \(x\) using approximations \(\tilde a\), \(\tilde b\), and \(\tilde x\). Then the violation error satisfies \[\left|(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)-(\tilde a^{\mathsf T}\tilde x-\tilde b)\right|\le \lVert a-\tilde a\rVert_*\lVert x\rVert+\lVert\tilde a\rVert_*\lVert x-\tilde x\rVert+|b-\tilde b|.\] Therefore the sign of the computed violation is guaranteed correct only when its absolute value exceeds this error bound; otherwise finite precision may turn a violated cut into an accepted inequality or conversely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sign of a computed cut violation is reliable only when the observed margin exceeds the accumulated coefficient, right-hand-side, and point errors.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) and \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\) are dual norms.
All displayed approximation errors are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violation margin exceeding the stated error bound preserves the exact sign.

notation.meaning: norm dual to the point-space norm

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Scope Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypotheses delimiting polynomial optimization–separation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Polynomial optimization–separation equivalence applies to convex sets supplied through compatible rational encodings and exact or appropriately specified weak oracles, with polynomial bounds on geometric descriptions and intermediate bit lengths. It does not by itself identify a violated member of an arbitrary prescribed inequality family, establish separation for a nonconvex integer-feasible set, or convert a fixed-error approximate oracle into an exact one. If rational well-describedness, oracle output-size bounds, or required interior and boundedness data for the chosen reduction are absent, polynomial oracle-call equivalence need not imply polynomial Turing-time equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equivalence concerns encoded convex sets and compatible oracle models; it does not automatically cover nonconvex sets, family-specific cuts, or uncontrolled approximation and bit growth.
assumptions_latex: Complexity is measured in the rational Turing model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing encoding, convexity, or oracle-compatibility hypotheses invalidates the unrestricted equivalence claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicitly represented family \(\mathcal F(I)=\{a_s^{\mathsf T}x\le b_s:s\in S(I)\}\) is polynomially separable if an algorithm, given an encoded instance \(I\) and rational point \(x\), either returns some \(s\in S(I)\) with \(a_s^{\mathsf T}x>b_s\) or certifies \(a_s^{\mathsf T}x\le b_s\) for every \(s\in S(I)\), using time polynomial in \(\langle I\rangle+\langle x\rangle\). The returned inequality and all intermediate data must also have polynomial encoding length. The family may contain exponentially many inequalities; only implicit access and separation complexity are constrained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is polynomially separable when exact violation detection and cut output take polynomial time in the encoded instance and query, despite possibly exponential family size.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomially Separable Families

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomially solvable separation for an indexed polyhedral family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform bit-complexity definition for indexed families of rational polyhedra, together with the analogous optimization definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((P_i\mid i\in\mathbb N)\) be a class of rational polyhedra. Suppose that, for every \(i\), natural numbers \(n_i\) and \(\varphi_i\) can be computed in time polynomially bounded by \(\log i\), with \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) and facet complexity at most \(\varphi_i\). Separation is polynomially solvable for this class if there is one algorithm that, for every input \((i,y)\) with \(y\in\mathbb Q^{n_i}\), solves separation for \(P_i\) at \(y\) in time polynomially bounded by \(\log i\) and \(\operatorname{size}(y)\). Polynomial solvability of optimization is defined analogously by replacing separation with optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation is polynomially solvable for an indexed rational-polyhedral family when its dimensions and facet-complexity bounds are efficiently computable from the index and a uniform algorithm separates every rational query point in time polynomial in the index length and query size. Optimization is defined analogously.
assumptions_latex: \forall i\in\mathbb N,\ P_i\text{ is a rational polyhedron}
n_i,\varphi_i\in\mathbb N\text{ are computable in time polynomially bounded by }\log i
P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}
\operatorname{facet\mbox{-}complexity}(P_i)\leq\varphi_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Separation is polynomially solvable when a uniform separator runs in }\operatorname{poly}(\log i,\operatorname{size}(y));\text{ optimization is defined analogously.}

Simplex-Tableau Rows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical tableau representation of a standard-form LP relative to a nonsingular basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), and let \(B\) and \(N\) partition the variable indices with the square matrix \(A_B\) nonsingular. Defining \(\bar b=A_B^{-1}b\) and \(\bar A=A_B^{-1}A_N\), the equality system has the tableau representation \[x_B=\bar b-\bar A x_N.\] Thus, for every \(i\in B\), its tableau row is \[x_i=\bar b_i-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j.\] These equations together with \(x_B\ge0\) and \(x_N\ge0\) represent \(P\) in the coordinates of basis \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular basis rewrites every basic variable as an affine function of the nonbasic variables; the tableau equations together with all variable bounds represent the standard-form relaxation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equations \(x_B=\bar b-\bar A x_N\), together with \(x_B\ge0\) and \(x_N\ge0\), give the simplex-tableau representation associated with \(B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translated simplicial outer cone induced by a feasible basis of a standard-form relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and let \(B\) be a nonsingular feasible basis with basic solution \(\bar x_N=0\) and \(\bar x_B=A_B^{-1}b\ge0\). For each \(j\in N\), define \(r^j\in\mathbb R^n\) by \(r^j_j=1\), \(r^j_\ell=0\) for \(\ell\in N\setminus\{j\}\), and \(r^j_B=-A_B^{-1}A_j\). The basis cone is \[C_B=\left\{\bar x+\sum_{j\in N}r^j s_j:s_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\in N\right\}=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x_N\ge0\}.\] It is obtained by dropping the restrictions \(x_B\ge0\), so \(P\subseteq C_B\); its tableau rays need not individually be feasible directions of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basis cone keeps the tableau equations and nonnegativity of nonbasic variables while dropping nonnegativity of basic variables, producing a translated polyhedral cone that contains the standard-form relaxation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(C_B=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x_N\ge0\}\) is the basis-cone representation induced by \(B\), and \(P\subseteq C_B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tableau-Pivot Search Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation of bases reachable through prescribed eligible simplex pivots and their tableau-derived cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an initial feasible basis \(B_0\), an eligibility relation for simplex pivots, and a tableau cut map \(g\) defined on eligible bases. The tableau-pivot search space is the directed graph \(\mathcal G=(\mathcal B,\mathcal E)\), where \(\mathcal B\) consists of the bases reachable from \(B_0\) by finite sequences of eligible pivots and \((B,B')\in\mathcal E\) exactly when one eligible pivot transforms \(B\) into \(B'\). Each vertex \(B\in\mathcal B\) is labeled by its tableau and, when defined, by the cut \(g(B)\). A search over a proper subset of \(\mathcal B\) can certify only what occurred at the visited bases; a claim about every basis in the prescribed search space requires exhaustive coverage of \(\mathcal B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Generating Linear Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized linear-program representation for selecting a disjunctive cut that separates a specified point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\) and let the finite disjunction have terms \(D^t x\ge d^t\) for \(t\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\). A normalized cut-generating linear program for \(\bar x\in\mathbb Q^n\) is \[\min\ \alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\] subject, for every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), to \[\alpha=A^\top u^t+(D^t)^\top v^t,\qquad \beta\le b^\top u^t+(d^t)^\top v^t,\qquad u^t\ge0,\quad v^t\ge0,\] together with a specified linear normalization that makes the feasible region nonempty and bounded. Every feasible solution represents an inequality \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) valid for each disjunctive term. A negative optimal value identifies a normalized cut violated by \(\bar x\); a nonnegative optimal value means that this normalized CGLP contains no cut violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized CGLP is a linear optimization model whose termwise nonnegative multipliers represent cuts valid for every disjunctive term and whose objective measures violation at the candidate point.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\), and the finite disjunction has terms \(D^t x\ge d^t\) for \(t=1,\ldots,q\).
The point to be separated is \(\bar x\in\mathbb Q^n\).
A specified linear normalization makes the CGLP feasible region nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized linear program represents valid disjunctive cuts and optimizes their normalized violation at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Search Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-dual certificate for optimality of a normalized linear cut-search model with unrestricted primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb Q^{m\times d}\), \(r\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb Q^d\), and consider the cut-search linear program \[p^*=\min\{c^\top z:Mz\ge r,\ z\in\mathbb R^d\}.\] A pair \((z^*,y^*)\in\mathbb Q^d\times\mathbb Q^m\) is a cut-search optimality certificate if \[Mz^*\ge r,\qquad y^*\ge0,\qquad M^\top y^*=c,\qquad c^\top z^*=r^\top y^*.\] These conditions certify that \(z^*\) is globally optimal and that \(p^*=c^\top z^*=r^\top y^*\). All certificate conditions are checkable by exact rational arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a cut-search LP with unrestricted primal variables, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and equality of the two objective values form an exactly checkable certificate of global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The normalized cut-search problem is \(p^*=\min\{c^\top z:Mz\ge r,\ z\in\mathbb R^d\}\), with \(M\in\mathbb Q^{m\times d}\), \(r\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb Q^d\).
The proposed certificate supplies \(z^*\in\mathbb Q^d\) and \(y^*\in\mathbb Q^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasibility conditions and equality \(c^\top z^*=r^\top y^*\) certify \(c^\top z^*=p^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Certificate Verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint verification of cut validity and optimality within a normalized cut-search model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\mathcal F\) be a normalized family of inequalities \(\alpha^Tx\leq\beta\) valid for \(S\). A joint certificate for \((\hat\alpha,\hat\beta)\in\mathcal F\) consists of a validity witness \(w_v\) and a search-optimality witness \(w_o\). A verifier accepts exactly when \(w_v\) establishes \(\hat\alpha^Tx\leq\hat\beta\) for every \(x\in S\), while \(w_o\) establishes \(\alpha^T\bar x-\beta\leq\hat\alpha^T\bar x-\hat\beta\) for every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal F\). Acceptance therefore certifies both validity and maximal violation over the specified family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The verifier accepts a cut only when one witness proves validity and another proves that no normalized candidate cut has greater violation.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\mathcal F\) is a specified normalized family of valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((w_v,w_o)\text{ accepted}\Rightarrow (\hat\alpha,\hat\beta)\in\arg\max_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal F}(\alpha^T\bar x-\beta)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Membership Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear feasibility representation of membership and nonmembership certificates for a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polyhedron \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\), membership of a query point \(\bar x\) is represented by the finite system \(A\bar x\leq b\), equivalently by \(\max_i(a_i^T\bar x-b_i)\leq0\). If the maximum is positive, any maximizing row \(i^*\) supplies the separating inequality \(a_{i^*}^Tx\leq b_{i^*}\), which is valid for every \(x\in P\) and violated by \(\bar x\). Thus the same model returns either a membership certificate consisting of all satisfied row inequalities or an explicit separating row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership is checked by the largest row violation; a positive maximum identifies a valid inequality separating the query point.

\(A\) has finitely many rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier representation of inequalities valid for a polyhedral projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+p}:Ax+By\leq d\}\) and \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). Every multiplier \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying \(\lambda^TB=0\) yields the projected-space inequality \(\lambda^TAx\leq\lambda^Td\). Indeed, the multiplier eliminates the auxiliary variables from the aggregated inequalities defining \(Q\). Consequently, if \(\lambda^TA\bar x>\lambda^Td\), this inequality separates \(\bar x\) from \(P\). Searching over a normalized multiplier set therefore gives a finite-dimensional separation model in the original \(x\)-space without explicitly constructing the full projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers that cancel auxiliary variables produce valid inequalities in the projected space and can separate a query point.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) be a polyhedron of cut parameters \(z\), where \(V\) and \(R\) are finite and \(V\neq\varnothing\), and let \(z\mapsto(\alpha(z),\beta(z))\) be affine, with every generated inequality valid for \(S\). For a query point \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(g(z)=\alpha(z)^T\bar x-\beta(z)\), and let \(g^{\infty}(r)\) denote its recession value in direction \(r\). If \(g^{\infty}(r)\leq0\) for every \(r\in R\), evaluate \(g(v)\) for every \(v\in V\), choose \(v^*\in\arg\max_{v\in V}g(v)\), and output the cut generated by \(v^*\) when \(g(v^*)>0\); otherwise report that this generator model contains no violated cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no recession generator improves the violation objective, evaluating all point generators finds a maximally violated cut in the generator polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of recession-ray generators on an affine cut-violation objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) be a nonempty polyhedron parameterizing valid cuts, and let \(g(z)=\alpha(z)^T\bar x-\beta(z)\) be affine. For each \(r\in R\), let \(g^{\infty}(r)\) be the recession value of \(g\) in direction \(r\). If some \(r^*\in R\) satisfies \(g^{\infty}(r^*)>0\), then for every \(z\in G\), \(z+tr^*\in G\) for all \(t\geq0\) and \(g(z+tr^*)\to+\infty\) as \(t\to+\infty\). Thus the cut-search objective is unbounded along that ray.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Generator Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski–Weyl decomposition of a cut-generator polyhedron into points and rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a nonempty polyhedron of cut parameters. There exist finite sets \(V\) and \(R\) such that \(G=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\). Hence every \(z\in G\) has a representation \(z=\sum_{v\in V}\theta_vv+\sum_{r\in R}\mu_rr\), where \(\theta_v\geq0\), \(\sum_v\theta_v=1\), and \(\mu_r\geq0\). Under an affine cut map, the generated cut combines a convex mixture of point-generated cuts with nonnegative homogeneous ray contributions; both components must therefore be accounted for when optimizing violation or certifying boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every polyhedral cut parameter is a convex combination of point generators plus a nonnegative combination of recession rays.
assumptions_latex: \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite point-and-ray representation is a correct representation-level statement for mixed generator geometry, with consistent notation and explicit assumptions. No Minkowski-Weyl source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Gomory Fractional Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer Gomory cut obtained from one fractional simplex-tableau row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the tableau row \(x_B=\bar b-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_jx_j\), where \(x_B\) and every \(x_j\) are nonnegative integer variables and \(f_0=\bar b-\lfloor\bar b\rfloor\in(0,1)\). For each \(j\), set \(f_j=\bar a_j-\lfloor\bar a_j\rfloor\). Generate the Gomory fractional cut \(\sum_{j\in N}f_jx_j\geq f_0\). The cut is valid for all integer solutions satisfying the tableau row and is violated by the associated basic relaxation solution, at which every nonbasic variable is zero and \(x_B=\bar b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional parts of a pure-integer tableau row define a valid cut excluding its fractional basic solution.
assumptions_latex: \(x_B,x_j\in\mathbb Z_+\) for every \(j\in N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\in N}f_jx_j\geq f_0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gomory fractional cut from a fractional optimal tableau row
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer standard-form maximization at an optimal basic solution of its LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\max\{cx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}\) with an optimal LP tableau row \(x_{B_u}+\sum_{j\in NB}\bar a_{uj}x_j=\bar a_{u0}\), where \(\bar a_{u0}\notin\mathbb Z\). Define \(f_{uj}=\bar a_{uj}-\lfloor\bar a_{uj}\rfloor\) and \(f_{u0}=\bar a_{u0}-\lfloor\bar a_{u0}\rfloor\). The Gomory fractional cut is \(x_{B_u}+\sum_{j\in NB}\lfloor\bar a_{uj}\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor\bar a_{u0}\rfloor\), equivalently \(\sum_{j\in NB}f_{uj}x_j\ge f_{u0}\). It is valid for every integer feasible point and excludes the current basic LP solution. In the equation \(s=-f_{u0}+\sum_{j\in NB}f_{uj}x_j\), the slack is a nonnegative integer at every integer point satisfying the cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an optimal tableau row whose basic value is fractional, round down its coefficients and right-hand side, and add the resulting Gomory fractional cut. The cut is valid for integer feasible solutions, excludes the current basic LP solution, and has integral nonnegative slack at integer points satisfying it.
assumptions_latex: \(\max\{cx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}\) is a pure-integer program whose LP relaxation has an optimal basis.
\(x_{B_u}+\sum_{j\in NB}\bar a_{uj}x_j=\bar a_{u0}\) is a row of the associated optimal tableau, with \(\bar a_{u0}\notin\mathbb Z\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{B_u}+\sum_{j\in NB}\lfloor\bar a_{uj}\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor\bar a_{u0}\rfloor\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \sum_{j\in NB}f_{uj}x_j\ge f_{u0};\quad x^*\text{ violates the cut, and }s\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\text{ at integer points satisfying it}.

knowledge_statements.title: Gomory Mixed-Integer Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-row GMI cut for nonnegative integer and continuous nonbasic variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_B=\bar b-\sum_{j\in I}\bar a_jx_j-\sum_{j\in C}\bar a_jx_j\), with \(x_B\in\mathbb Z\), \(x_j\in\mathbb Z_+\) for \(j\in I\), and \(x_j\in\mathbb R_+\) for \(j\in C\). Put \(f=\bar b-\lfloor\bar b\rfloor\in(0,1)\) and \(f_j=\bar a_j-\lfloor\bar a_j\rfloor\). Generate \[\sum_{\substack{j\in I\\f_j\leq f}}f_jx_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in I\\f_j>f}}\frac{f(1-f_j)}{1-f}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in C\\\bar a_j\geq0}}\bar a_jx_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in C\\\bar a_j<0}}\frac{-f\bar a_j}{1-f}x_j\geq f.\] This inequality is valid for the one-row mixed-integer set and cuts off its fractional basic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional mixed-integer tableau row is rounded piecewise to produce the standard single-row GMI cut.
assumptions_latex: \(x_B\in\mathbb Z\), \(x_I\in\mathbb Z_+^{|I|}\), and \(x_C\in\mathbb R_+^{|C|}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{the displayed GMI inequality is valid and excludes }(x_I,x_C)=(0,0)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the corner relaxation be \(x=f+\sum_{j=1}^m r^js_j\), where \(x\in\mathbb Z^q\), \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \(f\notin\mathbb Z^q\). Generate the intersection cut \(\sum_{j=1}^m\psi_B(r^j)s_j\geq1\). This inequality is valid for the corner relaxation and separates the point \(s=0\), whose associated integer-space point is \(f\).

children.title: Rounding-Aggregation Separator Family

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Rounding Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MIR separation for a nonnegative one-row mixed-integer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an aggregation yields \(\sum_{j=1}^pa_jx_j+\sum_{k=1}^qc_ky_k\geq b\), where \(x\in\mathbb Z_+^p\), \(y\in\mathbb R_+^q\), and all coefficients are nonnegative. Let \(f=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\in(0,1)\) and \(f_j=a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\). Generate \[\sum_{j=1}^p\left(\lfloor a_j\rfloor+\min\left\{\frac{f_j}{f},1\right\}\right)x_j+\sum_{k=1}^q\frac{c_k}{f}y_k\geq\lceil b\rceil.\] Evaluate this inequality at the relaxation point and return it when violated; otherwise this aggregation supplies no separating MIR cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round an aggregated mixed-integer row with the MIR function, then return the resulting valid inequality if it is violated.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb Z_+^p\), \(y\in\mathbb R_+^q\), and \(a,c\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{the displayed MIR inequality is valid for the aggregated one-row set}\).

notation.meaning: fractional part of the aggregated right-hand side
fractional part of integer-variable coefficient j

review_flags: restricted nonnegative-row MIR version requires formula verification against an authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record clearly isolates a nonnegative one-row MIR variant and uses the algorithm kind appropriately. Because the exact scaled coefficient formula is the substantive claim and no source is cited, authoritative formula verification is required.

The target feasible points lie in \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one Chvatal-Gomory cut search by nonnegative aggregation and rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and suppose the target feasible points satisfy \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\). Choose \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \(\lambda^TA\in\mathbb Z^{1\times n}\). The rank-one Chvatal-Gomory inequality is \(\lambda^TAx\leq\lfloor\lambda^Tb\rfloor\). For a query point \(\bar x\in P\), define \(v(\lambda)=\lambda^TA\bar x-\lfloor\lambda^Tb\rfloor\); return the inequality when \(v(\lambda)>0\), and otherwise report that this multiplier supplies no separating cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate rows with a nonnegative multiplier that makes the left-hand side integral, round down the aggregated right-hand side, and return the resulting valid inequality when it cuts off the query point.
knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Separation
Strong Chvátal–Gomory Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation over strengthened divisor-based Chvátal–Gomory inequalities for binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a valid inequality \(a^\top x\le b\) for \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), with \(a\in\mathbb Z^n\), \(b\in\mathbb Z\), choose an integer divisor \(d\ge2\). Write \(b=dq+r\), where \(0\le r<d\), and let \(r_j=a_j-d\lfloor a_j/d\rfloor\). Define \(\phi_{d,r}(a_j)=\lfloor a_j/d\rfloor+\max\{0,(r_j-r)/(d-r)\}\). The strengthened inequality is \[\sum_{j=1}^n\phi_{d,r}(a_j)x_j\le q.\] A strong Chvátal–Gomory separator searches admissible aggregations producing \(a^\top x\le b\) and divisors \(d\), returns an inequality maximizing positive violation at \(\bar x\), and reports none when the maximum is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search valid binary aggregations and divisors, strengthen the rounded coefficients by their remainders, and return a cut with positive violation at the relaxation point.
assumptions_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\) is valid and \(a,b\) are integral.
\(d\ge2\) and \(0\le r=b-d\lfloor b/d\rfloor<d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_j\phi_{d,r}(a_j)x_j\le\lfloor b/d\rfloor\) is valid and separates \(\bar x\) whenever its violation is positive.

notation.meaning: least nonnegative residue of coefficient a_j modulo d

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the separation leaf, and the variables and delimiter usage are consistent. However, the exact strengthened divisor-rounding function and its validity are convention-sensitive and have no cited source with an inspectable locator; source support is required before relying on this formula.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Aggregation Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One aggregation followed by integer rounding for a pure-integer linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax\le b\}\) and suppose feasible integer points satisfy \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\). For a relaxation point \(\bar x\in P\), search for a multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfying \(\lambda^\top A\in\mathbb Z^n\). The single aggregated inequality \((\lambda^\top A)x\le\lambda^\top b\) yields the rank-one cut \[(\lambda^\top A)x\le\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor.\] The separator maximizes \((\lambda^\top A)\bar x-\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor\) over its normalized multiplier domain and returns the cut if this value is positive; otherwise it certifies absence within that domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one nonnegative row aggregation with integral coefficients, round its right-hand side down, and return it exactly when it violates the relaxation point.
assumptions_latex: All variables governed by the cut are integer.
\(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\lambda^\top A\) is integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\lambda^\top A)x\le\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor\) is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-one aggregation and rounding statement is mathematically standard and the algorithm kind fits the leaf. No source is cited, however, and the normalized multiplier domain underlying the claimed maximization and absence certificate is not specified or sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Half Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation over Chvátal–Gomory multipliers restricted to zero and one-half.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax\le b\}\), with \(A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Z^m\), and integer-constrained \(x\), choose \(\lambda\in\{0,\tfrac12\}^m\) such that \(\lambda^\top A\in\mathbb Z^n\). The associated zero-half inequality is \[(\lambda^\top A)x\le\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor.\] At \(\bar x\in P\), the separator searches the admissible multiplier vectors, returns a maximizer of \((\lambda^\top A)\bar x-\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor\) when that value is positive, and otherwise reports that no zero-half cut in the searched family separates \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select half-weighted rows whose aggregated coefficients are integral, round the aggregated right-hand side down, and return a positively violated cut.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are integral.
The variables governed by the aggregation are integer.
\(\lambda\in\{0,\tfrac12\}^m\) and \(\lambda^\top A\in\mathbb Z^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\lambda^\top A)x\le\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor\) is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).

children.title: Parity-Based Separation

knowledge_statements.title: Parity-Based Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parity formulation of zero-half separation for integral inequality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index selected rows of the integral system \(Ax\le b\). Retain only sets satisfying \(\sum_{i\in S}A_{ij}\equiv0\pmod 2\) for every \(j\). Assign multiplier \(1/2\) to rows in \(S\) and zero otherwise, obtaining \[\frac12\sum_{i\in S}A_i x\le\left\lfloor\frac12\sum_{i\in S}b_i\right\rfloor.\] A parity-based separator searches such row sets, evaluates the displayed inequality at \(\bar x\), and returns a positively violated inequality. Sets with an odd selected right-hand-side sum are the nontrivial parity cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find rows whose column sums are all even, halve their aggregation, round the right-hand side, and return a violated parity cut.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb Z^m\).
\(x\) is integer constrained.
Every selected column sum is even.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tfrac12\sum_{i\in S}A_i x\le\lfloor\tfrac12\sum_{i\in S}b_i\rfloor\) is valid for all integer feasible points.

notation.meaning: row i of the constraint matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The even-column parity construction agrees algebraically with zero-half aggregation and the algorithm kind fits the terminal container. The record nevertheless has no citation or inspectable locator supporting the separator formulation and its characterization of nontrivial cases.

children.title: Zero-Half Parity Relationship
children.top_down_role: Containment, overlap, and distinction between the two separator families.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Half Parity Relationship
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between zero-half multipliers and even-column row subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integral \(Ax\le b\), associate with each \(\lambda\in\{0,\tfrac12\}^m\) the row set \(S=\{i:\lambda_i=\tfrac12\}\). Then \(\lambda^\top A\in\mathbb Z^n\) if and only if \(\sum_{i\in S}A_{ij}\equiv0\pmod2\) for every column \(j\). Under this correspondence, the zero-half cut and parity cut coincide: \[(\lambda^\top A)x\le\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac12\sum_{i\in S}A_i x\le\left\lfloor\frac12\sum_{i\in S}b_i\right\rfloor.\] Moreover, the rounding is strict precisely when \(\sum_{i\in S}b_i\) is odd.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-half multipliers correspond exactly to row subsets with even column sums; both constructions produce the same cut, with strict rounding for an odd right-hand-side sum.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are integral.
\(\lambda_i\in\{0,\tfrac12\}\) for every row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible zero-half aggregations and even-column parity row sets define identical rounded inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated correspondence is algebraically plausible, but it is an equivalence or representation rather than a duality in the usual mathematical sense. It also lacks any source locator, so the intended named relationship and the strict-rounding characterization require source confirmation before a content-kind revision can be accepted.

children.title: Disjunctive Separators
children.top_down_role: Separation methods based on split, intersection, lift-and-project, and multi-term disjunctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical intersection cut from a basic cone and a lattice-free convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a relaxation near a basic point \(\bar x\) have cone representation \(x=\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^q r^j s_j\), with \(s\ge0\). Choose a closed convex lattice-free set \(L\) with \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}(L)\). For each ray define \(\alpha_j=\sup\{t\ge0:\bar x+t r^j\in L\}\), using \(1/\alpha_j=0\) when \(\alpha_j=+\infty\). The separator returns \[\sum_{j=1}^q\frac{s_j}{\alpha_j}\ge1\] when it is violated by the target relaxation solution. The inequality is valid for cone points outside \(\operatorname{int}(L)\), hence for the intended integer-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect each basic-cone ray with a lattice-free set boundary and combine the reciprocal ray lengths into a cut excluding the basic point.
assumptions_latex: \(s\ge0\) gives a valid cone representation at \(\bar x\).
\(L\) is closed, convex, lattice-free, and contains \(\bar x\) in its interior.
All intended integer-feasible cone points lie outside \(\operatorname{int}(L)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_j s_j/\alpha_j\ge1\) is valid for the intended integer-feasible cone points and excludes \(s=0\).

notation.meaning: distance parameter to the boundary along ray j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ray-intersection construction is a plausible classical intersection-cut algorithm, and the additional assumption about intended integer-feasible points avoids blending pure- and mixed-integer lattice-free settings. No cited source supports the exact ray-length convention, validity scope, or separation formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation from a two-term integral split disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(I\) index integer variables, and choose \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \(\pi_j=0\) for \(j\notin I\) and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\). Form the split disjunction \[\pi^\top x\le\pi_0\quad\vee\quad\pi^\top x\ge\pi_0+1.\] For \(\bar x\in P\), solve a normalized two-term disjunctive cut-generating program for an inequality \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) valid on both \(P\cap\{\pi^\top x\le\pi_0\}\) and \(P\cap\{\pi^\top x\ge\pi_0+1\}\). Return it when \(\alpha^\top\bar x>\beta\); otherwise report no separating cut for the searched splits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an integral split, derive an inequality valid for both sides, and return it when it cuts off the relaxation point.
assumptions_latex: Variables indexed by \(I\) are integer.
\(\pi\) is integral and supported on \(I\).
The cut-generating program is normalized to exclude scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned inequality is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(P\cap D)\), where \(D\) is the split disjunction, and separates \(\bar x\).

children.title: Lifted-Space Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation carried out in an extended or lifted representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Space Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive separation through a convex-hull extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_k\), where \(P_k=\{x:A^k x\le b^k\}\) are nonempty polyhedra with compatible recession assumptions. Introduce \(y^k\) and \(\lambda_k\ge0\) satisfying \[x=\sum_{k=1}^K y^k,\qquad A^k y^k\le b^k\lambda_k,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k=1.\] This lifted system represents \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\). To separate \(\bar x\), fix \(x=\bar x\) and test lifted feasibility, or solve the dual normalized separation problem. Lifted infeasibility yields a dual inequality in \(x\) that is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\) and violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent a finite polyhedral disjunction in an extended convex-hull space and use infeasibility or its dual to separate the original point.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a finite union of nonempty polyhedra.
The homogenized term formulations correctly include their recession behavior.
\(\bar x\) is the point tested for membership in \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lifted infeasibility at \(x=\bar x\) produces an inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\) and violated by \(\bar x\).

children.title: Projection-Based Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space cuts from lifted-space results.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Cut Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of an original-space cut from a lifted separation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a lifted formulation be \(Q=\{(x,z):Gx+Hz\le h\}\), and suppose \(\bar x\notin\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). A projection certificate consists of \(u\ge0\) satisfying \(u^\top H=0\). Multiplying the lifted inequalities by \(u\) eliminates \(z\) and gives the original-space inequality \[(u^\top G)x\le u^\top h.\] If additionally \((u^\top G)\bar x>u^\top h\), this inequality separates \(\bar x\) from \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). Its validity and violation are directly verifiable from the multiplier sign, the cancellation equation, and the displayed scalar inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use nonnegative multipliers that cancel every lifted variable; the resulting original-space inequality is valid and its violation certifies separation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=\{(x,z):Gx+Hz\le h\}\) is a valid lifted formulation.
\(u\ge0\) and \(u^\top H=0\).
\((u^\top G)\bar x>u^\top h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((u^\top G)x\le u^\top h\) is valid for \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\) and separates \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: projection of Q onto the original variables

children.title: Disjunction Choice Effects
children.top_down_role: Dependence of the resulting cut family on the selected disjunction.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunction Choice Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic effect of disjunction containment on the resulting disjunctive hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(D_1,D_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be valid disjunctive sets containing every intended integer-feasible point of \(P\). If \(D_1\subseteq D_2\), then \[\operatorname{conv}(P\cap D_1)\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(P\cap D_2).\] Consequently, every inequality valid for the larger hull is valid for the smaller hull, while the smaller hull may admit additional separating inequalities. Thus replacing a disjunction by a contained valid disjunction cannot weaken the ideal disjunctive relaxation, although its lifted formulation or separation problem may become more expensive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contained valid disjunction yields a contained disjunctive hull and therefore a relaxation at least as strong, though potentially harder to separate.
assumptions_latex: \(D_1\subseteq D_2\).
Both disjunctions contain all intended integer-feasible points of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(P\cap D_1)\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(P\cap D_2)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Term Disjunctive Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-generating linear program for a finite union of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\bigcup_{t=1}^K P_t\), where \(P_t=\{x:A^t x\le b^t\}\). An inequality \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) is certified valid for every term by multipliers \(u^t\ge0\) satisfying \[(u^t)^\top A^t=\alpha,\qquad (u^t)^\top b^t\le\beta,\qquad t=1,\ldots,K.\] Given \(\bar x\), solve a normalized cut-generating linear program maximizing \(\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\) subject to these constraints. A positive optimum returns a separating inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\); a nonpositive optimum certifies absence of separation within the chosen normalization and inequality template.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use one nonnegative multiplier vector per disjunctive term and optimize a common valid inequality for maximum violation at the target point.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a finite union of polyhedra \(P_t\).
Each multiplier \(u^t\) is nonnegative.
A normalization makes the cut-generating program bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive optimum yields \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\) and violated by \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: validity multiplier for disjunctive term t
common cut coefficients and right-hand side
