knowledge_statements.title: V-Polyhedral Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation from a polyhedron supplied by vertices and extreme rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\), where \(V=\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}\) and \(R=\{r^1,\ldots,r^q\}\). To separate \(\bar x\), solve a normalized optimization problem over \((\alpha,\beta)\) maximizing \(\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\) subject to \[\alpha^\top v^i\le\beta\quad(i=1,\ldots,p),\qquad \alpha^\top r^j\le0\quad(j=1,\ldots,q).\] A positive optimum supplies an inequality \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) valid for all of \(Q\) and violated by \(\bar x\). A nonpositive optimum means that the selected normalized inequality class does not separate \(\bar x\) from the supplied V-polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize a cut against every supplied vertex and ray; positive violation separates the target point from the represented polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) is the intended polyhedron.
The cut coefficients are normalized to prevent arbitrary scaling.
The vertex and ray lists are complete for the claimed representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive optimum yields an inequality valid for \(Q\) and violated by \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: finite set of generating recession rays

children.top_down_role: Named separators exploiting knapsack, binary-matrix, graph, routing, and network structure; the underlying inequality theory remains in the corresponding model chapters.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation of elementary cover inequalities for one binary knapsack row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(a\in\mathbb R_{>0}^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\), solve \[\min\left\{\sum_{i\in C}(1-\bar x_i):C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\ \sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\right\}.\] If no feasible \(C\) exists, stop without a cut. Otherwise, for an optimal \(C^*\), return \(\sum_{i\in C^*}x_i\le |C^*|-1\) exactly when \(\sum_{i\in C^*}(1-\bar x_i)<1\); if this test fails, no elementary cover inequality is violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a minimum-cost knapsack cover under costs one minus the fractional values; its cover cut is violated exactly when that minimum cost is below one.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfies \(a^\top x\le b\).
\(a_i>0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^*\) yields a violated cover inequality exactly when \(\sum_{i\in C^*}(1-\bar x_i)<1\).

notation.meaning: A cover whose total knapsack weight exceeds the capacity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization problem correctly characterizes violation of elementary cover inequalities for a binary knapsack row, and algorithm is the appropriate content kind. However, no citation is supplied for either cover validity or the exact separation characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Cover Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential up-lifting of a fixed cover under a prescribed variable order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a cover and order \(N\setminus C=(j_1,\ldots,j_q)\). Initialize \(L=C\) and \(\alpha_i=1\) for \(i\in C\). For \(k=1,\ldots,q\), compute \[\alpha_{j_k}=|C|-1-\max\left\{\sum_{i\in L}\alpha_i x_i:\sum_{i\in L}a_i x_i\le b-a_{j_k},\ x\in\{0,1\}^{L}\right\},\] then set \(L\leftarrow L\cup\{j_k\}\). Return \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{j\notin C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\) if its left side at \(\bar x\) exceeds \(|C|-1\); otherwise return no cut for this cover and order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequentially lift noncover variables by solving residual knapsack problems, then return the lifted cover inequality if it cuts off the fractional point.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfies \(a^\top x\le b\), with \(a_i>0\).
\(C\subseteq N\) satisfies \(\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\).
The variables outside \(C\) are fixed at zero before sequential up-lifting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed lifted-cover inequality is valid and is returned precisely when violated by \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Sequential lifting coefficient of noncover variable j.
Index set of binary knapsack variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential lifting formula is plausible, but the residual knapsack problem may be infeasible when a lifted variable alone exceeds the capacity, leaving the displayed maximum and coefficient undefined. An authoritative lifting source is needed to determine the intended hypotheses or convention without weakening the result.

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Cover Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Library-relative separation interface for a specified flow-cover formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{(x,y):x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ 0\le y_i\le u_ix_i,\ Dy\le d\}\) and let the input library be \(\mathcal F_{FC}=\{(\alpha^k,\gamma^k,\beta_k):k\in K\}\), where every tagged flow-cover inequality \((\alpha^k)^\top x+(\gamma^k)^\top y\le\beta_k\) is valid for \(X\). At \((\bar x,\bar y)\), compute \(v_k=(\alpha^k)^\top\bar x+(\gamma^k)^\top\bar y-\beta_k\). Return an index maximizing \(v_k\) and its inequality when \(\max_{k\in K}v_k>0\); otherwise certify that no member of the supplied library is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate every certified flow-cover inequality in the selected formulation and return the most violated one, or certify that this supplied library contains none.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite.
Every inequality in \(\mathcal F_{FC}\) has already been certified valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a maximally violated member of \(\mathcal F_{FC}\), or a certificate that all its violations are nonpositive.

notation.meaning: Capacity activated by binary variable i.
Specified finite library of valid flow-cover inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-library scan is correct for any supplied family of certified inequalities, but the generic system Dy<=d does not identify a canonical flow-cover formulation or define the flow-cover inequalities being separated. Source support is needed to fix the mathematical family and its hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Set Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family separation for a declared canonical mixing-set convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(M(b)=\{(s,z)\in\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb Z^n:s+z_i\ge b_i\text{ for all }i\}\). Let \(\mathcal F_M(b)=\{(p^k,q^k,r_k):k\in K\}\) be a finite supplied family of mixing inequalities \(p^ks+(q^k)^\top z\ge r_k\), each valid for \(M(b)\). At \((\bar s,\bar z)\), compute \(v_k=r_k-p^k\bar s-(q^k)^\top\bar z\). Return a maximizer when \(\max_{k\in K}v_k>0\); otherwise certify that no inequality in the supplied mixing family is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the canonical mixing set, evaluate a supplied finite family of valid mixing inequalities and return its most violated member, if any.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite.
Every member of \(\mathcal F_M(b)\) is valid for \(M(b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a maximally violated supplied mixing inequality or certifies nonviolation of the entire supplied family.

notation.meaning: Supplied finite family of valid mixing inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record only scans an externally supplied finite family and does not state the canonical mixing inequalities or a construction of the family. Because the cited section has not been inspected and the candidate itself flags the canonical formula as pending, the substantive separation claim cannot yet be validated.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact clique-cut separation in the conflict graph of binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a conflict graph: every feasible binary vector \(x\) has at most one unit-valued component on each edge. Given \(\bar x\in[0,1]^V\), solve the maximum-weight clique problem \[\omega(\bar x)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in Q}\bar x_i:Q\subseteq V\text{ is a clique of }G\right\}.\] If \(\omega(\bar x)>1\), return an attaining clique \(Q^*\) and the valid inequality \(\sum_{i\in Q^*}x_i\le1\). Otherwise certify that no clique inequality of \(G\) is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a maximum-weight clique problem using fractional variable values; return its clique inequality exactly when the optimum exceeds one.
assumptions_latex: The support of every feasible binary vector is a stable set of \(G\).
\(V\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A clique inequality is violated if and only if \(\omega(\bar x)>1\).

notation.meaning: Maximum fractional weight of a clique.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of odd-cycle inequalities for the stable-set formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite conflict graph and \(\bar x\in[0,1]^V\). For every simple odd cycle \(C\) of length \(|C|=2k+1\), define \(v(C)=\sum_{i\in C}\bar x_i-k\). Compute a cycle \(C^*\) maximizing \(v(C)\). If \(v(C^*)>0\), return the valid odd-cycle inequality \(\sum_{i\in C^*}x_i\le k\). If no odd cycle exists or the maximum violation is nonpositive, certify that no odd-cycle inequality is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find an odd cycle maximizing fractional weight minus its stability bound, and return its inequality if that value is positive.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible binary vector is the incidence vector of a stable set in \(G\).
Only simple odd cycles are considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned inequality is violated exactly when \(\max_C v(C)>0\).

notation.meaning: Simple odd cycle in the conflict graph.
Integer satisfying the odd cycle length equation.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Hole Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation restricted to induced odd cycles of length at least five.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite conflict graph and \(\bar x\in[0,1]^V\). For every induced odd cycle \(H\) with \(|H|=2k+1\ge5\), define \(v(H)=\sum_{i\in H}\bar x_i-k\). Compute an odd hole \(H^*\) maximizing \(v(H)\). If \(v(H^*)>0\), return \(\sum_{i\in H^*}x_i\le k\); if no odd hole exists or the maximum is nonpositive, certify that no odd-hole inequality is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search induced odd cycles of length at least five and return the odd-hole inequality having greatest positive violation.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible binary vector is the incidence vector of a stable set in \(G\).
An odd hole is an induced odd cycle of length at least five.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The odd-hole family cuts off \(\bar x\) exactly when \(\max_H v(H)>0\).

notation.meaning: Odd hole of the conflict graph.
Stability number of the odd cycle.

children.title: Chordality Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions distinguishing general odd cycles from odd holes.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordality Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary at which nontrivial odd-hole separation disappears.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the finite conflict graph \(G\) is chordal, every cycle of length at least four has a chord. Consequently \(G\) contains no odd hole, so the odd-hole separation family \(\{\sum_{i\in H}x_i\le (|H|-1)/2:H\text{ is an odd hole}\}\) is empty. This does not eliminate all odd-cycle cuts: triangles may remain and yield clique inequalities \(\sum_{i\in Q}x_i\le1\). Thus chordality is a boundary for odd-hole generation, not for clique or triangle separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal conflict graphs have no odd holes, so odd-hole separation is vacuous, although triangle and larger clique inequalities may still be relevant.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite chordal graph.
Feasible binary supports are stable sets of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Chordality makes the odd-hole family empty but does not make clique separation empty.

notation.meaning: Induced odd cycle of length at least five.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical boundary is stated correctly and failure_boundary is the appropriate content kind: chordal graphs have no odd holes, while triangles and other cliques may remain. No inspectable citation is supplied, so the record remains source-blocked.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Packing Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct separation of the rows in a binary set-packing formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) and \(P=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\le\mathbf1\}\). Given \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\), compute \(v_r=\sum_{j=1}^n A_{rj}\bar x_j-1\) for every row \(r\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). If \(\max_r v_r>0\), return a maximizing row and its set-packing inequality \(\sum_jA_{rj}x_j\le1\). Otherwise certify that \(\bar x\) satisfies every row of the supplied set-packing system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scan all packing rows and return the row with greatest positive excess above one, or certify that every supplied row is satisfied.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite binary matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A supplied set-packing row is violated if and only if \(\max_r v_r>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Cut Separation of Subtour-Elimination Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded separation procedure for subtour-elimination inequalities at a candidate edge vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a graph \(G\) and a candidate edge vector \(x^*\), form a digraph \(G'\) by orienting each edge \(e\in E(G)\) arbitrarily as an arc \(\bar e\), and set \(c(\bar e)=x_e^*\) and \(l(\bar e)=-x_e^*\). Fix \(v\in V(G)\), compute a minimum-capacity \(v\)-\(w\) cutset \(S_w\) for each \(w\in V(G)\setminus\{v\}\), and choose \(S\) of minimum capacity among them. If \(C(S)\ge 2\), then all subtour-elimination inequalities are satisfied by \(x^*\). If \(C(S)<2\), then either \(W=S\) or \(W=V(G)\setminus S\) describes a subtour-elimination inequality violated by \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orient every graph edge, assign its candidate value and negative candidate value as the stated upper and lower bounds, and find the least-capacity cut from one fixed vertex to every other vertex. Capacity at least two certifies all subtour-elimination inequalities; otherwise the cut or its complement identifies a violated inequality.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a graph}
x^*\text{ is the candidate edge vector}
v\in V(G)
c(\bar e)=x_e^*,\quad l(\bar e)=-x_e^*
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(S)\ge 2\Rightarrow x^*\text{ satisfies all subtour-elimination inequalities};\qquad C(S)<2\Rightarrow \exists W\in\{S,V(G)\setminus S\}\text{ describing a violated inequality}.

knowledge_statements.title: Cutset Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cut separation for uniform undirected connectivity requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), capacities \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_+^E\), and \(\kappa>0\), seek a nonempty proper set \(S\subset V\) minimizing \(\bar x(\delta(S))=\sum_{e\in\delta(S)}\bar x_e\). Compute a global minimum cut, or, for rooted connectivity, compute minimum \(r\)-to-\(v\) cuts for every required vertex \(v\ne r\). If the resulting value is below \(\kappa\), return \(x(\delta(S))\ge\kappa\); otherwise certify that no inequality in the corresponding cutset family is violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-cut computation either finds a cutset inequality violated by the fractional edge vector or certifies that every required cut has sufficient capacity.

children.title: Connectivity-Cutset Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity-Cutset Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support connectivity characterized by positive capacity across every proper cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be undirected and let \(x\in\mathbb R_+^E\). The support graph \(G_x=(V,\{e\in E:x_e>0\})\) is connected if and only if \(x(\delta(S))>0\) for every nonempty proper subset \(S\subset V\). If \(x\in\{0,1\}^E\) additionally satisfies degree equations \(x(\delta(v))=2\) for all \(v\in V\), then every cut has even cardinality; hence support connectivity is equivalent to \(x(\delta(S))\ge2\) for all nonempty proper \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative edge support is connected exactly when every proper cut has positive capacity; for binary degree-two tours, the equivalent threshold is two.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and undirected.
\(x\in\mathbb R_+^E\).

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation problem for rounded capacitated-routing cut inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{0\}\cup C\) be a depot-customer vertex set, with demands \(d_i\ge0\) and vehicle capacity \(Q>0\). For a candidate edge vector \(\bar x\), minimize over nonempty \(S\subseteq C\) the slack \(\bar x(\delta(S))-2\lceil d(S)/Q\rceil\), where \(d(S)=\sum_{i\in S}d_i\). If the minimum is negative, output the rounded capacity inequality \(x(\delta(S))\ge2\lceil d(S)/Q\rceil\) for a minimizing set; if it is nonnegative, certify that this entire inequality family has no violated member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation minimizes rounded-capacity slack over customer subsets and returns the associated cut precisely when that minimum is negative.
assumptions_latex: \(d_i\ge0\) for every customer \(i\in C\).
\(Q>0\) and \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_+^E\).

knowledge_statements.title: Comb-Inequality Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation over the symmetric traveling-salesperson comb family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a complete undirected graph and candidate \(\bar x\), search for a handle \(H\subset V\) and an odd number \(t\ge3\) of pairwise disjoint teeth \(T_1,\ldots,T_t\subset V\) satisfying \(H\cap T_i\ne\varnothing\) and \(T_i\setminus H\ne\varnothing\). Compute \(L=\bar x(\delta(H))+\sum_{i=1}^t\bar x(\delta(T_i))\). If \(L<3t+1\), return the comb inequality \(x(\delta(H))+\sum_{i=1}^t x(\delta(T_i))\ge3t+1\); otherwise report that the searched comb family contains no detected violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A comb separator searches admissible handles and odd tooth systems and returns their comb inequality whenever its cut sum is below the required bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_+^E\) is a candidate symmetric TSP edge vector.
\(t\ge3\) is odd.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected comb is violated exactly when \(L<3t+1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Inequality Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic separation interface; the intended routing path family requires disambiguation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a specified family of valid routing inequalities indexed by admissible paths \(P\), each written \(a(P)^Tx\le b(P)\). Given \(\bar x\), solve \(P^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{P\in\mathcal P}\{a(P)^T\bar x-b(P)\}\). Return \(a(P^*)^Tx\le b(P^*)\) when the maximum is positive, and otherwise certify absence of a violated member of \(\mathcal P\). The admissibility rules and coefficient map must be fixed before this interface defines a concrete separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a precise path-inequality family is supplied, separation maximizes violation over admissible paths and returns a cut exactly when that maximum is positive.

\(a(P)\) and \(b(P)\) are defined for every \(P\in\mathcal P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Routing-Family Overlap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical handling of inequalities generated by multiple routing separators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent every nonzero routing cut as \(a^Tx\le b\) and choose a deterministic positive normalization \(N(a,b)\), including a fixed sign convention. Cuts generated by two families are identical when their normalized pairs coincide, and one dominates another with the same normalized left-hand side when its normalized right-hand side is smaller. A cut manager may retain one canonical copy without changing the relaxation \(\{x:a^Tx\le b\text{ for every retained cut}\}\). Family labels remain metadata and do not alter mathematical validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize generated cuts to detect duplicates and same-left-side dominance; keeping one strongest canonical copy leaves the relaxation unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Every submitted cut is a nonzero linear inequality.
Normalization uses only positive scaling and a fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing normalized duplicates and weaker equal-left-side cuts does not change the represented feasible region.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical-Inference Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of linear cuts induced by valid Boolean implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary variables, let each literal value \(\ell_j(x)\) be either \(x_j\) or \(1-x_j\). A valid implication \(\ell_1=\cdots=\ell_k=1\Rightarrow\ell=1\) yields \(\sum_{i=1}^k\ell_i(x)-\ell(x)\le k-1\). Given \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\), scan the available valid implications and maximize \(v=\sum_{i=1}^k\ell_i(\bar x)-\ell(\bar x)-(k-1)\). Return the corresponding inequality if \(v>0\); otherwise certify that none of the scanned inference cuts is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate each valid Boolean implication into a linear inequality and return the implication having positive maximum violation at the fractional point.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) in the underlying logical model.
Each scanned implication is valid for every integer-feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication cut is violated by \(\bar x\) exactly when \(v>0\).

notation.meaning: Value of a positive or negated binary literal.

knowledge_statements.title: Implied-Bound Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of linear bounds activated by a binary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\{0,1\}\), let \(y\le U_0\) be globally valid, and suppose \(z=1\Rightarrow y\le U_1\), where \(U_1\le U_0\). Then \(y\le U_0-(U_0-U_1)z\) is valid. At a relaxation point \((\bar y,\bar z)\), return this implied-bound cut when \(\bar y>U_0-(U_0-U_1)\bar z\). Analogously, from \(y\ge L_0\) and \(z=1\Rightarrow y\ge L_1\), with \(L_1\ge L_0\), separate \(y\ge L_0+(L_1-L_0)z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary-activated tighter bound interpolates linearly between global and conditional bounds and cuts any relaxation point violating that interpolation.
assumptions_latex: \(z\in\{0,1\}\) in integer-feasible solutions.
The global and conditional bounds are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities are valid and are separated by direct evaluation at \((\bar y,\bar z)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Graph Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-weight-clique separation of pairwise-conflicting binary events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_c=(W,F)\) be a conflict graph whose vertex \(w\) represents a binary event variable \(y_w\), and whose edges join events that cannot occur together. Every clique \(K\subseteq W\) gives the valid inequality \(\sum_{w\in K}y_w\le1\). Given \(\bar y\in[0,1]^W\), compute a maximum-weight clique with weights \(\bar y_w\). If its weight exceeds \(1\), return its clique inequality; otherwise certify that no clique inequality of \(G_c\) is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weight conflict-graph vertices by their fractional event values; a maximum-weight clique exceeding one supplies a violated clique cut.
assumptions_latex: Every edge of \(G_c\) encodes mutual exclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violated conflict-graph clique cut exists iff \(\max_{K\text{ clique}}\sum_{w\in K}\bar y_w>1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Approximation Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order separation of differentiable convex nonlinear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable on a convex domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let feasible points \(x\in D\) satisfy \(g(x)\le0\). Given \(\bar x\in D\) with \(g(\bar x)>0\), output the affine outer-approximation cut \(g(\bar x)+\nabla g(\bar x)^T(x-\bar x)\le0\). This inequality is valid for every feasible point and is violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a violated differentiable convex constraint, linearization at the candidate point produces a valid affine cut that excludes that candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective-Cut Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be closed convex, and consider the on-off epigraph \(z\in\{0,1\}\), \(y=0\) when \(z=0\), and \(t\ge f(y)\) when \(z=1\). For a relaxation point with \(\bar z>0\), set \(u=\bar y/\bar z\) and choose \(s\in\partial f(u)\). The perspective cut is \(t\ge s^Ty+(f(u)-s^Tu)z\). It is valid for the closed perspective epigraph and is violated whenever \(\bar t<\bar z f(\bar y/\bar z)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Disjunctive-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-generating linear program for a finite polyhedral disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the feasible set is contained in \(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\), where \(P_i=\{x:A_ix\ge b_i\}\). A positive optimum returns the valid disjunctive cut \(\alpha^Tx\ge\beta\); a nonpositive optimum certifies no normalized cut represented by this formulation separates \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone certificate for separating a point from a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a nonempty closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, and define \(K^*=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\ge 0\ \text{for every }x\in K\}\). For every \(z\notin K\), there exists \(y\in K^*\) such that \(\langle y,z\rangle<0\). Thus \(\langle y,x\rangle\ge 0\) is valid for every \(x\in K\) and strictly separates \(z\). The pair of checks \(y\in K^*\) and \(\langle y,z\rangle<0\) is a verifiable conic-separation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point outside a closed convex cone is rejected by a dual-cone vector whose inner product is nonnegative on the cone and negative at the point.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The ambient inner-product space is finite-dimensional.
\(z\notin K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvector certificate for separation from the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S^n\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(X)<0\) and \(v\) is a unit eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(X)\), then \(Y=vv^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and \(\langle Y,X\rangle=v^{\mathsf T}Xv=\lambda_{\min}(X)<0\). Since \(\langle Y,Z\rangle\ge0\) for every \(Z\succeq0\), the inequality \(\langle Y,Z\rangle\ge0\) separates \(X\) from \(\mathbb S_+^n\). Conversely, absence of a negative eigenvalue is equivalent to \(X\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-eigenvalue eigenvector produces a rank-one positive-semidefinite matrix defining a valid inequality that rejects the non-PSD matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(v\) is a unit eigenvector for \(\lambda_{\min}(X)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y=vv^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and \(\langle Y,X\rangle<0\), while \(\langle Y,Z\rangle\ge0\) for all \(Z\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Specific Oracle Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness and completeness boundary for a cone-separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex cone \(K\), a cone oracle queried at \(z\) may return \(\mathrm{IN}\), \(\mathrm{SEP}(y)\), or \(\mathrm{UNKNOWN}\). It is sound precisely when \(\mathrm{IN}\) is returned only for \(z\in K\), and every \(\mathrm{SEP}(y)\) satisfies \(y\in K^*\) and \(\langle y,z\rangle<0\). It is complete when every \(z\notin K\) produces \(\mathrm{SEP}(y)\). Therefore a nonseparation response certifies \(z\in K\) only for a complete oracle; \(\mathrm{UNKNOWN}\) carries no feasibility conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-oracle cuts must have a dual-feasible normal and negative violation. Failure to find a cut proves membership only when the oracle is complete.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
Oracle arithmetic and dual-cone membership tests use the declared accuracy convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{SEP}(y)\Rightarrow y\in K^*\land\langle y,z\rangle<0\); no-cut implies \(z\in K\) only under completeness.

knowledge_statements.title: Point-Regime Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving dispatch when the representation of the separated point changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a relaxation point and let \(\mathcal A_B\), \(\mathcal A_P\), and \(\mathcal A_I\) denote sound separators requiring, respectively, a valid basis \(B\), only point coordinates, or interior-domain subgradient data. Dispatch to \(\mathcal A_B\) only while \(B\) represents \(\bar x\); after loss of that basis, use \(\mathcal A_P\), and use \(\mathcal A_I\) only when its domain assumptions hold. Across a transition, retain a generated inequality only after rechecking validity for the unchanged target set and violation at the current point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When point metadata changes, select only a separator whose prerequisites still hold and recheck every retained cut against the current point and target set.
assumptions_latex: Each component separator is sound on its declared domain.
The target feasible set is fixed during the transition.
The current point and available metadata are explicitly identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained cut remains valid for the target set and is returned as separating only if it violates the current \(\bar x\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly formalizes transitions among basis, nonbasic, and interior-point separation regimes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dispatch principle is plausible, but no citation formalizes the proposed transition among basis-dependent, coordinate-only, and interior-domain regimes or the stated cut-retention checks.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Primal-Solution Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-based strong separation of any point outside a closed convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\). Compute the Euclidean projection \(p=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\|x-\bar x\|_2\). If \(p=\bar x\), return membership in \(Q\). Otherwise return \((\bar x-p)^{\mathsf T}(x-p)\le0\). The projection optimality condition makes the inequality valid for every \(x\in Q\), while its left side at \(\bar x\) equals \(\|\bar x-p\|_2^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project an arbitrary point onto a closed convex relaxation; the projection residual defines a valid hyperplane that strictly separates every exterior point.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Euclidean projection onto \(Q\) can be computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(\bar x\in Q\), or \((\bar x-p)^{\mathsf T}(x-p)\le0\) strongly separates \(\bar x\) from \(Q\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection of the queried point onto Q

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Candidate Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-constraint separation after the designated integer coordinates are integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x\in D:g_j(x)\le0\ (j=1,\ldots,m),\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I)\}\), where every \(g_j\) is convex on the open convex set \(D\). Given \(\bar x\in D\) with \(\bar x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for \(i\in I\), select any index \(j\) satisfying \(g_j(\bar x)>0\), choose \(s_j\in\partial g_j(\bar x)\), and return \(g_j(\bar x)+s_j^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\le0\). If no constraint is violated, accept \(\bar x\) relative to this formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an integral candidate, linearize any violated convex constraint to reject it; if none is violated, the candidate satisfies the stated formulation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_j\) is convex on the open convex domain \(D\).
All designated integer coordinates of \(\bar x\) are integral.
A subgradient is available for every selected violated constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violated constraint yields a valid separating cut; otherwise \(\bar x\in S\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separation Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete separation relative to a normalized valid-inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\mathcal F\) be a compact normalized family of pairs \((\alpha,\beta)\) satisfying \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in S\). Compute \(v^*=\max_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal F}(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta)\). If \(v^*>0\), output an attaining inequality; if \(v^*\le0\), output the certificate that no inequality in \(\mathcal F\) separates \(\bar x\). Exactness refers to complete optimization over \(\mathcal F\), not necessarily over all valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact separator globally maximizes normalized violation over its declared cut family and certifies absence of a separating family member when the optimum is nonpositive.
assumptions_latex: Every inequality represented by \(\mathcal F\) is valid for \(S\).
\(\mathcal F\) is compact under the chosen normalization.
The maximization is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^*>0\) yields a valid violated cut, while \(v^*\le0\) proves nonseparability relative to \(\mathcal F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Exact Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimization over a proper, explicitly declared subfamily of cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\) be a compact normalized subfamily represented by pairs \((\alpha,\beta)\) whose inequalities \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) are valid for every \(x\in S\). Given \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), compute \(v'=\max_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal F'}(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta)\) globally. Return an attaining inequality when \(v'>0\); otherwise certify only that no member of \(\mathcal F'\) separates \(\bar x\). Even with exact solution of the restricted problem, \(v'\le0\) does not imply that no inequality in \(\mathcal F\), or no valid inequality for \(S\), separates \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted exact separation is globally complete only within its declared subfamily; failure there gives no completeness claim for a larger cut family.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\) is compact and normalized.
Every member of \(\mathcal F'\) is valid for \(S\).
The restricted maximization is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result is exact for \(\mathcal F'\), but a nonpositive \(v'\) is not a nonseparation certificate for \(\mathcal F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound but incomplete search for a violated valid inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal F\) be a family of pairs \((\alpha,\beta)\) representing inequalities \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) valid for every \(x\in S\), and let \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) be the queried point. A heuristic separator inspects a finite, adaptively chosen subset \(H(\bar x)\subseteq\mathcal F\). It may return \((\alpha,\beta)\in H(\bar x)\) only after confirming its validity for \(S\) and verifying \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta>0\). If no inspected inequality passes both checks, it returns \(\mathrm{NONE}\); this response does not certify that \(\bar x\) is unseparable by \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic separator may incompletely search a cut family, but every returned cut must be valid and violated; failure to find one proves nothing globally.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(H(\bar x)\subseteq\mathcal F\) is finite.
Returned inequalities undergo validity and violation checks.
The heuristic need not inspect all of \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned cut is sound, whereas \(\mathrm{NONE}\) is not a completeness certificate for \(\mathcal F\).

notation.meaning: no cut found by the heuristic

assumptions_latex: The separation domain is a nonempty set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The cut family is \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\), and every \((a,b)\in\mathcal C\) represents an inequality \(a^\top x\le b\) valid for \(X\).
The heuristic and exact routines test violation relative to the same tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and the exact routine terminates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(\bar x)=\varnothing\) does not certify the absence of a violated member of \(\mathcal C\), whereas \(E(\bar x)=\varnothing\) certifies \(a^\top\bar x\le b+\varepsilon\) for every \((a,b)\in\mathcal C\).

notation.meaning: Family of valid inequalities represented by coefficient-right-hand-side pairs
Heuristic routine returning a possibly incomplete set of cuts violated beyond the tolerance
Terminating complete routine returning cuts violated beyond the tolerance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escalation from incomplete heuristic search to a terminating complete separation routine at a fixed candidate point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), first compute \[H(\bar x)\subseteq\{(a,b)\in\mathcal C:a^\top\bar x>b+\varepsilon\}.\] If \(H(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\), return one or more members of \(H(\bar x)\). If \(H(\bar x)=\varnothing\) and separation completeness is required, invoke \(E\), where \[E(\bar x)=\{(a,b)\in\mathcal C:a^\top\bar x>b+\varepsilon\}.\] Return one or more members of \(E(\bar x)\) when this set is nonempty; otherwise return the certificate that no member of \(\mathcal C\) is violated beyond \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a candidate point, run an incomplete heuristic separator first. If it returns no cut and completeness is required, run a terminating exact separator over the same cut family and tolerance. Only an empty exact result certifies that no family member is violated beyond the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic-to-Exact Escalation

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is nonempty.
\(J=\{j_1,\ldots,j_k\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a finite set of distinct indices, listed in the order in which they are lifted.
\(a_j=0\) for every \(j\in J\), and \(a^\top x\le b\) is valid for every \(x\in X\) satisfying \(x_j=0\) for all \(j\in J\).
For every stage \(t\), the lifting subproblem with \(x_{j_t}=1\) and \(x_{j_s}=0\) for all \(s>t\) has a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursively constructed inequality \(a^\top x+\sum_{t=1}^k\lambda_{j_t}x_{j_t}\le b\) is valid for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of indices lifted from zero
Coefficient assigned to the variable lifted at stage t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sequential up-lifting of finitely many binary variables initially fixed at zero, under nonempty stage subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each stage \(t\in\{1,,k\}\), define \[\lambda_{j_t}=b-\max\left\{a^\top x+\sum_{r=1}^{t-1}\lambda_{j_r}x_{j_r}:x\in X,\ x_{j_t}=1,\ x_{j_s}=0\ \text{for every }s>t\right\}.\] After computing \(\lambda_{j_t}\), append the term \(\lambda_{j_t}x_{j_t}\). At every stage \(t\), the inequality \[a^\top x+\sum_{r=1}^{t}\lambda_{j_r}x_{j_r}\le b\] is valid on the face of \(X\) defined by \(x_{j_s}=0\) for every \(s>t\). In particular, after stage \(k\), the fully lifted inequality is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order the binary variables initially fixed at zero. At each stage, assign the next coefficient as the residual slack obtained from an exact optimization over the enlarged face. Assuming every stage subproblem is feasible, the final inequality is valid on the entire binary feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Lifting

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential lifting for full-dimensional binary packing sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-by-variable lifting of a facet from a coordinate face of a downward-closed binary set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\le b\}\) have dimension \(n\), with \(A\ge0\), and let \(\sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j\le\beta\) define a facet of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\cap\{x:x_j=0\text{ for all }j\in N\setminus C\}\). Choose an ordering \(j_1,\ldots,j_\ell\) of \(N\setminus C\), set \(C_0=C\) and \(C_h=C_{h-1}\cup\{j_h\}\), and successively compute \[\alpha_{j_h}:=\beta-\max\left\{\sum_{j\in C_{h-1}}\alpha_jx_j:x\in S,\ x_j=0\ \forall j\in N\setminus C_h,\ x_{j_h}=1\right\}.\] Each subproblem is feasible, and the resulting inequality \(\sum_{j=1}^n\alpha_jx_j\le\beta\) defines a facet of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Different orderings may produce different lifted inequalities, and not every lifting is obtainable by this procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting orders the omitted variables and assigns each its largest valid coefficient given the variables already lifted. For a full-dimensional binary packing set, the subproblems are feasible and the final inequality is facet-defining. The outcome can depend on the order, and sequential lifting does not generate every lifting.
assumptions_latex: A\ge0
\dim(S)=n
\sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j\le\beta\text{ defines a facet on the face }x_j=0\ (j\notin C)
(j_1,\ldots,j_\ell)\text{ is an ordering of }N\setminus C
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j=1}^n\alpha_jx_j\le\beta\text{ is facet-defining for }\operatorname{conv}(S);\text{ the result may depend on the ordering, and not every lifting is sequentially obtainable.}

children.title: Simultaneous Lifting
children.top_down_role: Lifting regimes where multiple coefficients are treated jointly.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is nonempty.
\(a^\top x\le b\) is valid on \(X\cap\{x_J=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\lambda\in L\) yields the valid lifted inequality \(a^\top x+\lambda^\top x_J\le b\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint lifting region for binary variables fixed to zero in the base face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The simultaneous lifting region is \[L=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{J}:\max_{x\in X}\left(a^\top x+\lambda^\top x_J\right)\le b\right\}.\] Thus simultaneous lifting determines all coefficients in one joint validity problem rather than through an ordering. Any \(\lambda\in L\) gives a valid inequality. A componentwise maximal member of \(L\), when it exists, is undominated within this fixed left-hand-side family: no component can be increased while the others remain fixed without violating the inequality at some point of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous lifting chooses all new coefficients from one joint feasibility region. Componentwise maximal feasible vectors give undominated lifted inequalities within the prescribed family.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Lifting

children.title: Sequence-Independent Lifting
children.top_down_role: Lifting regimes whose outcome does not depend on coefficient order.

assumptions_latex: Exact sequential lifting is well-defined for every ordering of a finite index set \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifting is sequence-independent exactly when \(\lambda^\pi=\lambda^\sigma\) for all permutations \(\pi,\sigma\) of \(J\).

notation.meaning: Final coefficient vector produced in order \(\pi\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational order invariance for exact sequential binary lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each permutation \(\pi\) of \(J\), apply the same exact sequential lifting rule and write the resulting coefficient vector as \(\lambda^\pi\in\mathbb{R}^J\). The procedure is sequence-independent on the given instance if and only if \[\lambda^\pi=\lambda^\sigma\qquad\text{for every pair of permutations }\pi,\sigma\text{ of }J.\] Equivalently, every adjacent interchange of two still-unlifted indices leaves their two assigned coefficients, and hence the final vector, unchanged. This property concerns coefficients, not merely equality of the feasible regions cut off by differently scaled inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact sequential lifting is sequence-independent when every ordering produces the same indexed coefficient vector; checking invariance under adjacent order swaps is equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Independent Lifting

children.title: Order-Sensitivity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating order-dependent outcomes from sequence-independent outcomes.

assumptions_latex: Sequential lifting uses exact residual-slack subproblems.
The base inequality is \(x_1\le1\) on the face \(x_2=x_3=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The orders \((2,3)\) and \((3,2)\) produce coefficient pairs \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\), respectively.

notation.meaning: Lifted coefficients of variables two and three

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A three-variable binary instance exhibiting order-dependent exact lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[X=\{(0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1),(0,1,1)\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^3.\] Starting from \(x_1\le1\) on \(x_2=x_3=0\), lifting \(x_2\) first gives \(\lambda_2=1\); the point \((0,1,1)\) then forces \(\lambda_3=0\). Reversing the order gives \(\lambda_3=1\) and then \(\lambda_2=0\). Both inequalities are valid for \(X\), but their indexed coefficient vectors differ. Hence exact sequential lifting need not be order-invariant without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A five-point binary set makes exact lifting order-sensitive: lifting variable two first gives coefficients (1,0), while lifting variable three first gives (0,1).
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Sensitivity Boundary

children.title: Modularization Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Coefficient strengthening through modular structure.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n\) satisfies the integer equality \(q^\top x=r\).
\(a^\top x\le b\) is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(m\in\mathbb{Z}\), \((a+mq)^\top x\le b+mr\) defines the same inequality on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of a valid inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-based modularization before applying a coefficient-sensitive strengthening rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(m\in\mathbb{Z}\), replace \((a,b)\) by \((a+mq,b+mr)\). Since \(q^\top x=r\) for all \(x\in X\), \[(a+mq)^\top x-(b+mr)=a^\top x-b\qquad(x\in X).\] Thus modularization preserves the represented inequality on the integer feasible set. Its strengthening effect arises only after a subsequent coefficient-sensitive operation, such as rounding or disjunctive coefficient selection: one chooses \(m\) so the congruent representative has residues that produce a dominating valid cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an integer multiple of an equality changes coefficient representatives but not the inequality on the feasible set; later rounding or disjunctive processing may then yield a stronger cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Modularization Strengthening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality substitution is mathematically valid, but the record identifies it with modularization strengthening without evidence that the cited section uses that exact equality-based notion. Full-text inspection is required to determine whether the local concept instead concerns modularization of disjunctive-cut coefficients or a different congruence operation.

children.title: Rounding Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Coefficient strengthening through rounding structure.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n\) is nonempty.
\(c\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(c^\top x\le\beta\) is valid for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(c^\top x\le\lfloor\beta\rfloor\) is valid for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-hand-side rounding for an inequality whose left-hand side is integer-valued on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(c^\top x\le\beta\) is valid for every \(x\in X\), with \(X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), then \[c^\top x\le\lfloor\beta\rfloor\] is valid for every \(x\in X\). If \(\beta\in\mathbb{Z}\), the transformation leaves the inequality unchanged. If \(\beta\notin\mathbb{Z}\) and \(c\ne0\), the rounded inequality defines a proper subset of the original halfspace in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality with an integer-valued left side on every feasible point remains valid after its right side is rounded down. The ambient halfspace is strictly reduced when the right side is nonintegral and the coefficient vector is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Strengthening

children.title: Combined Strengthening Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interaction, ordering effects, and overlap between the two transformations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n\) satisfies \(q^\top x=r\) with \((q,r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{Z}\).
\(a^\top x\le b\) is valid for \(X\), and some \(m\in\mathbb{Z}\) makes \(a+mq\) integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((a+mq)^\top x\le\lfloor b+mr\rfloor\) is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A validity-preserving composition of modularization and integer right-hand-side rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First modularize by adding \(m(q^\top x-r)=0\), obtaining the equivalent valid inequality \[(a+mq)^\top x\le b+mr.\] If \(a+mq\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), its left-hand side is integer-valued on \(X\), so right-hand-side rounding gives \[(a+mq)^\top x\le\lfloor b+mr\rfloor.\] The composition is valid because the first transformation is exact on \(X\) and the second exploits integrality. Strengthening is strict for the continuous relaxation whenever \(b+mr\) is nonintegral and the rounded hyperplane removes a relaxation point retained before rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality may first modularize coefficients into an integral vector; the resulting integer-valued inequality can then have its right side rounded down validly.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Strengthening Regimes

assumptions_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\) is valid on a nonempty set \(X\subseteq\{x:l\le x\le u\}\).
All bounds used in the adjustment are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat a^\top x\le b+\sum_j\max\{(\widehat a_j-a_j)l_j,(\widehat a_j-a_j)u_j\}\) is valid on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coefficient replacement using finite variable bounds and an explicit right-hand-side correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed coefficient vector \(\widehat a\), define \[\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^n\max\{(\widehat a_j-a_j)l_j,(\widehat a_j-a_j)u_j\}.\] Every \(x\in X\) satisfies \((\widehat a-a)^\top x\le\Delta\). Hence validity of \(a^\top x\le b\) implies \(\widehat a^\top x\le b+\Delta\). This bound is the smallest correction derivable from the box alone, because each summand maximizes its linear error over \([l_j,u_j]\). A smaller correction requires additional information coupling the variables in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After changing coefficients, finite variable bounds provide an explicit worst-case right-side correction. It is the tightest correction justified solely by the bounding box.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Based Coefficient Tightening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The box-error correction is mathematically valid, but arbitrary coefficient replacement followed by a compensating right-hand-side increase is not necessarily coefficient tightening and may enlarge or incomparablely alter the halfspace. It therefore does not match the exact terminal container, even though it is useful as a validity-preserving perturbation rule.

children.title: Coefficient Scaling
children.top_down_role: Normalization of coefficient magnitude and row representation.

assumptions_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\) is an inequality and \(s>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\) and \((sa)^\top x\le sb\) define the same closed halfspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive rescaling used to canonicalize a linear cut without changing its halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[a^\top x\le b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (sa)^\top x\le sb\] whenever \(s>0\). Thus positive scaling preserves validity, violation signs, and the represented halfspace, while multiplying every slack and violation magnitude by \(s\). Canonical choices such as \(\|sa\|_2=1\) are available when \(a\ne0\). Scaling by \(s<0\) reverses the inequality direction, and scaling by \(s=0\) discards the original constraint, so neither is an equivalent same-orientation normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying every coefficient and the right side by a positive number preserves the cut's halfspace; negative scaling reverses orientation, and zero scaling destroys the constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Scaling

children.title: Coefficient Rounding
children.top_down_role: Controlled coefficient approximation during cut cleanup.

assumptions_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\) is valid on nonempty \(X\subseteq\{x:l\le x\le u\}\) with finite bounds.
\(\widehat a\) is obtained by rounding components of \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrected rounded inequality \(\widehat a^\top x\le b+\Delta\) is valid on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical coefficient rounding with a rigorous box-based validity correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a rounding grid and round \(a\) to \(\widehat a\). Compute \[\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^n\max\{(\widehat a_j-a_j)l_j,(\widehat a_j-a_j)u_j\}.\] Output \(\widehat a^\top x\le b+\Delta\), optionally followed by a positive common scaling. The correction bounds the largest possible increase of the left-hand side caused by rounding over the known box, so the output remains valid for \(X\). Omitting \(\Delta\) is justified only when an independent argument proves \((\widehat a-a)^\top x\le0\) throughout \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round coefficients to the desired grid, compute the maximum possible error from variable bounds, and add that correction to the right side before optional positive rescaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Rounding

children.title: Validity-Preservation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits governing when cleanup transformations preserve cut validity.

assumptions_latex: \(a^\top x\le b\) is valid on a nonempty feasible set \(X\).
A transformed pair \((\widehat a,\widehat b)\) is proposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformation preserves validity exactly when \(\sup_{x\in X}(\widehat a^\top x-\widehat b)\le0\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set on which validity is required

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validity test and perturbation boundary for cut canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The transformed inequality \(\widehat a^\top x\le\widehat b\) is valid for \(X\) if and only if \[\sup_{x\in X}(\widehat a^\top x-\widehat b)\le0.\] In particular, writing \(e=\widehat a-a\), validity follows from \(\widehat b-b\ge\sup_{x\in X}e^\top x\). If instead \(\widehat b-b<e^\top x^*\) for some \(x^*\in X\) with \(a^\top x^*=b\), then the transformed cut excludes \(x^*\) and is invalid. Consequently arbitrary independent coefficient rounding has no general validity guarantee; positive common scaling is the unconditional equivalence operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized cut remains valid exactly when its maximum transformed violation over the feasible set is nonpositive. Uncompensated rounding can exclude a feasible boundary point.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Preservation Boundaries
Support Sparsification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving removal of selected cut coefficients using a certified bound over the relaxation domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a valid cut \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), select indices \(D\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) to remove and compute a certified lower bound \(L_D\leq\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{j\in D}a_jx_j\). Define \(a'_j=0\) for \(j\in D\), \(a'_j=a_j\) otherwise, and \(\beta'=\beta-L_D\). Admit the sparsified row only when \(L_D\) is finite and certified; output \(a'^\top x\leq\beta'\). Then every \(x\in X\) satisfying the original cut satisfies the sparsified cut, although the latter may be weaker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove chosen coefficients and compensate the right-hand side with a certified lower bound on their discarded contribution, thereby preserving validity over the relaxation domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(X\).
\(L_D\) is a finite certified lower bound on the discarded contribution over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\cap\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\subseteq\{x:a'^\top x\leq\beta'\}\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on the discarded contribution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity-preserving compensation formula is mathematically plausible, but the cited general branch-and-cut section does not specifically support coefficient removal by a certified lower bound. A dedicated sparsification or cut-strengthening source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplicate detection after orienting all inequalities consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero rows \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) and \(d^\top x\leq\delta\), define them to be exact duplicates precisely when there exists \(\lambda>0\) such that \((d,\delta)=\lambda(a,\beta)\). If a canonicalization map \(N\) is invariant under positive row scaling and injective on positive scaling classes, then this condition is equivalent to \(N(a,\beta)=N(d,\delta)\). Duplicate detection may therefore compare or hash such canonical pairs. Numerical implementations must specify coefficient and right-hand-side tolerances separately and classify tolerance matches as approximate rather than exact duplicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two consistently oriented cuts are exact duplicates when their coefficient and right-hand-side vectors differ only by a positive scalar; a scale-invariant canonicalization that distinguishes positive scaling classes gives equal canonical pairs exactly in this case.
assumptions_latex: \(a,d\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\beta,\delta\in\mathbb{R}\).
Both inequalities use the same orientation convention.
\(N\) is invariant under positive scaling and injective on positive scaling classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) and \(d^\top x\leq\delta\) are exact duplicates if and only if \(\exists\lambda>0:(d,\delta)=\lambda(a,\beta)\), equivalently \(N(a,\beta)=N(d,\delta)\) under the stated properties of \(N\).

notation.meaning: canonicalization map invariant under positive scaling and injective on positive scaling classes

children.title: Dominance Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering based on comparative cut strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion dominance between two cuts relative to a fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the current relaxation and let \(H_i=\{x:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\}\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\). Cut \(H_1\) dominates cut \(H_2\) relative to \(P\) when \(P\cap H_1\subseteq P\cap H_2\). If the inclusion is strict, dominance is strict. A dominance filter may discard \(H_2\) whenever the inclusion is certified, because adding \(H_2\) after \(H_1\) cannot further reduce the relaxation. Dominance is domain-dependent and need not persist after changing \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One cut dominates another on a relaxation when every relaxation point satisfying the first also satisfies the second; the dominated cut can then be discarded.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the comparison relaxation.
\(H_1\) and \(H_2\) are valid halfspaces for the intended feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap H_1\subseteq P\cap H_2\Longrightarrow P\cap H_1\cap H_2=P\cap H_1\).

notation.meaning: relaxation relative to which dominance is tested

children.title: Redundancy Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering based on dispensability relative to retained constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical redundancy of one cut relative to a relaxation and the remaining cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(H_i\) be a candidate cut, and let \(Q=P\cap\bigcap_{j\neq i}H_j\) be the relaxation retained without it. The cut \(H_i\) is redundant relative to this pool exactly when \(Q\subseteq H_i\), equivalently when \(Q\cap H_i=Q\). For \(H_i=\{x:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\}\), redundancy is certified if \(\sup_{x\in Q}a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\); an unbounded or excessive supremum does not certify redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is pool-redundant when the relaxation and all other retained cuts already imply it; maximizing its left side supplies a certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and the retained halfspaces \(H_j\) define \(Q\).
\(H_i=\{x:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_i\text{ is redundant relative to }Q\iff Q\subseteq H_i\iff\sup_{x\in Q}a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\).

notation.meaning: relaxation formed without the tested cut

children.title: Local Versus Poolwise Filtering
children.top_down_role: Scope differences between pairwise checks and pool-level assessments.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Versus Poolwise Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of filters using one incumbent cut versus the entire retained pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(H\) be a candidate halfspace, and let \(H_1,\ldots,H_m\) be retained cuts. Local filtering rejects \(H\) only if some single \(H_k\) satisfies \(P\cap H_k\subseteq H\). Poolwise filtering rejects \(H\) when \(P\cap\bigcap_{k=1}^mH_k\subseteq H\). Every locally rejected cut is poolwise redundant, but the converse can fail because several cuts may jointly imply \(H\) although none implies it alone. Both predicates must be recomputed when the comparison domain or retained pool changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-cut dominance implies poolwise redundancy, but several retained cuts can jointly imply a candidate even when no individual cut does.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is fixed during the comparison.
\(H,H_1,\ldots,H_m\) are halfspaces valid for the intended feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\exists k:P\cap H_k\subseteq H\bigr)\Longrightarrow P\cap\bigcap_{k=1}^mH_k\subseteq H\), and the reverse implication need not hold.

children.title: Violation Geometry Calculus
children.top_down_role: Geometric conventions used to compare violations and candidate cut depth.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Norm Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical positive rescaling of a nonzero inequality row by a chosen norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) and a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), its row-norm-normalized representation is \(\widehat a^\top x\leq\widehat\beta\), where \(\widehat a=a/\|a\|\) and \(\widehat\beta=\beta/\|a\|\). Because \(\|a\|>0\), the normalized and original inequalities define the same halfspace, and \(\|\widehat a\|=1\). The selected norm is part of the representation: different norms generally yield different normalized coefficients and normalized violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide a nonzero cut row and its right-hand side by the row norm; the halfspace is unchanged and the normalized row has unit norm.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\).
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}=\{x:\widehat a^\top x\leq\widehat\beta\}\) and \(\|\widehat a\|=1\).

children.title: Cut Depth
children.top_down_role: Depth-based assessment of a candidate cut relative to a reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Depth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unnormalized signed violation of a cut at a reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an oriented cut \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) and a reference point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define its signed cut depth by \(d_{\mathrm{raw}}(\bar x;a,\beta)=a^\top\bar x-\beta\), and its positive cut depth by \(d_+(\bar x;a,\beta)=\max\{0,d_{\mathrm{raw}}(\bar x;a,\beta)\}\). The point violates the cut exactly when the signed depth is positive. Under positive row scaling by \(\lambda\), raw and positive depths are multiplied by \(\lambda\), so depth is not scale-invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut depth is the signed, unnormalized violation at a reference point; positive depth means violation and scales with the cut row.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
The cut is oriented as \(a^\top x\leq\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\notin\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\iff d_{\mathrm{raw}}(\bar x;a,\beta)>0\).

children.title: Cut Distance
children.top_down_role: Distance-based assessment under a selected geometric convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean distance from a violating reference point to the cut hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), let \(H=\{x:a^\top x=\beta\}\), and let \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The Euclidean distance from \(\bar x\) to the cut hyperplane is \(\operatorname{dist}_2(\bar x,H)=|a^\top\bar x-\beta|/\|a\|_2\). For cut admission at a violating point, the directed distance removed by the cut is \((a^\top\bar x-\beta)/\|a\|_2>0\). Both quantities are invariant under multiplying \((a,\beta)\) by any positive scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut distance divides violation by the Euclidean row norm, giving the geometric distance to the boundary and eliminating positive row-scaling effects.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
Directed distance is used only when \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_2(\bar x,H)=\frac{|a^\top\bar x-\beta|}{\|a\|_2}\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean norm of the cut row

children.title: Depth-Distance Normalization
children.top_down_role: Comparability and convention dependence across the two measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-Distance Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of raw cut depth into norm-relative geometric distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a violated cut \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) at \(\bar x\), with \(a\neq0\), the positive raw depth is \(d_+=a^\top\bar x-\beta\). Normalizing the entire row by a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) gives normalized depth \(d_{\|\cdot\|}=d_+/\|a\|\). Under the Euclidean norm, this equals the directed Euclidean distance from \(\bar x\) to \(\{x:a^\top x=\beta\}\). If the norm is positively homogeneous, \(d_{\|\cdot\|}\) is invariant under every positive rescaling of the inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing positive raw depth by the row norm produces a scale-invariant score; with the Euclidean norm it is directed distance to the cut boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) and \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\).
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a positively homogeneous norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\|\cdot\|}=\frac{a^\top\bar x-\beta}{\|a\|}\), and \(d_{\|\cdot\|}\) is invariant under \((a,\beta)\mapsto(\lambda a,\lambda\beta)\) for \(\lambda>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Relative Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Angular comparison of a cut normal with the objective direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero cut normal \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and nonzero objective vector \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define signed objective alignment by \(\rho(a,c)=a^\top c/(\|a\|_2\|c\|_2)\in[-1,1]\), and unoriented parallelism by \(|\rho(a,c)|\). Equivalently, the angle \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\) satisfies \(\cos\theta=\rho(a,c)\). The signed score depends on the inequality orientation, whereas absolute parallelism does not. Both are invariant under positive rescaling of either vector and compare direction rather than violation magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-relative geometry measures the angle or cosine alignment between the cut normal and objective vector, independently of their positive scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(a,c\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\).
The Euclidean inner product and norm are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(a,c)=\frac{a^\top c}{\|a\|_2\|c\|_2}=\cos\theta\in[-1,1]\).

notation.meaning: angle between the cut normal and objective vector

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of cut-quality scores on row scaling and the selected normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(a,\beta;\bar x)=a^\top\bar x-\beta\). Under positive scaling \((a,\beta)\mapsto(\lambda a,\lambda\beta)\), raw violation becomes \(\lambda v(a,\beta;\bar x)\). For any positively homogeneous normalizer \(g\), the normalized score \(s_g(a,\beta;\bar x)=v(a,\beta;\bar x)/g(a)\) is scaling-invariant because \(g(\lambda a)=\lambda g(a)\). Nevertheless, two normalizers \(g_1\) and \(g_2\) can rank cuts differently unless their ratio is constant on all compared row directions. Thus an admission threshold is meaningful only together with its normalization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raw violation changes under row scaling; homogeneous normalization removes that scaling dependence, but different normalizers can still produce different cut rankings.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\lambda>0\).
\(g(a)>0\) and \(g(\lambda a)=\lambda g(a)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_g(\lambda a,\lambda\beta;\bar x)=s_g(a,\beta;\bar x)\), while rankings induced by distinct normalizers need not coincide.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Efficacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-normalized violation of an individual cut at the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cut \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) with \(a\neq0\), a reference point \(\bar x\), and a selected norm \(\|\cdot\|\), define cut efficacy by \(\operatorname{eff}(a,\beta;\bar x)=\max\{0,a^\top\bar x-\beta\}/\|a\|\). Efficacy is zero for a satisfied cut and positive for a violated cut. It is invariant under positive rescaling of the entire row. With the Euclidean norm, efficacy equals the directed Euclidean distance from a violating point to the cut hyperplane; changing the norm changes the score and may change cut rankings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut efficacy is positive violation divided by a chosen row norm; it is scale-invariant and, under the Euclidean norm, equals directed boundary distance.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\|\cdot\|\) is the declared row norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{eff}(a,\beta;\bar x)=\frac{\max\{0,a^\top\bar x-\beta\}}{\|a\|}\geq0\).

notation.meaning: cut efficacy at the reference point

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Cutoff Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-directed distance from a relaxation point to a separating cut hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^\top x\le \beta\) be valid for the integer-feasible set, violated by the relaxation solution \(\bar x\), and satisfied by an incumbent \(x^I\). Put \(v=a^\top\bar x-\beta>0\) and assume \(a^\top(\bar x-x^I)>0\). The segment from \(\bar x\) toward \(x^I\) meets the cut hyperplane at \(x(t)=\bar x+t(x^I-\bar x)\), where \(t_*=v/[a^\top(\bar x-x^I)]\). The directed cutoff distance is \(d_{\mathrm{dir}}=t_*\lVert x^I-\bar x\rVert_2\). A larger value means that the cut removes a longer initial portion of this incumbent-directed segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metric is the Euclidean distance traveled from the relaxation solution toward an incumbent before reaching the cut boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\)
\(a^\top x^I\le\beta\)
\(x^I\ne\bar x\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{dir}}=\dfrac{a^\top\bar x-\beta}{a^\top(\bar x-x^I)}\lVert x^I-\bar x\rVert_2\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: segment-intersection formula is elementary, but the normalization convention for directed cutoff distance is solver-dependent

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Parallelism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant alignment of a cut normal with the linear objective vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero cut normal \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and nonzero objective vector \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), define objective parallelism by \(p_{\mathrm{obj}}(a,c)=|a^\top c|/(\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert c\rVert_2)\). Then \(0\le p_{\mathrm{obj}}\le1\); it equals \(1\) precisely when the two vectors are linearly dependent and equals \(0\) precisely when they are orthogonal. If orientation matters, the signed variant is \(p_{\mathrm{obj}}^{\pm}(a,c)=a^\top c/(\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert c\rVert_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective parallelism is the absolute cosine between the cut normal and objective vector; values near one indicate strong alignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{obj}}(a,c)=\dfrac{|a^\top c|}{\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert c\rVert_2}\in[0,1]\)

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fraction of a cut’s active variables that are integer-constrained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index variables required to be integral, and let \(S(a)=\{j:a_j\ne0\}\) be the support of a nonzero cut normal \(a\). The integer-support ratio of the cut is \(s_I(a)=|S(a)\cap I|/|S(a)|\). Thus \(s_I(a)\in[0,1]\); the value is \(1\) exactly when every variable appearing in the cut is integer-constrained, and it is \(0\) exactly when no integer-constrained variable appears.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer support is the proportion of nonzero cut coefficients attached to integer-constrained variables.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
\(a\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\)
