children.title: Cut Density
children.top_down_role: Support-size characteristics used in candidate assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Density
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized number of nonzero coefficients in a cut row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cut normal \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), define its support by \(S(a)=\{j\in\{1,ldots,n\}:a_j\ne0\}\). Its cut density is \(\delta(a)=|S(a)|/n\). Hence \(0\le\delta(a)\le1\), with \(\delta(a)=1\) for a fully dense cut and \(\delta(a)=k/n\) when exactly \(k\) coefficients are nonzero. In floating-point implementations, the predicate \(a_j\ne0\) may be replaced by the declared scale-aware test \(|a_j|>\varepsilon_a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut density is the fraction of model variables having nonzero, or numerically significant, coefficients in the cut.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R^n\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized row support is the usual density measure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized support-cardinality definition is plausible, but it has no cited support and the support set contains the malformed token `1,ldots,n` instead of `1,\ldots,n`. A source is needed to confirm whether density is normalized over all model variables or another eligible-variable set.

children.title: Coefficient Dynamism
children.top_down_role: Coefficient-range characteristics relevant to cut assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Dynamism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant spread between the largest and smallest significant cut coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero cut normal \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and a declared significance tolerance \(\varepsilon_a\ge0\), let \(S_\varepsilon(a)=\{j:|a_j|>\varepsilon_a\}\). Provided \(S_\varepsilon(a)\ne\varnothing\), the coefficient dynamism is \(D(a)=\max_{j\in S_\varepsilon(a)}|a_j|/\min_{j\in S_\varepsilon(a)}|a_j|\). It satisfies \(D(a)\ge1\) and is invariant under multiplication of the entire cut by any nonzero scalar. Large \(D(a)\) signals coefficients occurring on widely separated numerical scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient dynamism is the ratio of the largest to smallest significant absolute coefficient in a cut.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\)
\(\varepsilon_a\ge0\)
\(S_\varepsilon(a)\ne\varnothing\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(a)=\dfrac{\max_{j\in S_\varepsilon(a)}|a_j|}{\min_{j\in S_\varepsilon(a)}|a_j|}\ge1\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: max-to-min magnitude ratio is the standard coefficient-range statistic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: With a fixed absolute significance tolerance, scaling the cut can change the significant support and therefore the reported ratio, so the claimed invariance under every nonzero scalar is false as written. A source is needed to determine the intended zero-tolerance or scale-aware convention before the statement can be corrected reliably.

children.title: Numerical Cut Quality
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision robustness and numerical reliability of candidate cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Cut Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility predicate combining density, coefficient range, and scale-normalized violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^\top x\le\beta\) be violated by \(\bar x\), and fix thresholds \(\bar\delta\in(0,1]\), \(\bar D\ge1\), and \(\underline e>0\). Define \(e(a,\beta;\bar x)=(a^\top\bar x-\beta)/\lVert a\rVert_2\). The cut has acceptable numerical quality when \(\delta(a)\le\bar\delta\), \(D(a)\le\bar D\), and \(e(a,\beta;\bar x)\ge\underline e\). Each comparison is invariant under positive rescaling of the cut, provided the significance tolerance used in \(D(a)\) is scaled with \(a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is numerically admissible when it is sufficiently sparse, has bounded coefficient range, and separates the current point by a normalized margin.
assumptions_latex: \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\)
\(\bar\delta\in(0,1],\ \bar D\ge1,\ \underline e>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\mathrm{num}}=1\iff \delta(a)\le\bar\delta,\ D(a)\le\bar D,\ e(a,\beta;\bar x)\ge\underline e\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scale-invariant threshold conjunction formalizes a common numerical screening policy
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is a suitable role for an admission predicate, but the three-way conjunction is a proposed solver policy rather than a generally canonical definition of numerical cut quality. Its coefficient-dynamism component also inherits the unresolved tolerance and scaling convention. An inspectable algorithm or solver reference is required.

children.title: Quality Tradeoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among sparsity, coefficient range, and numerical robustness.

knowledge_statements.title: Quality Tradeoff Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto regimes for balancing separation strength against numerical burden.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each candidate cut \(r\) the quality vector \(q(r)=(e_r,-\delta_r,-\log D_r)\), where larger coordinates are preferred. A cut \(r\) dominates \(s\) when \(q_i(r)\ge q_i(s)\) for every coordinate and at least one inequality is strict. A threshold regime admits cuts satisfying \(e_r\ge\underline e\), \(\delta_r\le\bar\delta\), and \(D_r\le\bar D\); a weighted regime ranks them by \(w_1e_r-w_2\delta_r-w_3\log D_r\), with \(w_i\ge0\). Any maximizer under strictly positive weights is nondominated within the compared finite pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quality regimes either impose minimum numerical standards or rank nondominated cuts by weighted separation, sparsity, and coefficient-range preferences.
assumptions_latex: the candidate pool is finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\succ s\iff q(r)\ge q(s)\text{ componentwise and }q(r)\ne q(s)\)

notation.meaning: multi-criterion quality vector of cut r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pareto dominance and weighted scalarization are standard multicriteria constructions

The selected condition kind is plausible but remains policy-dependent.

children.title: Cut-Set Quality
children.top_down_role: Properties of a selected batch that are not reducible to independent candidate scores.

children.title: Parallelism Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering candidates that align too closely with retained cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallelism Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy rejection of candidate cuts nearly parallel to already retained cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input nonzero candidate normals \(a^1,ldots,a^m\), scores \(s_1,ldots,s_m\), and threshold \(\rho\in[0,1]\). Process candidates in nonincreasing score order, starting with \(K=\varnothing\). For candidate \(i\), compute \(p_{ij}=|(a^i)^\top a^j|/(\lVert a^i\rVert_2\lVert a^j\rVert_2)\) for every \(j\in K\). Add \(i\) to \(K\) exactly when \(K=\varnothing\) or \(\max_{j\in K}p_{ij}<\rho\). Output \(K\). Consequently, every distinct retained pair satisfies \(p_{ij}<\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process cuts by score and retain a cut only when its absolute cosine with every retained cut is below the parallelism threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(a^i\ne0\) for every candidate \(i\)
scores induce a fixed tie-broken order
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i,j\in K,\ i\ne j\implies \dfrac{|(a^i)^\top a^j|}{\lVert a^i\rVert_2\lVert a^j\rVert_2}<\rho\)

notation.meaning: absolute cosine similarity of two cut normals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: greedy cosine-threshold filtering is a direct angular-diversity construction

However, the input list contains the malformed token `a^1,ldots,a^m`, and no source supports the strict threshold, score ordering, or absolute-cosine convention as the intended filtering algorithm.

children.title: Orthogonality Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering or prioritization based on angular diversity.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonality Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy selection using minimum orthogonality between retained cut normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input nonzero candidate normals \(a^1,ldots,a^m\), an ordered priority list, and \(\eta\in[0,1]\). Define pairwise orthogonality by \(o_{ij}=1-|(a^i)^\top a^j|/(\lVert a^i\rVert_2\lVert a^j\rVert_2)\). Initialize \(K=\varnothing\), scan the priority list, and append candidate \(i\) precisely when \(K=\varnothing\) or \(\min_{j\in K}o_{ij}\ge\eta\). Return \(K\). The output has pairwise orthogonality at least \(\eta\); sign reversal or positive rescaling of any cut does not change the decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain each candidate only when its orthogonality score against every previously retained cut reaches the required minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(a^i\ne0\) for every candidate \(i\)
the scan order is fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i,j\in K,\ i\ne j\implies o_{ij}\ge\eta\)

notation.meaning: orthogonality score of two cut normals

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: one minus absolute cosine is a conventional orthogonality score
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, and the pairwise guarantee is consistent with the acceptance test. The input list contains the malformed token `a^1,ldots,a^m`, while the orthogonality transformation, non-strict threshold, and priority policy lack source support.

children.title: Angular Threshold Regimes
children.top_down_role: Threshold conventions and degeneracy boundaries for angular comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Angular Threshold Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent cosine, orthogonality, and acute-angle acceptance thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero cut normals \(a^i,a^j\), let \(p_{ij}=|(a^i)^\top a^j|/(\lVert a^i\rVert_2\lVert a^j\rVert_2)\), \(o_{ij}=1-p_{ij}\), and \(\theta_{ij}=\arccos(p_{ij})\in[0,\pi/2]\). Given \(\rho\in[0,1]\), the three pairwise diversity tests \(p_{ij}\le\rho\), \(o_{ij}\ge1-\rho\), and \(\theta_{ij}\ge\arccos(\rho)\) are equivalent. Thus strict, moderate, and permissive angular regimes correspond respectively to smaller, intermediate, and larger values of \(\rho\), with exact numerical bands declared by the cut-management policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cosine, orthogonality, and acute-angle thresholds are equivalent parameterizations; smaller allowed cosine enforces stronger directional diversity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{ij}\le\rho\iff o_{ij}\ge1-\rho\iff\theta_{ij}\ge\arccos(\rho)\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equivalence follows directly from cosine and orthogonality definitions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence of cosine, complementary orthogonality, and acute-angle thresholds is correct for nonzero normals. Nevertheless, the named strict, moderate, and permissive regimes have no defined bands or cited cut-management source, so the container-specific regime statement remains unsupported.

children.title: Separator-Family Diversity
children.top_down_role: Diversity across cut-generating families within an admitted batch.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator-Family Diversity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized entropy of separator-family representation in a retained cut set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a nonempty retained set \(K\) contain cuts labeled by separator families in a finite set \(F\). For each \(f\in F\), put \(p_f=|\{i\in K:\phi(i)=f\}|/|K|\), and let \(F_K=\{f:p_f>0\}\). When \(|F|\ge2\), define separator-family diversity by \(H_F(K)=-\sum_{f\in F_K}p_f\log p_f/\log|F|\). Then \(0\le H_F(K)\le1\); concentration in one family gives \(0\), while equal representation of all available families gives \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separator-family diversity is normalized entropy of family labels among retained cuts, increasing as representation becomes more balanced.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ne\varnothing\)
\(2\le|F|<\infty\)
\(\phi:K\to F\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_F(K)=-\dfrac{\sum_{f:p_f>0}p_f\log p_f}{\log|F|}\in[0,1]\)

notation.meaning: proportion of retained cuts from family f

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized Shannon entropy is a standard categorical-diversity measure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized entropy formula is mathematically valid when the denominator uses the full finite family set, and definition is an appropriate content kind. No source establishes normalized Shannon entropy, rather than another categorical-diversity index or normalization over represented families, as the intended separator-family diversity measure.

children.title: Support Diversity
children.top_down_role: Diversity across variable supports within an admitted batch.

knowledge_statements.title: Support Diversity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Average pairwise dissimilarity of variable supports among retained cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each retained cut \(i\in K\), let \(S_i=\{j:a^i_j\ne0\}\), and assume \(|K|\ge2\) and every \(S_i\ne\varnothing\). Define pairwise support dissimilarity by \(d_J(i,j)=1-|S_i\cap S_j|/|S_i\cup S_j|\). The support-diversity score is the mean \(D_S(K)=2[|K|(|K|-1)]^{-1}\sum_{i<j}d_J(i,j)\). It lies in \([0,1]\), equals \(0\) when all supports coincide, and equals \(1\) when every pair of supports is disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support diversity is the average Jaccard dissimilarity between the variable supports of all retained cut pairs.
assumptions_latex: \(S_i\ne\varnothing\) for every \(i\in K\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_S(K)=\dfrac{2}{|K|(|K|-1)}\sum_{i<j}\left(1-\dfrac{|S_i\cap S_j|}{|S_i\cup S_j|}\right)\in[0,1]\)

notation.meaning: variable support of retained cut i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: mean Jaccard dissimilarity is a standard set-diversity statistic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The average pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity is well-defined under the stated nonempty-support assumptions and has the claimed range. No source establishes this particular index as the intended support-diversity measure in cut-set management, so the convention requires citation.

children.title: Cross-Diversity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Conflicts and complementarities between family-level and support-level diversity.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Diversity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarized tradeoff between separator-family coverage and support-pattern diversity in an admitted cut batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a finite candidate-cut set, let \(f:C\to\mathcal F\) assign separator families, let \(S(c)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the support of cut \(c\), and let \(Q:2^C\to\mathbb R\) be a batch-quality function. For \(B\subseteq C\), define \(D_F(B)=|\{f(c):c\in B\}|\) and \(D_S(B)=\sum_{\{c,d\}\subseteq B}(1-|S(c)\cap S(d)|/|S(c)\cup S(d)|)\), with a summand of zero when both supports are empty. Given \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) and \(\lambda_F,\lambda_S\ge0\), select \[B^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\subseteq C,\ |B|\le k}\{Q(B)+\lambda_FD_F(B)+\lambda_SD_S(B)\}.\] Varying \((\lambda_F,\lambda_S)\) explores the tradeoffs supported by this scalarization with unit weight on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a bounded cut batch by scalarizing intrinsic quality, separator-family coverage, and support dissimilarity; changing the diversity weights explores the tradeoffs represented with quality weight fixed at one.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite, \(Q:2^C\to\mathbb R\), and \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\).
\(\lambda_F,\lambda_S\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\subseteq C,\ |B|\le k}\{Q(B)+\lambda_FD_F(B)+\lambda_SD_S(B)\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-set scalarization is a standard formulation of competing batch-quality criteria

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy-Aware Batch Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch admission penalizing pairwise similarity among otherwise valuable cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite candidate set \(C\), relevance scores \(r_c\in\mathbb R\), symmetric similarities \(s_{cd}\in[0,1]\), penalty \(\lambda\ge0\), and batch limit \(k\), introduce \(z_c\in\{0,1\}\). Select \[z^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}\left\{\sum_{c\in C}r_cz_c-\lambda\sum_{\{c,d\}\subseteq C}s_{cd}z_cz_d:\sum_{c\in C}z_c\le k\right\}.\] Return \(B^*=\{c:z_c^*=1\}\). Similarity may be computed from normalized cut normals, supports, or another fixed representation, but it must be specified before optimization. If several maximizers exist, apply a deterministic tie-breaking order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose at most k cuts by maximizing individual relevance minus a penalty for admitting similar pairs.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\).
\(s_{cd}=s_{dc}\in[0,1]\) and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B^*=\{c\in C:z_c^*=1\}\) has \(|B^*|\le k\) and optimizes the stated relevance-redundancy objective.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quadratic relevance-minus-similarity selection is a standard finite batch-diversification model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite quadratic selection model is internally correct and algorithm is the appropriate kind, but it is one possible redundancy-aware policy. No inspectable source establishes this objective or its similarity conventions for cut-batch management.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Size-Aware Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut selection constrained by row count, nonzeros, or predicted relaxation-solving cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate cut \(c\in C\), let \(r_c\) be its predicted benefit and \(a_c\ge0\) its estimated relaxation-size cost, such as added nonzeros or incremental solution time. Given limits \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) and \(A\ge0\), solve \[z^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}\left\{\sum_{c\in C}r_cz_c:\sum_{c\in C}z_c\le k,\ \sum_{c\in C}a_cz_c\le A,\ z_c\in\{0,1\}\right\}.\] Return the rows indexed by \(B^*=\{c:z_c^*=1\}\). A penalized variant replaces the size constraint by subtracting \(\mu\sum_ca_cz_c\), where \(\mu\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admit cuts with high predicted benefit while respecting limits on row count and estimated relaxation-growth cost.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite, \(a_c\ge0\), and \(A\ge0\).
Benefits and costs are evaluated on the current relaxation state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|B^*|\le k\) and \(\sum_{c\in B^*}a_c\le A\).

notation.meaning: estimated relaxation-size cost of cut c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cardinality-and-resource-constrained subset selection is a standard admission model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The resource-constrained subset-selection algorithm is precise, but treating nonzeros and predicted solution time as interchangeable additive costs is an application-specific modeling choice unsupported by a cited cut-management source.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Hybrid, dynamic, and ensemble cut selectors

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Score Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear aggregation of normalized cut-quality features followed by budgeted ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each candidate \(c\in C\) have normalized feature vector \(x(c)\in[0,1]^p\), and choose weights \(w\in\mathbb R_+^p\). Compute \(s(c)=w^\top x(c)\). Given batch limit \(k\), threshold \(\tau\), and deterministic tie-breaking order, form \(E=\{c\in C:s(c)\ge\tau\}\) and return the first \(\min\{k,|E|\}\) elements of \(E\) in nonincreasing score order. Features may include violation, efficacy, orthogonality, sparsity, or predicted objective improvement; their scaling and score orientation must be fixed before applying the rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize cut features, combine them with nonnegative weights, discard low scores, and admit the highest-scoring cuts up to the batch limit.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite, \(x(c)\in[0,1]^p\), and \(w\ge0\).
\(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) and ties follow a fixed total order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\subseteq\{c:s(c)\ge\tau\}\), \(|B|\le k\), and every selected cut precedes every unselected eligible cut in score order.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linear multi-criteria scoring followed by top-k selection is standard
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ranking algorithm is well defined and fits the leaf, but no source supports the stated cut features, normalization conventions, or linear aggregation as the intended cut-selection policy.

children.title: Threshold-Based Selection
children.top_down_role: Candidate admission controlled by quality or resource thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold-Based Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admission by simultaneous lower or upper bounds on cut-quality attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite candidate set \(C\), let \(q_j:C\to\mathbb R\) be quality measures for \(j=1,\ldots,p\). Partition indices into lower-bound criteria \(L\) and upper-bound criteria \(U\), with thresholds \(\ell_j\) and \(u_j\). Define \[E=\{c\in C:q_j(c)\ge\ell_j\ \text{for all }j\in L,\ q_j(c)\le u_j\ \text{for all }j\in U\}.\] If \(|E|\le k\), return \(E\); otherwise return the first \(k\) elements under a predetermined priority order. Thus every admitted cut satisfies every active threshold, although eligible cuts may be omitted because of the batch limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is eligible only if every active quality measure passes its prescribed threshold; a fixed priority rule enforces the batch limit.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and all \(q_j(c)\) are defined.
\(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) and the priority order is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\subseteq E\) and \(|B|\le k\).

notation.meaning: j-th quality measure of cut c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conjunctive threshold filtering is an unambiguous finite-set selection rule
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conjunctive threshold algorithm is mathematically precise and matches the title, but it is an uncited policy construction rather than source-supported cut-management knowledge.

children.title: Filter Cascades
children.top_down_role: Candidate screening through ordered filtering stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Cascades
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential application of eligibility filters to progressively smaller candidate sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0=C\) be a finite candidate set and let \(F_i:2^C\to2^C\) satisfy \(F_i(A)\subseteq A\) for every \(A\subseteq C\) and \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Given the ordered list \((F_1,\ldots,F_m)\), compute \(C_i=F_i(C_{i-1})\) sequentially. If \(C_i=\varnothing\), set \(C_j=\varnothing\) for every \(j=i+1,\ldots,m\) and stop evaluating filters. Return \(C_m\); if a final batch limit \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) is imposed, retain the first \(\min\{k,|C_m|\}\) candidates under a fixed priority order. A filter may use statistics recomputed from its current input, so the order is part of the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply an ordered sequence of contracting filters, propagate an empty result through all remaining stages, and optionally truncate the final surviving set to a batch limit.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and \(F_i(A)\subseteq A\) for every \(A\subseteq C\).
The cascade order and final priority rule are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_m\subseteq C_{m-1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq C_0=C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: composition of contracting set filters gives the canonical cascade semantics

children.title: Cascade Ordering Effects
children.top_down_role: Selection consequences arising from filter order and early rejection.

knowledge_statements.title: Cascade Ordering Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncommuting, state-dependent filters can produce order-dependent admitted cut sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cascade order is invariant when all filters commute on every reachable subset: \(F_i(F_j(A))=F_j(F_i(A))\). Without commutativity, equal outputs are not guaranteed. For example, let \(C=\{a,b\}\), let \(F(A)\) retain one element of \(A\) maximizing \(u\), and let \(G(A)=\{c\in A:v(c)\ge1\}\), where \(u(a)=2\), \(u(b)=1\), \(v(a)=0\), and \(v(b)=1\). Then \(G(F(C))=\varnothing\), whereas \(F(G(C))=\{b\}\). Hence changing the order of individually contracting filters can change both batch composition and cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter order is harmless under commutativity, but noncommuting filters can return different batches or even turn a nonempty result into an empty one.
assumptions_latex: Each filter maps subsets of the finite candidate set into themselves.
Filters may rank or threshold using their current input subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(F(C))\ne F(G(C))\) in the displayed example.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit two-element construction directly establishes the stated failure boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct and the failure_boundary kind fits exactly, but the record has no inspectable citation. Standard-field rationale supports candidacy but does not establish the cut-management interpretation.

children.title: Adaptive Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection policies that change in response to observed solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online adjustment of cut-admission parameters using observed solver feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(t\), observe candidate features \(X_t\), use \(\theta_t\in\Theta\) to select \(B_t=\pi_{\theta_t}(X_t)\), and observe feedback \(y_t\) measuring the resulting solver outcome. Construct a loss \(\ell_t:\Theta\to\mathbb R\), choose \(g_t\in\partial\ell_t(\theta_t)\), and update \[\theta_{t+1}=\Pi_\Theta(\theta_t-\eta_tg_t),\] where \(\eta_t>0\) and \(\Pi_\Theta\) is the Euclidean projection onto the nonempty closed convex set \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). Stop at a prescribed round or when \(\|\theta_{t+1}-\theta_t\|\le\varepsilon\), and output the current policy and admitted batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select cuts with the current parameters, observe solver feedback, and update the parameters by a projected online step over a closed convex parameter set until a prescribed stopping condition holds.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\ell_t:\Theta\to\mathbb R\) and its feedback construction are specified before the update.
\(g_t\in\partial\ell_t(\theta_t)\) exists and \(\eta_t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_{t+1}\in\Theta\) and \(B_t=\pi_{\theta_t}(X_t)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projected online updating over a closed convex set is a standard adaptive update

children.title: Context-Aware Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection policies conditioned on node, phase, family, or relaxation context.

knowledge_statements.title: Context-Aware Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection conditioned on the current node, relaxation, and candidate-pool state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\in\mathcal H\) encode the current solver context, including prescribed node, relaxation, incumbent, and candidate-pool statistics. A context-aware policy consists of a measurable parameter map \(\phi:\mathcal H\to\Theta\) and a feasible selector \(\pi_\theta\). On input \((h,C)\), compute \(\theta=\phi(h)\), evaluate the candidates using \(\pi_\theta\), and return \(B=\pi_{\phi(h)}(C)\subseteq C\). The selector must satisfy the fixed admission constraints, such as \(|B|\le k(h)\) and any relaxation-size budget \(a(B)\le A(h)\), for every admissible context.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map the current solver state to policy parameters, then select a feasible cut batch using those context-specific parameters and budgets.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and \(h\in\mathcal H\).
\(\phi\) and \(\pi_\theta\) are fixed at decision time.
The context-dependent feasibility budgets are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\pi_{\phi(h)}(C)\subseteq C\), \(|B|\le k(h)\), and \(a(B)\le A(h)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: state-conditioned parameterization is the standard mathematical form of contextual decision rules
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state-conditioned selector is coherent and fits the algorithm leaf, but the chosen context variables, parameter map, and context-dependent budgets are not supported by an inspectable cut-selection source.

children.title: Adaptation Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Robustness limits for changing policies across solver contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction criterion separating stable parameter adaptation from regimes lacking a convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let adaptation under a fixed context be \(\theta_{t+1}=T(\theta_t)\) on a complete metric space \((\Theta,d)\). A sufficient stability boundary is the existence of \(q<1\) such that \(d(T(\theta),T(\theta'))\le qd(\theta,\theta')\) for all \(\theta,\theta'\in\Theta\). Then the update has a unique fixed point \(\theta^*\) and \(d(\theta_t,\theta^*)\le q^t d(\theta_0,\theta^*)\). If only a Lipschitz bound with \(q\ge1\) is available, contraction-based convergence and perturbation attenuation are not certified; additional structure or damping is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contraction factor below one guarantees stable convergence to a unique policy parameter; a bound at least one provides no such certificate.
assumptions_latex: \((\Theta,d)\) is complete.
\(T:\Theta\to\Theta\) is globally Lipschitz with constant \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q<1\Rightarrow d(\theta_t,\theta^*)\le q^t d(\theta_0,\theta^*)\); \(q\ge1\) gives no contraction certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard contraction-mapping stability boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contraction condition and its conclusion are mathematically standard and correctly stated, and condition is the appropriate kind. A specific source is still required both for the contraction theorem and for its interpretation as a boundary for cut-policy adaptation.

children.title: Ensemble Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Portfolio-based selection using multiple policy outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Ensemble Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of multiple cut selectors by weighted voting with feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a finite candidate set and let \(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_M\) be base policies producing \(B_m=\pi_m(h,C)\subseteq C\). Given \(w_m\ge0\) with \(\sum_{m=1}^M w_m=1\) and a threshold \(\tau\in(0,1]\), assign \(v(c)=\sum_{m=1}^M w_m\mathbf 1\{c\in B_m\}\). Form \(E=\{c\in C:v(c)\ge\tau\}\), order \(E\) by nonincreasing vote with fixed tie-breaking, and scan that order once, admitting a candidate whenever doing so preserves all prescribed cardinality and relaxation-size constraints. Return the resulting feasible batch \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine base selectors using normalized nonnegative votes, retain candidates meeting a positive vote threshold, and scan them in vote order while preserving all admission constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and the base-policy family are finite.
Tie-breaking and feasibility constraints are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\subseteq E\subseteq\bigcup_{m=1}^M B_m\), and \(B\) satisfies all prescribed admission constraints.

notation.meaning: weighted admission vote for cut c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive-threshold weighted voting followed by feasibility restoration is a standard ensemble construction

children.title: Learning-Based Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Data-driven policies for selecting cuts or cut families.

knowledge_statements.title: Learning-Based Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supervised empirical-risk training of a feasible context-dependent cut selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given training samples \((h_i,C_i,y_i)_{i=1}^N\), where each \(C_i\) is finite and \(y_i(c)\) is a target utility or admission label for \(c\in C_i\), define \[J(\theta)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{c\in C_i}\ell(s_\theta(h_i,c),y_i(c))+\lambda R(\theta).\] Assuming \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}J(\theta)\ne\varnothing\), choose \(\widehat\theta\) from this set. At deployment, score each \(c\in C\) by \(s_{\widehat\theta}(h,c)\), order candidates by decreasing score with fixed tie-breaking, and scan the order once, admitting a candidate whenever doing so preserves the prescribed batch and relaxation-size constraints. Return the resulting feasible batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a regularized empirical training objective with an attained minimizer, then rank new candidates by the learned score and admit them while preserving fixed feasibility budgets.
assumptions_latex: \(N\in\mathbb Z_+\), every \(C_i\) is finite, and all targets \(y_i(c)\) are defined.
\(\ell\), \(R\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\Theta\) are fixed, and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}J(\theta)\ne\varnothing\).
Deployment uses the same feature semantics as training, and its tie-breaking and feasibility constraints are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=\pi_{\widehat\theta}(h,C)\subseteq C\) satisfies the prescribed admission constraints.

notation.meaning: learned contextual score for candidate c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: attained regularized empirical-risk minimization followed by constrained ranking is a standard learned-selection formulation

children.title: Hybrid Policy Arbitration
children.top_down_role: Coordination between ensemble outputs and learned policy recommendations.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Policy Arbitration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitration between rule-based and learned cut-admission scores within one separation round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidates \(C\), features \(\phi(c,s)\), a deterministic score \(h(c,s)\), a learned score \(\ell_\theta(\phi(c,s))\), and gate \(g_\eta(s)\in[0,1]\), compute \[q(c,s)=(1-g_\eta(s))h(c,s)+g_\eta(s)\ell_\theta(\phi(c,s)).\] Discard every \(c\) failing validity or mandatory efficacy tests. Rank the remainder by \(q\), admit the highest-ranked cuts subject to the round budget and compatibility constraints, and stop when no eligible cut remains or the budget is exhausted. If a learned score or gate is unavailable, nonfinite, or outside its declared domain, set \(g_\eta(s)=0\) for that decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blend heuristic and learned cut scores through a state-dependent gate, then admit valid cuts by blended rank under budget and compatibility constraints, with deterministic fallback.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite candidate set and every admitted member is valid for the integer-feasible region.
\(h\), \(\ell_\theta\), and \(g_\eta\) are defined on their declared inputs.
The admission budget and compatibility predicate are fixed for the current round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\subseteq C\) is the budget-feasible set returned by gated score arbitration.

notation.meaning: hybrid admission score of candidate cut c

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this specific learning-based arbitration rule.
Policy is a precise interface definition, not a convergence claim.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the particular convex score blend, gate behavior, ranking procedure, and deterministic fallback are substantive design choices with no cited support.

children.title: Separator Scheduling Integration Interface
children.top_down_role: Temporal orchestration of separators and their coordination with the surrounding branch-and-cut relaxation loop.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Node Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated cut generation at the root relaxation before ordinary tree processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the mixed-integer feasible set, let \(P^0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a root relaxation satisfying \(X\subseteq P^0\), and let \(R_{\max}\in\mathbb N\) be the root-round limit. For each \(r=0,\ldots,R_{\max}-1\), solve the current relaxation \(P^r\). If it is infeasible, terminate. Otherwise, obtain an optimal relaxation solution \(x^r\), invoke the enabled separators, and retain a finite family \(A^r\) of inequalities valid for \(X\). Set \[P^{r+1}=P^r\cap\bigcap_{(a,b):\,a^\top x\le b\in A^r}\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a^\top x\le b\}.\] Stop if \(A^r=\varnothing\), if \(x^r\in X\), or if another root budget or stopping guard is reached. Return the final root relaxation for subsequent branch-and-cut processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the root, repeatedly solve the current relaxation, separate an optimal relaxation solution, add admitted cuts valid for the mixed-integer feasible set, and stop on infeasibility, integrality, stalling, or budget exhaustion.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the mixed-integer feasible set and \(X\subseteq P^0\).
\(R_{\max}\in\mathbb N\) is fixed for the root-separation episode.
Every inequality admitted in \(A^r\) is valid for \(X\), and each relaxation solve returns a certified status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the returned relaxation is \(P^k\), then \(X\subseteq P^k\subseteq P^0\).

notation.meaning: root relaxation after r completed separation rounds
optimal solution of the current feasible root relaxation
finite family of valid cuts admitted in round r
maximum number of attempted root-separation rounds

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Node Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local or globally valid separation at a nonroot branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be a live nonroot node, let \(X_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the mixed-integer feasible set compatible with its node domain, let \(P_v^0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(X_v\subseteq P_v^0\), and let \(R_v\in\mathbb N\) be its separation-round limit. For each \(r=0,\ldots,R_v-1\), solve \(P_v^r\). If it is infeasible, prune \(v\). Otherwise, obtain an optimal relaxation solution \(x_v^r\), separate it, and partition the admitted inequalities into a finite globally valid family \(G^r\) and a finite family \(L_v^r\) valid throughout the domain of \(v\). Update \[P_v^{r+1}=P_v^r\cap\bigcap_{(a,b):\,a^\top x\le b\in G^r\cup L_v^r}\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a^\top x\le b\}.\] Propagate an admitted inequality only to nodes whose domains lie within its validity domain. Stop on integrality, absence of admitted cuts, pruning by a valid bound, or exhaustion of the node budget; otherwise return the strengthened node relaxation for branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a live nonroot node, repeatedly solve its relaxation and add admitted global or node-local cuts through their corresponding halfspaces, respecting each cut's validity domain until pruning, integrality, stalling, or budget exhaustion.
assumptions_latex: \(X_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the feasible mixed-integer set compatible with node \(v\), and \(X_v\subseteq P_v^0\).
Every inequality in \(G^r\) is globally valid, and every inequality in \(L_v^r\) is valid throughout the domain of \(v\).
\(R_v\in\mathbb N\) is fixed, and each relaxation solve returns a certified status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every completed update, \(X_v\subseteq P_v^{r+1}\subseteq P_v^r\), so the returned relaxation preserves all feasible solutions compatible with \(v\).

notation.meaning: mixed-integer feasible set compatible with node v
node relaxation after r completed separation rounds
optimal solution of the current feasible node relaxation
globally valid inequalities admitted in round r
inequalities admitted in round r and valid throughout node v's domain
maximum number of separation rounds at node v

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Triggered Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation invoked when a newly accepted incumbent supplies a designated trigger state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\) is accepted, evaluate a trigger predicate \(T(\bar x,s)\). If it is false, perform no incumbent-triggered round. If it is true, invoke the designated separators using \(\bar x\) and state \(s\), retain only cuts valid on their declared global or local domains, and admit a budget-feasible family \(A(\bar x,s)\). Install each admitted cut only within its validity domain, update affected relaxations, and resume search. The trigger may depend on incumbent improvement, age, violation diagnostics, or remaining budget, but it must not substitute observed violation at \(\bar x\) for a validity test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A new incumbent may trigger designated separators; admitted cuts must independently pass validity and budget checks before affected relaxations are updated.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is feasible for the mixed-integer model currently being solved.
\(T\) is a deterministic predicate of the incumbent and recorded solver state.
Every admitted cut has a certified validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All relaxations modified by \(A(\bar x,s)\) retain every feasible solution in their respective validity domains.
review_flags: Supplied branch-and-cut locators do not identify an incumbent-triggered separation regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but separation performed using a feasible incumbent is not a standard violated-cut separation step without further separator semantics. No source supports the trigger regime or clarifies what information the incumbent supplies.

children.title: Restart-Epoch Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation behavior at solver restarts and renewed search epochs.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Epoch Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation scheduled immediately after a search restart establishes a new root epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At restart epoch \(e\), construct a new root relaxation \(P_e^0\) from the original formulation and cuts selected for transfer. Solve it to obtain \(x_e^0\), then perform at most \(R_e\) separation rounds. In round \(r\), generate and admit valid cuts \(A_e^r\) and set \[P_e^{r+1}=P_e^r\cap\bigcap_{a^\top x\le b\in A_e^r}\{x:a^\top x\le b\}.\] Stop on stalling, infeasibility, integrality, or epoch-budget exhaustion. Start the restarted tree from the final relaxation, while preserving the incumbent and all globally valid bounds required by the restart protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a restart, rebuild the root relaxation, transfer eligible cuts, run a bounded root-separation phase, and launch the new search epoch.
assumptions_latex: Transferred and newly admitted cuts are valid for the restarted model.
\(R_e\) and the epoch resource budget are finite.
The incumbent and global bounds retained across restart remain valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final \(P_e\) is a valid strengthened root relaxation for restart epoch \(e\).

notation.meaning: root relaxation in epoch e after r rounds
cuts admitted in epoch e, round r

review_flags: The supplied locator supports branch-and-cut generally but may not specify restart epochs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic branch-and-cut locator does not specifically support restart epochs, cut transfer, preservation of bounds, or the stated restart protocol. A restart-specific source is required.

children.title: Reoptimization Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation during repeated optimization after model or state changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation after model data change, using a reoptimized relaxation and revalidated cut state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a modified model \(M'\), first revalidate every retained cut against the feasible set and variable space of \(M'\); remove any cut lacking a valid transfer certificate. Form the resulting relaxation \(P'^0\), reoptimize it to obtain \(x'^0\), and execute bounded separation rounds. In round \(r\), admit cuts \(A'^r\) valid for \(M'\) and set \[P'^{r+1}=P'^r\cap\bigcap_{a^\top x\le b\in A'^r}\{x:a^\top x\le b\}.\] Stop on stalling, infeasibility, integrality, or budget exhaustion, and return the final relaxation and bound for the reoptimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After model modification, revalidate retained cuts, reoptimize the relaxation, and separate it using only cuts valid for the modified model.
assumptions_latex: The modified model \(M'\) and its variable correspondence are explicitly defined.
A retained cut is installed only if its validity transfers to \(M'\).
Each newly admitted cut is valid for \(M'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned relaxation contains the feasible set of \(M'\) and supplies a valid reoptimization bound.

notation.meaning: cuts admitted for the modified model in round r

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports cut revalidation under model modification.
The admissible transfer certificate depends on the permitted model changes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but validity transfer depends materially on which model and variable-space modifications are permitted. No source establishes the claimed revalidation protocol or transfer certificate.

children.title: Cut-State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Retention, reassessment, and migration of cut state across restart or reoptimization boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-State Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility conditions for carrying stored cuts into a restart or reoptimization state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a stored cut be \(a^\top x\le b\), with validity domain \(D\), variable map \(\pi\), and metadata \(m\). It is transferable from state \(s\) to state \(s'\) exactly when: the mapped inequality is well-defined in the variable space of \(s'\); every feasible point of \(s'\) lying in the mapped domain satisfies it; its local-domain predicate remains enforceable; and its numerical representation passes the destination tolerances. A transferable cut may carry age, activity, and provenance metadata, but such metadata does not establish validity. A cut failing any condition must be discarded or independently regenerated and certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored cut transfers only when its variables, validity domain, local scope, and numerical representation remain valid in the destination state.
assumptions_latex: The source and destination variable spaces and map \(\pi\) are known.
The cut's global or local validity domain \(D\) is recorded.
Destination feasibility and numerical tolerances are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transferred cut is installed only if it remains valid throughout its enforceable destination domain.

notation.meaning: recorded validity domain of the cut
nonvalidity metadata carried with the cut

review_flags: No supplied source directly specifies restart or reoptimization cut-state transfer conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the exact biconditional is unsupported. Passing destination tolerances is an installation condition rather than mathematical validity, and the required transfer conditions depend on the permitted state transformation.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Frequency Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic eligibility rule controlling how often each separator may be invoked.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each separator \(j\), let \(f_j\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), eligible depth set \(D_j\subseteq\mathbb N\), and optional cooldown \(c_j\in\mathbb N\). At search event \(t\), node depth \(d_t\), and last invocation \(\tau_j\), separator \(j\) is frequency-eligible when \[d_t\in D_j,\qquad t\equiv o_j\pmod{f_j},\qquad t-\tau_j\ge c_j,\] and all global resource guards hold. Root-only, every-node, and periodic policies arise by choosing \(D_j\), \(f_j\), and offset \(o_j\). Eligibility permits invocation but does not require it when higher-priority scheduling or budget constraints intervene.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator is frequency-eligible only at configured depths, periodic event offsets, and after its cooldown, subject to global resource guards.
assumptions_latex: Search events \(t\) and depths \(d_t\) are integer-indexed.
Each separator has fixed frequency, offset, eligible depths, and cooldown.
Budget and priority guards are evaluated separately from frequency eligibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate determines when separator \(j\) may be scheduled, without asserting that it must run.
review_flags: The formula is a generic scheduling interface; solver-specific frequency semantics may differ.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the cited general branch-and-cut section does not establish the particular event-index congruence, cooldown, depth-set, and offset semantics. The domain of the offset is also not specified.

children.title: Separation-Round Limits
children.top_down_role: Caps governing the number of separation rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Round Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard cap on successive solve-separate-add cycles within one separation episode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a separation episode with nonnegative integer limit \(R_{\max}\). Initialize the round counter at \(r=0\). A new solve-separate-add round may begin only if \(r<R_{\max}\) and every other stopping guard is false. After each attempted round, increment \(r\) once, irrespective of whether the round generates or admits cuts. Hence the episode performs at most \(R_{\max}\) attempted rounds. Early termination remains mandatory when the relaxation is infeasible, an accepted stopping state is reached, no admissible progress is possible, or a stricter time, work, or cut budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation episode can attempt at most a configured number of rounds and may stop earlier under feasibility, progress, or tighter resource guards.
assumptions_latex: \(R_{\max}\in\mathbb N\) is fixed at episode initialization.
A round is one attempted solve-separate-add cycle.
The round counter is incremented exactly once per attempted cycle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of attempted rounds \(R\) satisfies \(0\le R\le R_{\max}\).

notation.meaning: maximum attempted rounds in the episode

review_flags: Exact round-counting convention is an interface definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is internally precise, but counting every attempted cycle, including an unproductive one, is an interface convention not supported by the cited general branch-and-cut locator.

children.title: Per-Round Cut Limits
children.top_down_role: Caps governing cut volume within a single separation round.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Round Cut Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality budget applied independently to the cuts admitted in each round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For separation round \(r\), let \(C_r\) be the finite candidate family and let \(K_r\in\mathbb N\) be its admission cap. The selected family \(A_r\) must satisfy \[A_r\subseteq C_r,\qquad |A_r|\le K_r,\] together with all validity, compatibility, and numerical admissibility predicates. If more than \(K_r\) candidates remain eligible, a declared ranking and tie-breaking rule chooses the admitted subset. The cap counts installed cuts, not merely generated candidates, unless the interface explicitly declares a generation cap. Unused capacity in round \(r\) is not transferred to another round unless a separate cross-round quota permits it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each round admits no more than its cut cap; excess eligible cuts are ranked, and unused capacity does not carry over by default.
assumptions_latex: \(C_r\) is finite and \(K_r\in\mathbb N\).
Validity and numerical admissibility are tested before installation.
Ranking and tie-breaking are declared when eligible candidates exceed the cap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The installed family in round \(r\) satisfies \(|A_r|\le K_r\).

notation.meaning: candidate cuts generated in round r

review_flags: Admission-versus-generation counting is an explicit interface convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the cited locator does not specifically support counting installed rather than generated cuts or the default prohibition on carrying unused capacity across rounds.

children.title: Cross-Round Cut Quotas
children.top_down_role: Aggregate cut allowances distributed across multiple rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Round Cut Quotas
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cumulative cut-admission budget shared across several rounds of one separation episode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an episode contain rounds \(r=0,\ldots,R-1\), with installed cut families \(A_r\), nonnegative cut costs \(w(c)\), and cumulative quota \(Q\ge0\). Admission in round \(r\) is permitted only if \[\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\sum_{c\in A_i}w(c)+\sum_{c\in A_r}w(c)\le Q.\] With \(w(c)=1\), this is a cardinality quota. The remaining quota before round \(r\) equals \(Q-\sum_{i<r}\sum_{c\in A_i}w(c)\). Per-round caps may further restrict admission; they cannot authorize violation of the cumulative quota. The episode stops admitting cuts when the remaining quota is insufficient for every eligible candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cumulative quota bounds total cut cost across rounds; per-round caps may tighten but cannot exceed this shared budget.
assumptions_latex: The episode has finite quota \(Q\ge0\).
Every admitted cut has declared nonnegative cost \(w(c)\).
Installed families \(A_r\) are recorded without double counting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every prefix of the episode has cumulative admitted-cut cost at most \(Q\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly specifies cumulative cross-round cut quotas.
Weighted quota is a generic interface formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cumulative-budget condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no source supports the weighted cross-round quota or its stopping semantics.

children.title: Wall-Clock Separation Limits
children.top_down_role: Elapsed-time allowances for separation activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Wall-Clock Separation Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elapsed real-time budget for a separation episode, including declared accounting boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t_0\) be the monotonic-clock time at episode start and let \(T_{\max}\ge0\) be its wall-clock budget. Before launching any interruptible separation task at time \(t\), require \(t-t_0<T_{\max}\). During execution, poll or interrupt according to the declared scheduler granularity; after the first observation with \(t-t_0\ge T_{\max}\), launch no further task and terminate the episode after required cleanup. The accounting convention must declare whether relaxation solves, synchronization, and cut installation are included. Because interruption is discrete, actual elapsed time may exceed \(T_{\max}\) by at most the latency of one noninterruptible segment plus cleanup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotonic elapsed-time budget prevents new separation work after expiry, with bounded overshoot determined by polling and noninterruptible cleanup.
assumptions_latex: \(T_{\max}\ge0\) and \(t_0\) are fixed at episode start.
Elapsed time is measured by a monotonic clock.
Every task is interruptible or has a declared finite noninterruptible latency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No new separation task begins after observed elapsed time reaches \(T_{\max}\).
review_flags: No supplied source directly specifies wall-clock accounting or interruption semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The wall-clock condition fits the leaf, but the claimed overshoot bound requires an explicit bound on polling or interrupt-response latency in addition to noninterruptible work and cleanup. No source supports the accounting and interruption semantics.

children.title: Computational Work Limits
children.top_down_role: Allowances measured through solver effort or resource consumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Computational Work Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic accounting limit for one separation episode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the scheduled separator calls and let \(w_s\ge 0\) denote the charged work of call \(s\), measured in a fixed unit such as oracle calls or processed rows. Given budget \(B_W\ge 0\), a work-feasible execution may start a call only when its reserved charge fits the remaining budget, and it must satisfy \[W(S):=\sum_{s\in S}w_s\le B_W.\] If actual charges are revealed after execution, the scheduler instead reserves certified upper bounds \(\widehat w_s\ge w_s\), ensuring \(\sum_{s\in S}\widehat w_s\le B_W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total charged separator work cannot exceed the prescribed budget; uncertain call costs are controlled using valid upper-bound reservations.
assumptions_latex: \(B_W\ge 0\) is fixed for the separation episode.
\(w_s\ge 0\) is measured consistently across calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(S)\le B_W\)

notation.meaning: charged work of separator call s
set or sequence of executed calls

review_flags: work-accounting convention is an interface parameterization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited branch-and-cut-system section does not specifically substantiate the additive work-accounting and certified-reservation policy. This is a feasibility condition or interface policy, not a complexity bound.

children.title: Budget Conversion Policies
children.top_down_role: Calibration between time-based and work-based separation allowances.

knowledge_statements.title: Budget Conversion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts wall-clock allowances into conservative work budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a time allowance \(B_T\ge 0\), a calibrated upper work rate \(\rho\ge 0\), and a safety factor \(\eta\in[0,1]\). Initialize the computational-work allowance by \[B_W:=\left\lfloor \eta\rho B_T\right\rfloor.\] During execution, after observed pairs \((T_k,W_k)\), a policy may update \(\rho\) only to a certified upper rate \(\rho_k\) and set the remaining allowance to \(\lfloor\eta\rho_k(B_T-T_k)_+\rfloor\). The scheduler outputs this allowance and admits calls by the computational-work limit; conversion never overrides the wall-clock stop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A calibrated work rate and safety factor convert remaining time into a conservative work allowance without disabling the time limit.
assumptions_latex: All time and work observations use consistent units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_W=\lfloor\eta\rho B_T\rfloor\) initially, with both time and work limits enforced.
review_flags: conversion formula is a configurable interface policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conversion formula and adaptive rate update are configurable engineering choices not supported by the cited general branch-and-cut section. The meaning of a certified upper work rate also does not by itself establish the claimed wall-clock conservatism.

children.title: Stall Detection Criteria
children.top_down_role: Signals used to identify ineffective separation activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Stall Detection Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed predicate for insufficient separation progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_k\) be a scalar progress measure after separation round \(k\), oriented so that larger values are better. For window length \(m\in\mathbb N\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and minimum eligible round \(k_0\), declare a stall at round \(k\) precisely when \[k\ge \max\{k_0,m\}\quad\text{and}\quad q_k-q_{k-m}\le\varepsilon.\] If progress is multidimensional, the configured scalarization defining \(q_k\) must be fixed throughout the window. Missing or incomparable measurements do not satisfy the predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stall occurs when improvement over a complete observation window is no greater than the configured tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\), \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and \(k_0\ge 0\).
The progress measure is comparable throughout each window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{stall}(k)\iff k\ge\max\{k_0,m\}\ \land\ q_k-q_{k-m}\le\varepsilon\)
review_flags: stall metric and thresholds are implementation parameters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The windowed difference predicate is a coherent configurable stall criterion, but the cited source does not specifically support this exact metric, threshold rule, or missing-measurement convention.

children.title: Progress-Based Continuation
children.top_down_role: Progress signals supporting continued separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Based Continuation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation predicate under progress and remaining resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(k\), let \(g_k\ge 0\) be the measured progress over the configured observation window, let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}>0\) be the continuation threshold, and let \(R_k\) indicate that both time and work budgets permit another call. Separation continues exactly when \[R_k=1\quad\text{and}\quad g_k\ge\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}.\] Before a complete observation window exists, a configured warm-up rule may set the progress test to true. Exhaustion of either hard budget makes \(R_k=0\) and therefore overrides observed progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation continues only while measured progress reaches its threshold and all hard resource limits permit another call.
assumptions_latex: \(g_k\ge 0\) is computed by a fixed progress rule.
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{continue}(k)\iff R_k=1\ \land\ g_k\ge\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cont}}\)
review_flags: continuation threshold is a configurable policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact continuation equivalence, warm-up behavior, and combination of time and work admissibility are implementation policies not established by the cited textbook section.

children.title: Stopping Hysteresis
children.top_down_role: Stability controls that prevent oscillation between continuation and stopping.

knowledge_statements.title: Stopping Hysteresis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-threshold state machine suppressing stop–continue oscillation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose thresholds \(0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{resume}}\) and maintain state \(z_k\in\{0,1\}\), where one means separation is enabled. Given progress \(g_k\), update by \[z_{k+1}=\begin{cases}0,&z_k=1\text{ and }g_k\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stop}},\\1,&z_k=0\text{ and }g_k\ge\varepsilon_{\mathrm{resume}},\\z_k,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] A hard resource stop forces \(z_{k+1}=0\). Thus measurements strictly between the thresholds preserve the prior state, preventing repeated switching caused by small fluctuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct stopping and resumption thresholds create a deadband in which the previous separation state is retained.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{resume}}\).
\(g_k\) is measured consistently between updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}<g_k<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{resume}}\Rightarrow z_{k+1}=z_k\)
review_flags: hysteresis state machine is an interface design pattern

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-threshold state machine fits the leaf and algorithm kind, but the cited branch-and-cut section does not substantiate this particular hysteresis mechanism or its hard-stop interaction.

children.title: Separator Priority Ordering
children.top_down_role: Relative execution precedence among separators.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Priority Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic ordering of currently eligible separator families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each eligible separator \(i\) at scheduling epoch \(k\), compute a priority score \(p_i(k)\in\mathbb R\). Order eligible separators by nonincreasing score, so that \(i\) precedes \(j\) whenever \(p_i(k)>p_j(k)\). Resolve equal scores using a fixed total tie-break order \(\prec_0\). Traverse the resulting order, invoking each separator only while its eligibility predicate remains true and the separation budget admits its reserved cost. The output is the resulting deterministic invocation sequence for epoch \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eligible separators are invoked by decreasing priority, with deterministic tie-breaking and resource feasibility checked before every call.
assumptions_latex: The eligible separator set is finite at each epoch.
Each priority score is defined when ordering occurs.
\(\prec_0\) is a fixed total order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i(k)>p_j(k)\Rightarrow i\text{ precedes }j\)

notation.meaning: priority score of separator i at epoch k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic priority-and-tie-break algorithm fits the container, but the cited portfolio-selection and branch-and-cut sections do not specifically support this separator scheduling rule.

children.title: Invocation Delay Policies
children.top_down_role: Conditions for postponing separator execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Invocation Delay Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility rule imposing initial and inter-call delays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For separator \(i\), choose an initial eligibility epoch \(a_i\ge 0\) and a minimum inter-invocation delay \(d_i\ge 0\). Let \(\ell_i(k)\) be its most recent invocation epoch before \(k\), with value \(-\infty\) if it has never run. The separator is delay-eligible at epoch \(k\) exactly when \[k\ge a_i\quad\text{and}\quad \bigl(\ell_i(k)=-\infty\ \text{or}\ k-\ell_i(k)\ge d_i\bigr).\] Delay eligibility is necessary but not sufficient: activation, priority, and resource tests may still prevent invocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator may run only after its initial release epoch and, subsequently, after its configured minimum spacing has elapsed.
assumptions_latex: Scheduling epochs are totally ordered and integer-valued.
\(a_i,d_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{delayEligible}_i(k)\iff k\ge a_i\land(\ell_i(k)=-\infty\lor k-\ell_i(k)\ge d_i)\)
review_flags: delay semantics are an interface parameterization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The initial-release and inter-invocation-delay predicate is an implementation-specific parameterization not supported by the cited general branch-and-cut material.

children.title: Priority-Delay Interactions
children.top_down_role: Scheduling effects arising when precedence and postponement policies overlap.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Delay Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for priority ordering and delay eligibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At epoch \(k\), let \(E_k\) be the active separators satisfying their invocation-delay predicates. Priority ordering is applied only to \(E_k\): \[i\text{ is schedulable at }k\iff i\in E_k,\qquad i,j\in E_k,\,p_i(k)>p_j(k)\Rightarrow i\text{ precedes }j.\] Consequently, arbitrarily high priority cannot bypass an unsatisfied delay. After invoking \(i\), its last-invocation epoch is updated immediately, and its delay predicate is recomputed before any possible repeated call in the same epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delay first filters the eligible portfolio; priority orders only the survivors and cannot override a separator's delay.
assumptions_latex: Delay predicates are evaluated before priority ordering.
Priority scores are defined for all delay-eligible separators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\notin E_k\Rightarrow i\text{ is not invoked at }k\), independently of \(p_i(k)\).

notation.meaning: delay-eligible active separators at epoch k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Filter-before-ranking and immediate delay recomputation are plausible interface conventions, but the portfolio-selection citation does not establish them as stated.

children.title: Family Activation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing entry of separator families into the active portfolio.

knowledge_statements.title: Family Activation Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate admitting a separator family to the active portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For separator family \(f\) at epoch \(k\), let \(A_f(k)\) denote applicability to the current relaxation, \(R_f(k)\) resource admissibility, and \(U_f(k)\) policy permission. An inactive family is activated exactly when \[A_f(k)\land R_f(k)\land U_f(k)=1.\] Applicability includes satisfaction of every family-specific structural precondition; resource admissibility requires that a permitted call can fit applicable hard limits. Activation adds \(f\) to the schedulable portfolio but does not itself mandate immediate invocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family becomes active only when it is applicable, resource-admissible, and permitted by the portfolio policy.
assumptions_latex: Each predicate is evaluated on the same solver state.
The family is inactive immediately before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{activate}_f(k)\iff A_f(k)\land R_f(k)\land U_f(k)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three-factor activation equivalence is a configurable lifecycle design, not a result supported by the cited portfolio-selection section.

children.title: Family Deactivation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing removal of separator families from active use.

knowledge_statements.title: Family Deactivation Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate removing an unproductive or inapplicable family from scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active family \(f\) at epoch \(k\), let \(I_f(k)\) indicate current inapplicability, \(X_f(k)\) exhaustion of its family budget, and \(S_f(k)\) a configured stall predicate based on recent family outcomes. Deactivate the family exactly when \[I_f(k)\lor X_f(k)\lor S_f(k)=1.\] Deactivation removes \(f\) from subsequent scheduling without invalidating cuts already accepted from that family. A temporary stall may be designated recoverable, allowing a later reactivation policy to reconsider \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active family is removed when it becomes inapplicable, exhausts its budget, or satisfies its configured stall test.
assumptions_latex: The family is active immediately before evaluation.
Stall observations use a fixed family-specific metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{deactivate}_f(k)\iff I_f(k)\lor X_f(k)\lor S_f(k)\)
review_flags: deactivation disjunction is a configurable lifecycle policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact disjunction of inapplicability, exhaustion, and stall, including recoverability semantics, requires implementation-specific or directly supporting source evidence.

children.title: Family Reactivation Policies
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing renewed use of previously deactivated families.

knowledge_statements.title: Family Reactivation Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cooldown-and-trigger policy for reconsidering deactivated families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each recoverably deactivated family \(f\), store its deactivation epoch \(d_f\), cooldown \(c_f\ge 0\), and solver-state trigger \(T_f(k)\). At epoch \(k\), reconsider \(f\) only if \(k-d_f\ge c_f\) and \(T_f(k)=1\). Re-evaluate the complete family-activation predicate; reactivate \(f\) exactly when that predicate holds, otherwise leave it inactive. Permanent deactivation and exhausted hard family budgets are not recoverable. On reactivation, reset or retain historical performance statistics according to a fixed declared policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recoverably deactivated family is reconsidered after cooldown and a state-change trigger, then must again satisfy all activation criteria.
assumptions_latex: \(c_f\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\).
The deactivation cause is marked recoverable.
The trigger is evaluated on the current solver state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{reactivate}_f(k)\iff k-d_f\ge c_f\land T_f(k)\land\operatorname{activate}_f(k)\)
review_flags: cooldown and trigger semantics require implementation confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cooldown, state trigger, recoverability, and statistic-reset rules form a plausible algorithm but are not supported by the cited portfolio-selection locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Separator Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online selection of separator families from observed reward and cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_k\) be the eligible separator families at epoch \(k\). For each \(f\in F_k\), maintain call count \(n_f(k)\), empirical mean reward \(\widehat\mu_f(k)\), and mean charged cost \(\widehat c_f(k)>0\). With exploration parameter \(\beta>0\), select \[f_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{f\in F_k}\frac{\widehat\mu_f(k)+\beta\sqrt{\log(1+k)/(1+n_f(k))}}{\widehat c_f(k)}.\] Invoke \(f_k\) if its reserved cost fits the remaining budget, observe reward and cost, update its statistics, and stop when no eligible affordable family remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scheduler adaptively favors families with high estimated reward per cost while retaining an exploration bonus for less-tested families.
assumptions_latex: \(F_k\) is finite and contains only eligible families.
Observed rewards are scalar and use a fixed normalization.
\(\widehat c_f(k)>0\) for every candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_k\) maximizes the configured optimistic reward-per-cost index over \(F_k\).

notation.meaning: eligible family portfolio at epoch k
empirical mean reward of family f
empirical mean charged cost of family f

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

review_flags: specific optimistic index is a representative adaptive policy

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Neither cited locator supports the specific cost-normalized UCB-style index. The record also does not define how empirical rewards and costs are initialized before a family has observations, so the selection rule is not fully specified.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\) is the current relaxation and \(\bar x\in P\) is its solved point.
Every separator returns inequalities valid for the same mixed-integer feasible set \(X\subseteq P\).
Separators read an immutable snapshot of \((P,\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^+=P\cap\bigcap_{c\in C^{\mathrm{acc}}}c\) is a valid relaxation of \(X\), independently of separator completion order.

notation.meaning: current relaxation and its solved point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous portfolio execution against one relaxation snapshot, followed by centralized validation and merging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given enabled separators \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\), execute each \(S_i(P,\bar x)\) concurrently on the same immutable snapshot. Collect the returned multisets \(C_i\), discard every inequality lacking a validity certificate for \(X\), canonicalize equivalent inequalities, and apply deterministic efficacy, density, and numerical-safety filters to \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\). Resolve merge conflicts by a fixed total order independent of completion time. Insert the retained set \(C^{\mathrm{acc}}\) only after all required separator tasks finish or their declared budgets expire, and return \(P^+=P\cap\bigcap_{c\in C^{\mathrm{acc}}}c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run separators on one immutable relaxation, validate and deterministically merge their cuts, then insert the accepted batch without depending on task completion order.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Separator Execution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited branch-and-cut section does not specifically support concurrent snapshot execution, deterministic completion-order-independent merging, certification, or timeout semantics. These details materially define the proposed algorithm and require a parallel-separation or solver-interface source.

children.title: Cut Insertion Phase
children.top_down_role: Placement of admitted cuts into the active relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Insertion Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch insertion within a branch-and-cut cut-resolve loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate inequality \(a^\top x\le\beta\), verify validity for \(X\), finite coefficients, admissible scaling, and violation \(a^\top\bar x-\beta\ge\varepsilon_{\mathrm{viol}}>0\). Remove duplicates and candidates rejected by the configured efficacy, parallelism, density, or numerical filters. Let \(C^{\mathrm{acc}}\) be the retained batch.
