Add its inequalities atomically to the relaxation, update the row-to-cut provenance map, invalidate solution-dependent solver state, and output \(P^+=P\cap\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\text{ for every }(a,\beta)\in C^{\mathrm{acc}}\}\). If \(C^{\mathrm{acc}}=\varnothing\), leave \(P\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate, filter, and atomically add violated valid cuts, recording provenance and invalidating solver state that depends on the old relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and every candidate cut is asserted valid for \(X\).
\(\bar x\) is an optimal solution of the current relaxation \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inserted relaxation \(P^+\) satisfies \(X\subseteq P^+\subseteq P\), and every inserted cut excludes \(\bar x\) by at least its acceptance tolerance.

children.title: Relaxation Resolve Phase
children.top_down_role: Solver integration surrounding reoptimization of the modified relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Resolve Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reoptimization immediately following a cut-insertion batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from the solver state inherited from the previous relaxation, reoptimize \(\min\{c^\top x:x\in P^+\}\). Return exactly one outcome: certified infeasible; certified unbounded; certified optimal with \(\bar x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P^+}c^\top x\); or unresolved because a declared numerical or resource limit was reached. On an optimal outcome, publish \(\bar x^+\), its objective value, and the associated basis or warm-start state for subsequent separation. On certified infeasibility, close the current node. An unresolved outcome must not be treated as an optimal separation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimize the strengthened relaxation and report either a certified infeasible, unbounded, or optimal status, or an unresolved condition; when optimal, publish the solution, objective value, and reusable solver state.
assumptions_latex: \(P^+\) is the current relaxation after the preceding insertion phase.
The relaxation solver either returns a certified status or reports an unresolved numerical or resource condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The phase returns either a certified infeasible, unbounded, or optimal status, or an unresolved condition; when optimal, it returns \(\bar x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P^+}c^\top x\).

children.title: Resolve-Triggered Reseparation
children.top_down_role: Renewed separation prompted by the resolved relaxation state.

assumptions_latex: The preceding resolve phase returned an optimal point \(\bar x^k\) for relaxation \(P^k\).
Each accepted inequality is valid for the mixed-integer feasible set \(X\subseteq P^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The loop preserves \(X\subseteq P^{k+1}\subseteq P^k\) and terminates under its explicit stopping rule.

notation.meaning: relaxation and its optimal point at round k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated separation after each successful relaxation reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After obtaining \(\bar x^k\), invoke the eligible separators on \((P^k,\bar x^k)\), validate and filter their candidates, and form \(C_k^{\mathrm{acc}}\). If \(C_k^{\mathrm{acc}}\ne\varnothing\), set \(P^{k+1}=P^k\cap\bigcap_{c\in C_k^{\mathrm{acc}}}c\), resolve, and repeat at the new optimum. Stop when no cut passes the acceptance rules, a separation-round or resource limit is reached, the resolve proves infeasibility or unboundedness, or the resolve is unresolved. Return the last certified relaxation state together with the stopping reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each successful resolve, separate the new optimum again until no cut is accepted or a declared status or budget stops the loop.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolve-Triggered Reseparation

children.title: Pricing-First Coordination
children.top_down_role: Regimes where pricing precedes separation.

assumptions_latex: The restricted relaxation contains a finite active column set \(J^k\) and a finite active cut set \(R^k\).
Pricing can certify that no omitted column has improving reduced cost within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separation begins only at a pricing-stable solution for \(R^k\), namely after \(r_j^k\ge-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{price}}\) for every admissible omitted column \(j\).

notation.meaning: active columns and active cuts at iteration k
reduced cost of omitted column j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic coordination in which column pricing reaches tolerance before cut separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the restricted relaxation with \((J^0,R^0)\). At outer iteration \(k\), solve the restricted relaxation and repeatedly call pricing; add every accepted column with \(r_j^k< -\varepsilon_{\mathrm{price}}\), then re-solve, until pricing certifies \(r_j^k\ge-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{price}}\) for all admissible omitted columns. Only then call separation at the resulting solution. If cuts are accepted, add them to \(R^k\), retain the current columns, increment \(k\), and return to pricing. Stop when both pricing and separation certify no accepted addition, or when a declared resource or numerical limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaust improving column pricing before separating; after any accepted cuts, return to pricing and stop only when both oracles are inactive.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-First Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pricing-first policy is plausible, but no source supports its exact sequencing, certification semantics, or reduced-cost convention. Those choices materially determine the algorithm.

children.title: Separation-First Coordination
children.top_down_role: Regimes where separation precedes pricing.

assumptions_latex: The restricted relaxation has active columns \(J^k\), active cuts \(R^k\), and a solved point \(\bar x^k\).
Separation returns inequalities valid for the full feasible set represented by all admissible columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing begins only after separation is stable for the current restricted relaxation and point.

notation.meaning: active columns and cuts at iteration k
accepted cuts in a separation round

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic coordination in which separation reaches tolerance before column pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((J^0,R^0)\) and solve the restricted relaxation. At outer iteration \(k\), repeatedly separate \(\bar x^k\); when \(C_k^{\mathrm{acc}}\ne\varnothing\), add those cuts to \(R^k\), re-solve over \(J^k\), and separate again. Once no cut is accepted, invoke pricing. Add accepted improving columns, re-solve, increment \(k\), and return immediately to separation. Stop when separation accepts no cut and pricing certifies no improving omitted column, or when a declared resource or numerical limit is reached. Cuts whose validity depends on the current column restriction are inadmissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaust valid cut separation before pricing; after adding columns, return to separation and require cuts to remain valid for future columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation-First Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the separation-first ordering or the stated validity requirement under future column generation. A source on combined column-and-cut generation is needed to validate these material conditions.

children.title: Alternating Price-Separate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interleaved execution of pricing and separation phases.

assumptions_latex: Pricing and separation operate on a common solved relaxation state \(z^k\).
Each oracle has a finite per-call budget and returns accepted additions or a certified inactive status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted modification is followed by a resolve, and termination requires both oracles to be inactive at compatible solved states.

notation.meaning: solved relaxation state at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair alternation between bounded pricing and separation episodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an infinite fair schedule \((o_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(o_k\in\{\mathcal P,\mathcal S\}\), meaning that neither oracle is omitted indefinitely while it remains eligible. At solved state \(z^k\), run \(o_k\) within its budget, validate its output, insert accepted columns or cuts, and resolve before the next oracle call. If an oracle returns no accepted object, record its inactive status at \(z^k\) and continue with the other oracle. Stop only when both oracles are inactive without an intervening relaxation modification, or when a declared global limit or unresolved solver status occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate bounded pricing and separation calls fairly, resolving after each modification and stopping only after both are inactive on compatible states.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Price-Separate Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fair alternating schedule and compatible-state termination rule are substantive coordination choices with no cited support. Their correctness cannot be established from the supplied inventory.

children.title: Shared Resource Arbitration
children.top_down_role: Allocation of common computational resources between pricing and separation.

assumptions_latex: Pricing and separation share a finite resource budget \(B>0\) for the current coordination episode.
Each eligible task reports consumed resource and a comparable priority score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Total allocation satisfies \(\sum_t b_t\le B\), while mandatory minimum shares prevent starvation of continuously eligible task classes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget arbitration between pricing and separation tasks; the resource unit is solver-configured.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the eligible pricing and separation tasks. Reserve configured minimum shares for every continuously eligible task class, then repeatedly select a task maximizing \(q_t\) among tasks whose next quantum fits the remaining budget. Execute one resource quantum, update its measured consumption, marginal-benefit estimate, and \(q_t\), and return any accepted columns or cuts for validation. Enforce \(b_t\ge0\) and \(\sum_{t\in T}b_t\le B\). Stop when \(B\) is exhausted, no task is eligible, or all tasks report inactivity. The output includes allocations, accepted objects, and the arbitration stopping reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate a finite shared budget by updated task priorities, enforce minimum shares against starvation, and report allocations, accepted objects, and the stopping reason.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared Resource Arbitration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The arbitration algorithm lacks a source and leaves the common resource unit, priority normalization, quantum size, and feasibility of mandatory minimum shares unspecified. These omissions materially affect the claimed budget and starvation properties.

children.title: Pre-Branch Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation performed before committing to a branch.

assumptions_latex: \(P_v\) is the solved relaxation at an open branch-and-bound node \(v\), with optimum \(\bar x_v\).
Every accepted cut is valid for the node's integer-feasible set \(X_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching is deferred until separation stops, and the resulting relaxation \(P_v^+\) satisfies \(X_v\subseteq P_v^+\subseteq P_v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation rounds completed before selecting a branching disjunction at an open node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), solve \(P_v\) and perform cut-resolve rounds at the resulting optima. If a round accepts cuts, strengthen and re-solve before considering a branch. Stop pre-branch separation when no cut is accepted, a configured round or resource limit is reached, or the node is fathomed. If the final point is integer-feasible, process it as an incumbent candidate; otherwise select a branching disjunction from the final certified relaxation state and create children. Cuts inserted before branching must be valid for \(X_v\), so they may be inherited by every child of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finish configured cut-resolve rounds before choosing a branch, then branch from the final certified relaxation state unless the node is fathomed.
knowledge_statements.title: Pre-Branch Separation

children.title: Post-Branch Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation performed after child-node creation or branch commitment.

assumptions_latex: A child node \(w\) is formed by adding branch constraints \(D_w\) to its parent's relaxation.
Inherited cuts are valid for the parent integer-feasible set and therefore for the child set \(X_w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Post-branch separation produces \(X_w\subseteq P_w^+\subseteq P_w\) using the child-specific solved state.

notation.meaning: child relaxation before and after separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation performed after applying and solving a child node's branch constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each created child \(w\), form \(P_w=P_v^+\cap D_w\), propagate the branch bounds, and solve \(P_w\). If the child remains open, invoke separators eligible at its depth and state, validate returned cuts for \(X_w\), insert the accepted batch, and resolve according to the configured cut-resolve loop. Child-local cuts may exploit \(D_w\) but must not be exported outside the subtree unless independently certified for the destination. Return the strengthened relaxation \(P_w^+\), its certified solve status, and the scope attached to every retained cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply and solve child branch constraints, then run eligible separation; keep branch-dependent cuts within the subtree unless broader validity is independently certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Post-Branch Separation

children.title: Branch-Decision Feedback
children.top_down_role: Influence of branching choices on subsequent separator scheduling and scope.

assumptions_latex: A branching disjunction partitions the current node set into child domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_q\).
Separator eligibility and cut validity scope may depend on bounds, depth, and branch metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each child receives a separation context consistent with its domain, and no cut is reused outside its certified validity scope.

notation.meaning: child domains induced by the branch
certified validity scope of cut c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of branch outcomes into child separator state and cut-scope decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After selecting child domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_q\), construct each separation context \(\sigma_i\) from the child's bounds, depth, branch variable or disjunction, inherited cut scopes, and available parent statistics. Recompute separator eligibility and invalidate cached separation results whose premises conflict with \(D_i\). A cut \(c\) may enter child \(i\) only when \(D_i\subseteq V(c)\); a cut derived using child-specific premises receives a scope no broader than that child subtree. Feed measured child outcomes back to scheduling statistics only after preserving their node and branch provenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate each branch into child-specific separator state, invalidate incompatible caches, enforce cut scopes, and retain provenance when updating scheduling statistics.
knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Decision Feedback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general branch-and-cut citation does not specifically support cache invalidation, child-context construction, scoped-cut transfer, or provenance-aware scheduling feedback. These solver-interface claims require a more specific source.

children.title: Presolve Mapping Coordination
children.top_down_role: Alignment of separation data with presolved model representations.

assumptions_latex: Presolve supplies a reconstruction map \(T:\mathbb{R}^{n'}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(T(P')\) representing the original-space relaxation.
A cut is generated in either reduced or original coordinates with a declared validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An inserted reduced-space cut \(\alpha^	op y\le\beta\) is equivalent on \(P'\) to its declared original-space inequality under \(x=T(y)\).

notation.meaning: reconstruction map from reduced to original variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency requirement for cuts crossing original and presolved coordinate systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve mapping is separation-compatible precisely when every transferred cut carries a checkable transformation certificate. For an original-space inequality \(a^	op x\le b\), its reduced-space image must satisfy \(a^	op T(y)\le b\) for all \(y\in P'\) and be represented as \(\alpha^	op y\leeta\) with identical values on \(P'\). Conversely, lifting a reduced-space cut requires validity of its original-space representative for every feasible \(x=T(y)\). Fixed variables, substitutions, aggregations, scaling, and eliminated rows must be included in the certificate; otherwise the cut remains confined to the coordinate system where validity was established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer a cut across presolve only with a certificate showing equivalence under reconstruction, including substitutions, fixed variables, aggregation, scaling, and eliminated rows.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Mapping Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed presolve certificate, and the reconstruction map is not assumed affine even though a linear reduced-space image is asserted. The statement also contains the malformed command \leeta and conflicts with the conclusion's beta notation. Source-backed treatment of substitutions, aggregation, and noninvertible presolve transformations is required.

children.title: Propagation-Triggered Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation initiated after propagation changes the relaxation context.

assumptions_latex: The current node relaxation is \(R\), with propagation domain \(D\).
Propagation produces a strictly tighter domain \(D'\subsetneq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separation is invoked only when the trigger predicate is true, and every accepted inequality is valid for the updated feasible set \(F\cap D'\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-interface rule for invoking separation after domain propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a relaxation \(R\), domain \(D\), and propagation operator \(P\). Compute \(D'=P(R,D)\). If \(D'=\varnothing\), return infeasible. Otherwise invoke separation precisely when \(D'\subsetneq D\) and a prescribed trigger \(\tau(R,D,D')=1\), such as sufficient bound change or newly fixed variables. Each separator receives \((R,D')\) and may return inequalities \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\) satisfying \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\) for every \(x\in F\cap D'\). Add accepted inequalities to the relaxation and return the updated relaxation; if the trigger is false, return \(R\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After propagation tightens the node domain, eligible separators run on the tightened domain and may add cuts valid there; infeasibility terminates the node.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Triggered Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the propagation trigger, separator inputs, and cut-acceptance policy are implementation-specific and have no cited source.

children.title: Separation-Triggered Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation initiated after cut insertion changes inference opportunities.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation is \(R\), with domain \(D\).
Accepted cuts are valid for every feasible point in their declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation after row insertion preserves all feasible points in the cut scope and either tightens the domain, detects infeasibility, or reaches a fixed point.

notation.meaning: current relaxation and accepted cut set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-interface rule for rerunning propagation after cut insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \((R,D)\) and a set \(C\) of newly accepted inequalities. Form \(R'=R\cap\{x:a^Tx\le b\text{ for every }(a,b)\in C\}\). Apply propagation iteratively by \(D^{k+1}=P(R',D^k)\), starting with \(D^0=D\), until \(D^{k+1}=D^k\), an infeasible domain is obtained, or a prescribed propagation limit is reached. Output the final domain and infeasibility status. Any subsequent separation call must use that final domain and the relaxation containing \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once cuts enter the relaxation, propagation is rerun to a fixed point or limit, possibly tightening bounds or proving the node infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Triggered Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits, but no source supports the prescribed iteration policy. The assumptions also do not explicitly require the propagation operator to preserve feasible points.

children.title: Phase-Ordering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Alternative orderings of presolve, propagation, and separation phases.

assumptions_latex: Each phase is monotone: presolve preserves feasibility, propagation only tightens domains, and separation adds valid inequalities.
The implementation specifies finite phase and round limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every regime maintains a relaxation containing the relevant feasible set; convergence means that no enabled phase produces a material change.

notation.meaning: relaxation and domain at round k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible orderings of presolve, propagation, and separation in a relaxation loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A phase-ordering regime selects an ordered schedule from \(Q\), \(P\), and \(S\). A sequential regime applies \(Q\) once and then repeats \(P\) followed by \(S\); an interleaved regime repeats \(P\), \(S\), and again \(P\) whenever cuts were accepted. At round \(k\), update \((R^{k+1},D^{k+1})\) according to the selected schedule. Stop on infeasibility, resource exhaustion, or when \(R^{k+1}=R^k\) and \(D^{k+1}=D^k\) up to prescribed tolerances. Output the final relaxation, domain, and termination status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A phase-ordering regime fixes how presolve, propagation, and separation alternate and stops at infeasibility, a resource limit, or joint stabilization.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Ordering Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The schedule description fits the phase-ordering leaf, but the listed regimes, triggering rules, stabilization criterion, and feasibility-preservation claim require authoritative support.

children.title: Cut Lifecycle Management System
children.top_down_role: Storage tiers, locality, reuse, activity tracking, and retirement of generated cuts.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Cuts and Cutpools; separation-storage and cut-pool FAQ

assumptions_latex: A separation round is executed at one search node against a fixed relaxation snapshot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The store contains pending candidates only for the current round and is cleared or transferred after round processing.

notation.meaning: candidate cuts generated in round r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transient candidate storage within one separation round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation snapshot \(R_r\), separation-round storage is a transient collection \(C_r\) of generated cut records. Each record contains an inequality \(a^Tx\le b\), its declared validity scope, origin, and selection metadata. Membership in \(C_r\) does not itself make the inequality an active relaxation row. At the end of round \(r\), every record is either rejected, inserted into an active row set, transferred to an eligible persistent cut pool, or discarded; the transient collection is then empty for the next round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation-round storage temporarily holds generated cut records until each is rejected, activated, transferred to persistent storage, or discarded.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Round Storage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits transient separation-round storage, but its mandatory record fields and exhaustive end-of-round disposition policy are solver-specific and uncited.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation is represented by a finite system of active constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every active row participates in the current relaxation, while removal from the active set changes storage status rather than mathematical validity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts currently enforced as rows of the node relaxation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the base relaxation and let \(A\) be a finite set of accepted inequalities. The active relaxation rows are precisely the members of \(A\) currently enforced in \[R(A)=R_0\cap\bigcap_{(a,b)\in A}\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^Tx\le b\}.\] A valid cut may be inactive without losing validity; activation is the operational decision to include its inequality in \(R(A)\). Deactivation removes it from \(A\) and hence from the represented relaxation until possible reactivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active relaxation rows are accepted cuts currently enforced in the relaxation; inactive valid cuts may remain stored for later reactivation.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Relaxation Rows

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical representation is coherent, but the cited chapter on cuts does not directly support activation, deactivation, storage, or reactivation semantics.

assumptions_latex: Every stored inequality is valid for the global feasible set \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any pooled inequality may be considered at any search node, subject to selection rules, without excluding a point of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent repository restricted to globally valid cuts.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a mixed-integer feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a global cut pool \(G\) is a persistent collection of cut records \((a,b,m)\) satisfying \(a^Tx\le b\) for every \(x\in F\), where \(m\) denotes management metadata. Storage in \(G\) does not imply that the cut is active. At any search node, a selection rule may move a member of \(G\) into the active relaxation, and later return or retire it, without changing its global validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global cut pool persistently stores globally valid but not necessarily active cuts that may be selected at any search node.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut Pools

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global-validity component is standard, but the cited valid-cuts section does not establish the persistent pool, node-wide selection, return, or retirement semantics.

children.title: Local Cut Stores
children.top_down_role: Repositories for cuts whose validity is restricted to a local search region.

assumptions_latex: A search node \(v\) has domain \(D_v\) and feasible subset \(F_v=F\cap D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A record belongs to the local store at \(v\) only if its validity scope includes \(F_v\), and it cannot be used outside that scope.

notation.meaning: local cut store at node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent storage whose cuts have an explicitly restricted search scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be a search node with feasible subset \(F_v=F\cap D_v\). A local cut store \(L_v\) is a collection of inactive cut records, each carrying a validity region \(V_c\) such that \(F_v\subseteq V_c\) and \(a_c^Tx\le b_c\) for all \(x\in F\cap V_c\). A cut from \(L_v\) may be activated only at a node \(w\) whose feasible subset satisfies \(F_w\subseteq V_c\). The store therefore retains both the inequality and the scope needed to check eligibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local cut store retains inactive cuts with scope metadata and permits activation only at nodes whose feasible sets lie within that scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Cut Stores

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but the persistence, inactivity, scope metadata, and cross-node eligibility rules have no cited support.

children.title: Node Cut Stores
children.top_down_role: Repositories attached to individual search-tree nodes.

assumptions_latex: Each search node \(v\) defines a feasible subset \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node store is eligible at \(v\); eligibility at another node requires a separate scope-containment check.

notation.meaning: cut store owned by node v
validity region recorded for cut c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-owned specialization of a local cut store.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search node \(v\), a node cut store \(N_v\) is a local cut store owned by \(v\). Every record \(c\in N_v\) consists of an inequality \(a_c^Tx\le b_c\), metadata, and a validity region \(V_c\) satisfying \(F_v\subseteq V_c\) and \(a_c^Tx\le b_c\) for all \(x\in F\cap V_c\). Ownership identifies lifecycle and retrieval responsibility; it does not enlarge validity. Use at a node \(w\ne v\) is permitted only after verifying \(F_w\subseteq V_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node cut store is owned by one search node and stores cuts valid there; reuse elsewhere requires explicit scope verification.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Cut Stores

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the node-ownership and reuse policy. Moreover, the global feasible set F appears in the statement without being introduced in this record's assumptions or notation.

children.title: Subtree Cut Transfer
children.top_down_role: Movement and inheritance of stored cuts within valid subtrees.

assumptions_latex: A cut \(c\) has recorded validity region \(V_c\).
A descendant node \(w\) has feasible subset \(F_w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transfer to \(w\) is validity-preserving exactly when \(F_w\subseteq V_c\); transfer alone does not activate the cut.

notation.meaning: recorded validity region of cut c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for moving stored cuts between nodes of one subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) be stored at node \(v\), with validity region \(V_c\) and inequality \(a_c^Tx\le b_c\) valid on \(F\cap V_c\). Transfer of \(c\) to a descendant node \(w\) is admissible if and only if the implementation verifies \(F_w\subseteq V_c\). The transferred record must retain \(V_c\) and all dependencies used to establish it. If containment fails or cannot be verified, \(c\) must not enter the store or active relaxation of \(w\). Transfer changes ownership or availability, not activation status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut may move to a descendant store only when the descendant feasible set lies in its recorded validity region and all dependencies remain recorded.
knowledge_statements.title: Subtree Cut Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The containment test is sufficient for using validity established on V_c, but it is not mathematically necessary for the inequality to be valid at the descendant. The asserted if-and-only-if transfer rule and dependency policy require a source.

assumptions_latex: The original mixed-integer feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding a globally valid cut to any relaxation containing \(F\) cannot remove a feasible point of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity with respect to the original feasible set, independent of search-node restrictions.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set of the original mixed-integer problem. An inequality \(a^Tx\le b\) is a globally valid cut for \(F\) if \(a^Tx\le b\) for every \(x\in F\). Consequently, for every relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(F\subseteq R\), one has \[F\subseteq R\cap\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^Tx\le b\}.\] Global validity concerns preservation of all original feasible points and is independent of whether the inequality is currently active or stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally valid cut is satisfied by every original feasible point, so it may be added at any search node without excluding feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Globally Valid Cuts

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Valid cuts and support-function construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globally valid linear inequalities for the feasible set of the extended MINLP formulation; the relaxation strengthened by a cut need not be the auxiliary set used to bound the support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set. A valid cut is a redundant constraint that excludes no point of \(S\). If \(\widetilde S\supseteq S\), \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\bar a\geq\sigma_{\widetilde S}(a)=\max\{a^Tx:x\in\widetilde S\}\), then \(a^Tx\leq\bar a\) is valid for \(S\). Adding a valid cut strengthens a polyhedral or nonlinear relaxation; the strengthening is strict if the cut excludes all solution points of that relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut excludes no feasible point of the original MINLP. An upper bound on the support function of any set containing the feasible set yields a globally valid linear inequality. A valid cut strengthens a relaxation, strictly so when it excludes all solution points of that relaxation.
assumptions_latex: S\subseteq\mathbb R^n
\widetilde S\supseteq S
a\in\mathbb R^n
\bar a\geq\sigma_{\widetilde S}(a)=\max\{a^Tx:x\in\widetilde S\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a^Tx\leq\bar a\quad\forall x\in S

source_evidence.locator: Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction / 7.1. Valid cuts / Definition 7.1-extra-1

source_refs.locator: Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction / 7.1. Valid cuts / Definition 7.1-extra-1

knowledge_statements.title: Valid cuts and support-function construction

source_witnesses.locator: Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction / 7.1. Valid cuts / Definition 7.1-extra-1

assumptions_latex: A search node \(v\) restricts the original feasible set \(F\) to \(F_v=F\cap D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality can safely strengthen node \(v\) and any node \(w\) with \(F_w\subseteq F_v\), but need not be valid globally.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity restricted to one node domain and its contained descendants.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the original feasible set and let node \(v\) impose domain restriction \(D_v\), so \(F_v=F\cap D_v\). An inequality \(a^Tx\le b\) is locally valid at \(v\) if \(a^Tx\le b\) for every \(x\in F_v\). It is eligible at any node \(w\) satisfying \(F_w\subseteq F_v\). Local validity does not imply global validity: there may exist \(x\in F\setminus F_v\) with \(a^Tx>b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally valid cut holds for every feasible point under one node's restrictions and may be inherited only by nodes whose feasible sets are contained there.
knowledge_statements.title: Locally Valid Cuts

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent, but the cited general valid-cuts section does not directly establish node-local validity or the stated feasible-set containment rule for inheritance.

children.title: Conditional Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity restricted by explicit contextual conditions.

assumptions_latex: A cut inequality is derived under a predicate \(q(x)\) or an equivalent set of dependencies.
The original feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is usable exactly on search regions contained in \(V_q\); invalidation occurs when the condition or any required dependency ceases to hold.

notation.meaning: validity region defined by condition q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut validity guarded by an explicit predicate and its retained dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\) define \(V_q=\{x:q(x)=\mathrm{true}\}\). An inequality \(a^Tx\le b\) has conditional validity under \(q\) precisely when \[a^Tx\le b\quad\text{for every }x\in F\cap V_q.\] At a search node with feasible subset \(F_v\), the cut is eligible if \(F_v\subseteq V_q\) and every recorded dependency supporting \(q\) remains valid. If either requirement fails or cannot be verified, the cut must be inactive and unavailable for separation enforcement at that node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditionally valid cut may be enforced only where its guard holds throughout the node feasible set and every supporting dependency remains valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Cut Validity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The guarded-validity formula is coherent and the condition kind fits the leaf, but the eligibility, dependency-retention, and mandatory invalidation policy are uncited.

children.title: Dependency-Scoped Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity tied to recorded model, inference, or search dependencies.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Scoped Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of a cut whose derivation depends on a recorded solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(D)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set determined by dependency state \(D\), and let \(c=(a,\beta)\) denote the inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\). Given a dependency predicate \(P_c(D)\), the cut \(c\) is dependency-scoped valid at \(D\) precisely when \(P_c(D)\) holds and \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in F(D)\). Its validity scope is \(\mathcal D_c=\{D:P_c(D)\land F(D)\subseteq\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\}\). The cut may be imposed only while the current state belongs to \(\mathcal D_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dependency-scoped cut is usable exactly in states satisfying its recorded dependency predicate and where it remains valid for every feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) determines a well-defined feasible set \(F(D)\).
The cut stores a checkable dependency predicate \(P_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\text{ is usable at }D\iff D\in\mathcal D_c\).

notation.meaning: dependency state used to derive or validate the cut

children.title: Dependency Invalidation
children.top_down_role: Loss of cut eligibility after supporting dependencies cease to hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency Invalidation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational invalidation condition for dependency-scoped cuts after solver-state changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a stored cut \(c\) have validity scope \(\mathcal D_c\), and suppose the solver changes from state \(D\in\mathcal D_c\) to state \(D'\). The cut is invalidated exactly when \(D'\notin\mathcal D_c\). Upon invalidation it must be removed from the active relaxation before that relaxation is solved; it may remain archived with status inactive. Revalidation requires an explicit check that \(D''\in\mathcal D_c\) for the then-current state \(D''\); prior validity at \(D\) alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state change invalidates a scoped cut when the new state leaves its validity scope; the cut must then leave the active relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The cut's validity scope \(\mathcal D_c\) is recorded and testable.
The state transition is observed before the next relaxation solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D'\notin\mathcal D_c\implies c\text{ is inactive at }D'\).

notation.meaning: solver states before and after a transition
recorded validity scope of cut c

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Eligibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admission predicate for retaining a valid generated cut in a reusable pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a generated inequality \(c=(a,\beta)\), define \(E(c)=V(c)\land N(c)\land Q(c)\land S(c)\), where \(V(c)\) asserts validity on its declared scope, \(N(c)\) asserts that no equivalent cut is already stored, \(Q(c)\) asserts finite coefficients and satisfaction of numerical tolerances, and \(S(c)\) asserts compliance with configured size and support limits. The cut is eligible for pool admission if and only if \(E(c)\) holds. Eligibility permits storage but does not require immediate activation in the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is pool-eligible exactly when it is scoped-valid, nonduplicate, numerically acceptable, and within configured representation limits.
assumptions_latex: Equivalence, numerical acceptance, and size tests are deterministic under fixed tolerances.
The cut carries its validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\text{ is pool-eligible}\iff E(c)\).

notation.meaning: candidate inequality a-transpose x at most beta

knowledge_statements.title: Expensive-Cut Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention rule balancing future separation value against storage and evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each eligible cut \(c\), let \(B(c)\geq0\) estimate its expected future relaxation benefit and let \(K(c)>0\) measure storage, evaluation, and numerical-processing cost. Given a retention threshold \(\rho\geq0\), an expensive cut with \(K(c)>K_{\max}\) is retained only if \(B(c)/K(c)\geq\rho\), unless it is protected by correctness-relevant scope metadata or an explicit mandatory-retention flag. Thus computational expense alone neither forces deletion nor justifies retention; the configured benefit-cost test controls optional retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expensive cut is optionally retained only when its estimated future benefit justifies its cost, except when an explicit protection rule applies.
assumptions_latex: \(B(c)\) and \(K(c)\) are evaluated on a common retention horizon.
Protected cuts are identified independently of the benefit-cost score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(c)>K_{\max}\land\neg\operatorname{protected}(c)\implies[\operatorname{retain}(c)\iff B(c)/K(c)\geq\rho]\).

notation.meaning: estimated future benefit of retaining cut c
estimated computational and memory cost of cut c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The specific benefit-cost ratio rule is an implementation policy not established by the cited reference as presented. Moreover, K_{\max} is not introduced with a domain, and recorded scope metadata alone does not make retention correctness-required. A source supporting this policy and a precise definition of protected cuts are needed.

assumptions_latex: Every scanned cut has a testable current validity scope.
The ranking rule and tie breaking are fixed.
A deterministic set-admissibility predicate \(\mathsf M\) is specified, with \(\mathsf M(\varnothing)=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\subseteq P,\quad |R|\leq k,\quad \mathsf M(R)=1,\quad c_i\in R\implies v_i>\varepsilon.\)

notation.meaning: violation of cut i at the current LP solution
configured predicate asserting that a selected set of cuts is jointly admissible

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scanning inactive pooled cuts for violation at a current relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an LP solution \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), an inactive cut pool \(P\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), an activation budget \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), and a configured set-admissibility predicate \(\mathsf M\). For each currently scope-valid cut \(c_i:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\) in \(P\), compute \(v_i=a_i^\top\bar x-\beta_i\) and omit cuts with \(v_i\leq\varepsilon\). Rank the remaining cuts by a fixed score, such as normalized violation \(v_i/\max\{1,\lVert a_i\rVert\}\). Starting with \(R=\varnothing\), scan the ranked cuts and add \(c_i\) to \(R\) exactly when \(\mathsf M(R\cup\{c_i\})=1\), stopping when \(|R|=k\) or the ranked list is exhausted. Return \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reseparation scans currently valid inactive cuts, filters by violation, ranks the survivors, and selects at most the activation budget while enforcing a specified joint-admissibility predicate.
knowledge_statements.title: Pool Reseparation
Cut Reactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe transfer of a selected pooled cut back into the active relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a current solver state \(D\), relaxation solution \(\bar x\), an inactive cut \(c:a^\top x\leq\beta\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). First verify \(D\in\mathcal D_c\); otherwise leave \(c\) inactive. Next recompute its coefficients if the stored representation requires state-dependent reconstruction, verify numerical acceptability, and compute \(v=a^\top\bar x-\beta\). If \(v>\varepsilon\) and no equivalent active row exists, insert \(c\) into the relaxation and mark it active; otherwise retain it inactive. Output the updated relaxation and cut status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pooled cut is reactivated only after scope, representation, numerical, violation, and duplicate checks succeed.
assumptions_latex: The current validity scope \(\mathcal D_c\) is testable.
Active-row equivalence is decidable under fixed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{reactivate}(c)\implies D\in\mathcal D_c\land v>\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Based Aging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Age update driven by whether a cut is violated or nearly active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each stored cut \(c_i:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\), maintain an integer age \(g_i\geq0\). At inspection time \(t\), compute slack \(s_i^t=\beta_i-a_i^\top x^t\) at the current relaxation solution and choose tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Update \(g_i\leftarrow0\) when \(s_i^t\leq\varepsilon\), and update \(g_i\leftarrow g_i+1\) when \(s_i^t>\varepsilon\). The resulting age counts consecutive inspections at which the cut was neither violated nor within the prescribed activity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut's age resets when violated or nearly active and otherwise increments, counting consecutive inspections without relevance.
assumptions_latex: Each inspection uses a specified relaxation solution \(x^t\).
The activity tolerance \(\varepsilon\) remains fixed during an update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i^{t+1}=0\text{ if }s_i^t\leq\varepsilon;\quad g_i^{t+1}=g_i^t+1\text{ otherwise}.\)

notation.meaning: slack of cut i at inspection t

children.title: Activity-Based Retention
children.top_down_role: Retention decisions based on recent cut activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Based Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention signal based on recent violation or near-tightness at relaxation solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cut \(c_i:a_i^\top x\leq\beta_i\), inspection solutions \(x^{t-h+1},\ldots,x^t\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and window length \(h\geq1\), define \(A_i^t=1\) exactly when \(\beta_i-a_i^\top x^j\leq\varepsilon\) for at least one \(j\in\{t-h+1,\ldots,t\}\). An otherwise deletable cut satisfies the activity-based retention condition at time \(t\) if and only if \(A_i^t=1\). This is a retention signal, not a statement that the cut is globally indispensable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut receives the activity retention signal when it was violated or nearly tight at least once within the configured recent window.
assumptions_latex: The last \(h\) inspection solutions are available.
Slack is evaluated using a fixed tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_i^t=1\iff\min_{t-h+1\leq j\leq t}(\beta_i-a_i^\top x^j)\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Basis-Status Retention
children.top_down_role: Retention decisions based on basis participation or status.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Status Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention signal for a cut row participating materially in a current LP basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an LP relaxation in standard form with a cut row \(c_i\) and associated slack variable \(z_i\geq0\). Let \(B_i=1\) when \(z_i\) is nonbasic at its lower bound and the row is tight within feasibility tolerance, or when implementation-specific basis metadata marks the row as structurally participating in the current basis; otherwise let \(B_i=0\). An otherwise deletable cut satisfies the basis-status retention condition exactly when \(B_i=1\). Any cut removed despite this signal requires basis repair or refactorization before the next simplex solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut receives the basis-status retention signal when its row materially participates in the current simplex basis representation.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation exposes consistent row and slack basis statuses.
Tightness is evaluated with the solver's feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{basisRetain}(c_i)\iff B_i=1\).

notation.meaning: slack variable associated with cut row i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disjunction defining B_i mixes the precise status of a nonbasic slack with an undefined implementation-specific notion of structural participation. The claim about required basis repair or refactorization is also solver-dependent. A solver or algorithm reference defining these statuses and consequences is needed before the mathematical condition can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Combined Retention Signals
children.top_down_role: Joint use of activity and basis evidence in retention decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Retention Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean or weighted aggregation of activity, basis, protection, and value signals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_i,B_i,P_i\in\{0,1\}\) denote activity, basis-status, and mandatory-protection signals for cut \(c_i\), and let \(q_i\in[0,1]\) be a normalized value score. A Boolean combined policy is \(R_i=P_i\lor A_i\lor B_i\). More generally, for nonnegative weights \(w_A,w_B,w_q\) and threshold \(\tau\), an unprotected cut is retained when \(w_AA_i+w_BB_i+w_qq_i\geq\tau\), while \(P_i=1\) forces retention. The aggregation rule and parameters must be fixed before candidates are compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retention signals may be combined by a fixed Boolean rule or weighted score, with mandatory protection overriding optional deletion.
assumptions_latex: All component signals refer to the same cut and inspection epoch.
Scores are normalized before weighted aggregation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_i=P_i\lor[\,w_AA_i+w_BB_i+w_qq_i\geq\tau\,]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Age-Limit Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retirement of stale cuts after a configurable number of inactive inspections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a stored cut \(c_i\), its age \(g_i\), age limit \(G_i\geq1\), and retention indicator \(R_i\). After updating \(g_i\) at an inspection epoch, delete or archive \(c_i\) when \(g_i\geq G_i\) and \(R_i=0\). If \(R_i=1\), keep the cut and preserve or reset its age according to the declared retention policy. Before physical deletion, remove any active row safely and retain metadata required for audit or regeneration. Output the updated active set and pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut reaching its age limit is retired only when no retention signal protects it, with active-row removal handled safely.
assumptions_latex: Aging and retention are evaluated at the same inspection epoch.
The age limit \(G_i\) is fixed for the cut's policy class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i\geq G_i\land R_i=0\implies\operatorname{retire}(c_i)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Pressure Retirement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget-driven cut retirement using protected status and a deterministic priority score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a cut pool \(P\), memory usage \(M(P)\), budget \(M_{\max}\), protection indicators \(R_i\), and deletion priorities \(d_i\). If \(M(P)\leq M_{\max}\), return \(P\). Otherwise order unprotected cuts \(c_i\) with \(R_i=0\) by decreasing \(d_i\), where larger values indicate weaker expected utility per stored byte, and retire them sequentially until \(M(P)\leq M_{\max}\) or no unprotected cut remains. Never retire a cut whose current validity is required for correctness; report budget infeasibility if protected cuts alone exceed the budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under memory pressure, retire unprotected cuts in deterministic low-utility order until the budget is met, or report that protected cuts exceed it.
assumptions_latex: Memory usage is measurable after each retirement.
Deletion priorities and tie breaking are fixed.
Correctness-required cuts are included among protected cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(P_{\mathrm{out}})\leq M_{\max}\) unless \(M(\{c_i:R_i=1\})>M_{\max}\).

children.title: Cut-Family Provenance
children.top_down_role: Metadata identifying the structural family of a generated cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Family Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata identifying the mathematical family from which a managed cut originates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a cut repository and \(\mathcal F\) a controlled set of cut-family identifiers. Cut-family provenance is a persistent map \(p_F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal F\times\mathcal P\), where \(p_F(c)=(F,\theta)\) records the family \(F\) and family-specific parameters \(\theta\) used to derive cut \(c\). Scaling, canonicalization, or repository migration may change the stored inequality but must not change \(p_F(c)\); a mathematically new derivation receives a new provenance record.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each cut retains an immutable family identifier and family-specific derivation parameters, independent of normalization or repository migration.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) contains uniquely identified managed cuts.
\(\mathcal F\) is a controlled family vocabulary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_F(c)=(F,\theta)\) persistently attributes every \(c\in\mathcal C\) to one cut family and its parameters.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but immutability, the parameter schema, and behavior under migration or new derivations are repository-interface conventions with no cited support.

children.title: Generator Provenance
children.top_down_role: Metadata identifying the separator or generating component responsible for a cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Generator Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invocation-level identity of the software or mathematical generator that emitted a cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a managed cut \(c\), generator provenance is a tuple \(p_G(c)=(g,v,r,i)\), where \(g\) identifies the generating procedure, \(v\) its implementation or rule version, \(r\) the model or relaxation revision, and \(i\) the invocation identifier. The tuple is immutable after insertion. Two cuts may share \((g,v,r)\) while having different invocation identifiers, and identical inequalities generated by distinct invocations retain distinct generator-provenance records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut records its generator, version, model revision, and invocation, preserving distinct derivations even when inequalities coincide.
assumptions_latex: Every generator invocation has a stable identifier.
Model or relaxation revisions are distinguishable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_G(c)=(g,v,r,i)\) uniquely identifies the generating context of \(c\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches generator provenance, but the four-field schema, immutability rule, and treatment of coincident inequalities are unsupported design choices.

children.title: Cross-Generator Attribution
children.top_down_role: Attribution for cuts derived, strengthened, or rediscovered across multiple generators.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Generator Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued attribution for cuts jointly derived, rediscovered, or strengthened by multiple generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be the set of registered generators. Cross-generator attribution of a cut \(c\) is a finite nonempty set \(A(c)\subseteq G\times I\times[0,1]\) of generator, invocation, and contribution-weight triples. If weights express apportioned credit, they satisfy \(\sum_{(g,i,w)\in A(c)}w=1\); otherwise each weight is omitted rather than inferred. Adding an independent rediscovery appends an attribution entry and does not overwrite the cut's original generator provenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint derivations and rediscoveries are recorded as multiple generator-invocation attributions, with normalized weights only when contribution shares are known.
assumptions_latex: Generator and invocation identifiers are stable.
Attribution weights are used only when contribution shares are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(c)\) preserves every declared generator contribution without replacing original provenance.

notation.meaning: cross-generator attribution set of cut c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf and definition role align, but no source supports the weighted attribution convention. Moreover, A(c) is defined as triples containing weights while the statement later permits weights to be omitted, so the mathematical schema is not yet reliable.

children.title: Locality Provenance
children.top_down_role: Metadata recording the search region where a cut is valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Locality Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provenance specifying the search region on which a cut is certified valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the original feasible set and let \(R_s\) denote the region associated with search scope \(s\). Locality provenance of a cut \(c=(a,\beta)\) is a pair \(p_L(c)=(s,R_s)\) satisfying \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in X\cap R_s\). The cut is global when \(R_s\) is the entire ambient domain; otherwise it may be activated only in scope \(s\) or a descendant scope whose region is contained in \(R_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut records the search region where it is valid and may be activated only within that region or a contained descendant region.
assumptions_latex: Each search scope \(s\) determines a region \(R_s\).
The cut has the form \(a^\top x\leq\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_L(c)=(s,R_s)\) certifies validity on \(X\cap R_s\) and restricts activation accordingly.

notation.meaning: region represented by search scope s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local-validity formula is plausible and fits the leaf, but the global-domain convention and descendant-scope activation rule require an authoritative solver or branch-and-cut interface source.

children.title: Dependency Provenance
children.top_down_role: Metadata recording the conditions or inferences supporting cut validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed provenance recording objects and assumptions used to derive a managed cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\) be the set of versioned derivation objects, including cuts, bounds, rows, incumbents, and relaxation states. Dependency provenance assigns each cut \(c\) a finite set \(D(c)\subseteq O\) and typed edges \(d\to c\) for all \(d\in D(c)\). Each edge records the version of \(d\) consumed by the derivation. The resulting derivation graph must be acyclic, so recursively expanding dependencies terminates at source model data or independently certified objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each cut records versioned derivation dependencies in an acyclic graph that can be traced back to source data or certified objects.
assumptions_latex: Every derivation object has a stable versioned identity.
Dependencies are recorded before the cut is admitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(c)\) yields a finite, version-specific, acyclic dependency trace for every cut \(c\).

notation.meaning: c was derived using object d

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits dependency provenance, but the enumerated dependency objects, mandatory versioning, graph acyclicity, and terminal-object requirements are uncited interface requirements rather than established consequences.

children.title: Scope-Dependency Traceability
children.top_down_role: Traceability between a cut's locality and its supporting dependencies.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope-Dependency Traceability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition linking a cut's activation scope to the scopes of its dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each local derivation object \(d\), let \(R(d)\) be its validity region, and let \(D(c)\) be the direct dependencies of cut \(c\). A scope-dependency trace is consistent when the activation region \(R(c)\) satisfies \(R(c)\subseteq\bigcap_{d\in D(c)}R(d)\). Recursively, every active use of \(c\) must trace to dependency versions whose validity regions contain the current search region. Global dependencies are represented by the entire ambient domain and impose no additional locality restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut may be active only where all dependency versions used in its derivation remain valid.
assumptions_latex: Every local cut or derivation object has a recorded validity region.
The dependency graph is acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(c)\subseteq\bigcap_{d\in D(c)}R(d)\), and the containment condition holds recursively along every dependency path.

notation.meaning: activation or validity region of cut c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the traceability leaf and its containment formula is coherent, but the chosen region semantics and recursive activation rule depend on unsupported locality and dependency conventions.

children.title: Canonical Cut Representation
children.top_down_role: Normalized representations used to establish cut identity.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Cut Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalization of a nontrivial linear inequality modulo positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent a nontrivial cut as \(a^\top x\leq\beta\), with \(a\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\). Its canonical representation under positive scaling is \(\kappa(a,\beta)=(a/\lVert a\rVert_2,\beta/\lVert a\rVert_2)\). For any two representations \((a,
\beta)\) and \((a',\beta')\), one has \(\kappa(a,\beta)=\kappa(a',\beta')\) if and only if \((a',\beta')=\lambda(a,\beta)\) for some \(\lambda>0\). Numerical implementations must apply a declared quantization rule only after this exact normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear cut is normalized by the coefficient norm, producing the same canonical pair exactly when two inequalities differ by positive scaling.
assumptions_latex: The cut is a nontrivial linear inequality with \(a\neq0\).
Equivalent representations differ only by positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(a,\beta)=\kappa(\lambda a,\lambda\beta)\) for every \(\lambda>0\), and equality characterizes positive-scale equivalence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and positive-scale normalization are mathematically precise, but no cited source establishes Euclidean normalization and post-normalization quantization as the intended canonical repository interface.

children.title: Cut Fingerprinting
children.top_down_role: Hash-based identifiers derived from canonical cut representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Fingerprinting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic digest construction from a canonical cut and identity-relevant metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\kappa(c)\) be the canonical representation of cut \(c\), let \(m(c)\) contain identity-relevant metadata such as sense and locality, and let \(E\) be an injective serialization on the admitted canonical data. Given a deterministic hash \(H\), the cut fingerprint is \(f(c)=H(E(\kappa(c),m(c)))\). Equal canonical data and metadata must produce equal fingerprints. Fingerprint equality is only a candidate-identity test unless \(H\) is injective on all serialized repository entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fingerprint hashes deterministic serialized canonical cut data and relevant metadata; matching hashes identify candidates, not guaranteed equality.
assumptions_latex: Canonicalization and serialization are deterministic.
Identity-relevant metadata fields are fixed by the repository schema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\kappa(c),m(c))=(\kappa(d),m(d))\) implies \(f(c)=f(d)\), but the converse requires collision resolution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes deterministic equality from hash equality, but the identity-relevant metadata, serialization requirements, and collision semantics lack authoritative support.

children.title: Fingerprint Collision Handling
children.top_down_role: Identity safeguards for distinct cuts sharing a candidate fingerprint.

knowledge_statements.title: Fingerprint Collision Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplicate resolution when distinct serialized cuts share a fingerprint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a candidate cut \(c\), its canonical serialization \(z=E(\kappa(c),m(c))\), and the fingerprint bucket \(B_{H(z)}\). Compare \(z\) with every stored serialization in that bucket using exact equality, or a declared equivalence predicate when quantization is part of the schema. If a match exists, merge only the permitted lifecycle metadata and return its existing cut identifier. Otherwise insert \((z,c)\) as a distinct bucket entry. Thus hash equality alone never authorizes deduplication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a hash match, compare canonical serialized data; merge only exact equivalents and otherwise retain a distinct colliding entry.
assumptions_latex: Each fingerprint indexes a bucket of stored serializations.
The repository defines an exact or explicitly quantized equivalence predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure merges \(c\) with \(d\) only when \(E(\kappa(c),m(c))=E(\kappa(d),m(d))\) under the declared predicate.

notation.meaning: bucket indexed by the candidate fingerprint

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the collision-handling leaf and exact bucket comparison is coherent, but the equivalence predicate and permitted metadata-merge policy are repository-specific rules with no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Audit Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auditable record certifying cut validity for a model revision and declared scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a cut \(c=(a,\beta)\), model revision \(r\) with feasible set \(X_r\), and declared scope region \(R_s\), a validity-audit certificate records \((c,r,s,V,t,q)\), where \(V\) identifies the verifier, \(t\) the audit event, and \(q\) its result. An accepted result must certify \(\sup\{a^\top x-
\beta:x\in X_r\cap R_s\}\leq0\) by a reproducible exact argument or independently checkable certificate. Any change to the cut, revision, or scope invalidates reuse without a recorded transfer justification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An audit binds a cut-validity check to its model revision, scope, verifier, event, and reproducible result.
assumptions_latex: The model revision determines \(X_r\).
The locality record determines \(R_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in X_r\cap R_s\).

notation.meaning: feasible set at model revision r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A certificate is an appropriate role for this leaf, but the tuple format, admissible verification methods, and transfer-justification rule are unsupported. The available inventory does not specifically address audit provenance.

children.title: Callback-Based Separation
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing interfaces for custom separators, optional user cuts, and dynamically enforced model constraints.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: MIP callbacks, user cuts, and lazy constraints

knowledge_statements.title: LP-Solution Separator Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Callback contract for separating the current LP-relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input the current LP-relaxation solution \(\bar x\), its relaxation revision \(r\), search scope \(s\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\). A separator callback returns a finite set \(C\) of cuts and an outcome status. Every returned \(c=(a,
\beta)\) must carry provenance and a validity scope containing its activation region; it is reported as separating only if \(a^\top\bar x-\beta>\varepsilon\). The callback returns normally without cuts when no qualifying cut is found and must distinguish this outcome from interruption or execution failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback receives the current LP solution and returns valid, scoped, provenance-bearing cuts whose violation exceeds tolerance, plus an explicit outcome.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is associated with the supplied LP-relaxation revision.
The callback receives the current search scope and violation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every separating \(c\in C\) satisfies \(a^\top\bar x-\beta>\varepsilon\) and is valid on its declared activation scope.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic callback contract fits the LP-solution leaf, but its inputs, status distinctions, provenance obligations, scope rule, and strict tolerance test require a specific separator API or solver-interface source.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary-Solution Separator Callbacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Callback contract for separation at a supplied point not assumed LP-optimal or feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a point \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), model revision \(r\), search scope \(s\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), without assuming that \(y\) is feasible or LP-optimal. The callback returns a finite cut set \(C\) and an outcome status. Each returned \(c=(a,
\beta)\) must be valid for its declared scope and carry derivation provenance; it is marked separating precisely when \(a^\top y-
\beta>\varepsilon\). Failure to find such a cut is a normal outcome distinct from invalid input or execution failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The callback separates any supplied point without assuming feasibility or LP optimality and returns scoped, provenance-bearing cuts plus an explicit outcome.
assumptions_latex: The supplied point has the model's ambient dimension.
The model revision, search scope, and tolerance are supplied explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Every separating \(c\in C\) satisfies \(a^\top y-
\beta>\varepsilon\) and remains valid throughout its declared scope.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits arbitrary-point separation and clearly avoids feasibility or LP-optimality assumptions, but its status taxonomy, provenance and scope obligations, and strict violation convention are uncited interface requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Outcome Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract callback outcome contract, independent of solver-specific enumeration names.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a separator invocation return an outcome in \(\mathcal R=\{\mathrm{didNotRun},\mathrm{noCut},\mathrm{separated},\mathrm{cutoff},\mathrm{error}\}\). The meanings are: \(\mathrm{didNotRun}\), no separation attempt occurred; \(\mathrm{noCut}\), separation completed without submitting an admissible violated cut; \(\mathrm{separated}\), at least one admissible cut was submitted; \(\mathrm{cutoff}\), the callback established that the current node or candidate has no feasible completion; and \(\mathrm{error}\), the callback failed and its mathematical output must not be used. An outcome reports the strongest event established during that invocation and does not, by itself, assert global optimality or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator reports whether it was skipped, found no cut, submitted cuts, proved the current search object infeasible, or failed; none of these outcomes alone proves global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The solver distinguishes callback execution, cut submission, local cutoff, and failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned value uniquely specifies the callback's strongest established outcome for the invocation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the outcome-semantics container and is internally coherent, but the proposed outcome set, the ordering by strongest event, and the meanings of cutoff and error are API-contract claims with no cited source. An authoritative separator API reference with a specific result-code locator is required.

children.title: Separator Priority Interface
children.top_down_role: Plugin metadata and controls governing separator precedence.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Priority Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer priority metadata for ordering simultaneously eligible separator callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each registered separator \(s\), the priority interface supplies an integer \(p(s)\). Whenever a finite set \(E\) of separators is simultaneously eligible at the same scheduling point, the scheduler orders distinct \(s,t\in E\) so that \(p(s)>p(t)\) implies that \(s\) is considered before \(t\). Equal priorities impose no relative order unless a separate deterministic tie-break rule is declared. Priority affects consideration order only: it neither makes an ineligible separator eligible nor guarantees invocation after an earlier separator changes the relaxation, cuts off the node, or terminates the separation round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eligible separators with larger integer priorities are considered first; ties need a separate rule, and priority neither creates eligibility nor guarantees execution.
assumptions_latex: Only separators eligible at the same scheduling point are compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For eligible \(s,t\), \(p(s)>p(t)\) implies that \(s\) precedes \(t\) in consideration order.

notation.meaning: Separators eligible at one scheduling point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is well scoped to the priority interface, but higher-first ordering, tie behavior, and the distinction between consideration and invocation are solver-specific scheduling semantics unsupported by evidence.

children.title: Separator Timing Interface
children.top_down_role: Plugin metadata and controls governing eligible invocation phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Timing Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility predicate for execution at declared branch-and-cut scheduling points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) be the solver's finite set of separation timing points, and let a separator \(s\) declare an allowed set \(T_s\subseteq\mathcal T\). At a callback opportunity with timing label \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), timing eligibility is the predicate \(\tau\in T_s\). Invocation is permitted only when this predicate holds and all independent frequency, depth, delayed-execution, and solver-state conditions also hold. Thus a timing declaration is a necessary scheduling filter, not a promise that \(s\) will execute. If \(T_s=\varnothing\), the separator is timing-ineligible at every opportunity until its metadata changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator may run only at declared timing points and when every other scheduling condition holds; timing eligibility does not guarantee invocation.
assumptions_latex: Each callback opportunity has a well-defined timing label \(\tau\in\mathcal T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Timing eligibility of \(s\) at \(\tau\) holds exactly when \(\tau\in T_s\).

notation.meaning: Timing points allowed for separator s.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically consistent and fits the timing-interface leaf, but the timing-set abstraction and its interaction with frequency, depth, delay, and solver state require an authoritative separator API source.

children.title: Scheduler Metadata Contract
children.top_down_role: Scheduler-facing declarations connecting separator precedence with timing eligibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduler Metadata Contract
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined eligibility and ordering contract for separator scheduling metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate with each separator \(s\) metadata \(M_s=(p_s,T_s,f_s,d_s,\delta_s)\), consisting of priority, allowed timings, frequency, maximum depth, and delayed-execution flag. At scheduling state \(q\), define \(s\) to be eligible exactly when the timing of \(q\) lies in \(T_s\), its invocation count or node index satisfies \(f_s\), its current depth does not exceed \(d_s\), and the delayed-execution policy represented by \(\delta_s\) permits execution. The scheduler considers eligible separators in nonincreasing \(p_s\), subject to its tie-break rule, and may stop after cutoff, state invalidation, or round termination.
