knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal degeneracy of a standard-form LP relaxation at an optimal basic feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the relaxation \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\) with objective \(\min\{c^\top x:x\in P\}\). For a basis \(B\) of \(A\), let \(x_B=B^{-1}b\) and set all nonbasic variables to zero. An optimal basic feasible solution associated with \(B\) is degenerate when \(x_B\ge 0\), \(c^\top x\) is optimal over \(P\), and at least one component of \(x_B\) equals zero. The relaxation is degenerate at an optimal point when that point admits such an optimal degenerate basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP relaxation is degenerate at an optimum when an optimal basis has at least one zero basic variable.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(P\neq\varnothing\) and the relaxation has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists i\in B:(x_B)_i=0\).

notation.meaning: Basis matrix formed from columns of A.

review_flags: Exact source for LP degeneracy definition not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard degeneracy definition is plausible and fits the leaf, but no cited source supports it. Moreover, B is described as a basis matrix while the conclusion uses i\in B as though B were an index set.

children.title: Basis Churn
children.top_down_role: Repeated basis changes that yield little durable relaxation progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Churn
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition for repeated LP basis changes without corresponding relaxation progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((B_t,x^t,z_t)_{t=0}^T\) be consecutive reoptimization states, where \(B_t\) is the simplex basis, \(x^t\) the primal solution, and \(z_t=c^\top x^t\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_z\ge 0\) and an integer \(K\ge 1\), basis churn occurs on a window \(W\) when at least \(K\) indices \(t\in W\) satisfy \(B_{t+1}\ne B_t\), while \(\lVert x^{t+1}-x^t\rVert\le\varepsilon_x\) and \(|z_{t+1}-z_t|\le\varepsilon_z\). Thus combinatorial basis activity persists without material primal or objective movement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis churn is a sustained sequence of basis changes whose primal solutions and objective values remain essentially unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Consecutive states solve the same relaxation or its explicitly tracked incremental modification.
The tolerances and observation window are fixed before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\#\{t\in W:B_{t+1}\ne B_t,\ \lVert x^{t+1}-x^t\rVert\le\varepsilon_x,\ |z_{t+1}-z_t|\le\varepsilon_z\}\ge K\).

notation.meaning: Simplex basis at reoptimization state t.

review_flags: Operational threshold definition requires cut-management or solver reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Basis Churn, but K, the monitoring window, tolerances, and treatment of incrementally modified relaxations constitute an unsourced operational convention.

children.title: Degeneracy-Driven Churn
children.top_down_role: Feedback between degeneracy and unstable basis evolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Driven Churn
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic condition attributing basis churn to zero-length pivots at degenerate relaxation optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For consecutive simplex states \((B_t,x^t,z_t)\), degeneracy-driven churn is present on a window \(W\) if basis churn occurs and every counted transition is a degenerate pivot: the leaving basic variable has value zero before the pivot, \(B_{t+1}\ne B_t\), and \(x^{t+1}=x^t\), \(z_{t+1}=z_t\) up to prescribed tolerances. A sufficient diagnostic requires at least \(K\) such transitions in \(W\). This condition distinguishes degeneracy-induced basis motion from basis changes caused by genuine movement along an improving edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Churn is degeneracy-driven when repeated zero-length pivots change the basis but leave the relaxation point and objective unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The LP solver exposes consecutive bases and the leaving basic-variable value.
Numerical equality is interpreted using fixed primal and objective tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\#\{t\in W:B_{t+1}\ne B_t,\ (x^t)_{\ell_t}=0,\ x^{t+1}\approx x^t,\ z_{t+1}\approx z_t\}\ge K\).

notation.meaning: Index of the basic variable leaving at transition t.

review_flags: Causal diagnostic and tolerance convention need authoritative sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the causal attribution, K-transition diagnostic, and approximate equalities require an authoritative simplex or solver source and explicit tolerance definitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Redundant Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy of repeatedly proposed separation inequalities relative to the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_t\) be the current relaxation and let separator calls produce inequalities \(a_k^\top x\le\beta_k\). A generated inequality is redundant at call \(k\) when \(\sup_{x\in P_t}(a_k^\top x-\beta_k)\le\varepsilon\), or when it is equivalent within tolerance to an inequality already retained. Repeated redundant generation occurs on a window \(W\) when at least \(K\) generated inequalities are redundant and no accepted member of that subsequence produces relaxation-bound improvement exceeding \(\delta\). Scaling-equivalent inequalities are compared after a fixed normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated redundant generation means repeatedly producing cuts already implied by, or duplicating, the current relaxation without meaningful bound improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(P_t\) is nonempty.
Redundancy, equivalence, and bound-improvement tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\#\{k\in W:\sup_{x\in P_t}(a_k^\top x-\beta_k)\le\varepsilon\ \text{or the cut duplicates a retained cut}\}\ge K\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation present during the monitored separation round.

review_flags: Cut-equivalence and monitoring-window definition need a cut-management source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition fits the failure topic, but P_t is not related clearly to call k, and the duplication normalization, K-window rule, and bound-gain threshold are unsourced conventions.

children.title: Separator Starvation
children.top_down_role: Useful separators receiving insufficient execution opportunities.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Starvation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Window-based starvation condition for an eligible separator in a managed portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite separator portfolio. For \(s\in S\) and calls \(t\) in a window \(W\), let \(e_{s,t}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate eligibility, \(u_{s,t}\in\{0,1\}\) invocation, and \(q_{s,t}\ge0\) an estimated opportunity score. Separator \(s\) is starved on \(W\) when it is eligible with material opportunity at least \(K\) times but is never invoked: \(\sum_{t\in W}e_{s,t}\mathbf 1\{q_{s,t}\ge\eta\}\ge K\) and \(\sum_{t\in W}u_{s,t}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator is starved when it repeatedly qualifies and has material estimated opportunity but receives no invocation during the monitoring window.
assumptions_latex: Eligibility and opportunity scores are recorded before portfolio selection.
\(K\ge1\) and \(\eta\ge0\) are fixed monitoring parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{t\in W}e_{s,t}\mathbf 1\{q_{s,t}\ge\eta\}\ge K\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_{t\in W}u_{s,t}=0\).

notation.meaning: Eligibility indicator for separator s at call t.

review_flags: Starvation metric and thresholds are implementation-dependent and unsourced.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent starvation condition, but the opportunity score, eligibility semantics, and zero-invocation threshold are implementation-dependent and lack a supporting source.

children.title: Separator Overuse
children.top_down_role: Separators receiving disproportionate execution despite limited value.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Overuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-share condition identifying excessive use of one separator relative to realized utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a separator \(s\) over a window \(W\), let \(r_{s,t}\ge0\) be consumed resource and \(g_{s,t}\ge0\) realized utility, such as accepted-cut efficacy or bound gain. Define \(R_s=\sum_{t\in W}r_{s,t}\), \(R=\sum_{j\in S}\sum_{t\in W}r_{j,t}\), and \(G_s=\sum_{t\in W}g_{s,t}\). Separator \(s\) is overused when \(R_s/R\ge\rho\) while \(G_s/R_s\le\gamma\), with \(R_s>0\), for prescribed share and yield thresholds \(\rho\) and \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator is overused when it consumes a large portfolio resource share while delivering utility per unit resource below a fixed threshold.
assumptions_latex: All separator resources are measured in a common nonnegative unit.
Utility attribution and thresholds are fixed for the monitoring window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_s>0,\quad R_s/R\ge\rho,\quad G_s/R_s\le\gamma\).

notation.meaning: Realized utility attributed to separator s.

review_flags: Resource and utility metric requires solver-specific validation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Separator Overuse, but resource comparability, utility attribution, and the share and yield thresholds are solver-policy choices without cited support.

children.title: Portfolio Imbalance Detection
children.top_down_role: Signals revealing persistent underallocation or overallocation across separator families.

knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Imbalance Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window detector combining starvation and resource-adjusted overuse tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a separator set \(S\), monitoring window \(W\), eligibility, invocation, resource, and utility logs, and thresholds \(K,\eta,\rho,\gamma\). For each \(s\in S\), compute the eligible-opportunity count \(E_s=\sum_{t\in W}e_{s,t}\mathbf 1\{q_{s,t}\ge\eta\}\), invocation count \(U_s=\sum_{t\in W}u_{s,t}\), resource \(R_s\), and utility \(G_s\). Flag starvation if \(E_s\ge K\) and \(U_s=0\). Flag overuse if \(R_s>0\), \(R_s/\sum_jR_j\ge\rho\), and \(G_s/R_s\le\gamma\). Output all flags with their computed statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute per-separator opportunity, invocation, resource, and utility statistics; then report separators satisfying the configured starvation or overuse tests.
assumptions_latex: The log covers one consistently defined window.
The total portfolio resource is positive when the overuse test is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{(s,\mathrm{starved}):E_s\ge K,\ U_s=0\}\cup\{(s,\mathrm{overused}):R_s>0,\ R_s/\sum_jR_j\ge\rho,\ G_s/R_s\le\gamma\}\).
review_flags: Detector is a formalized operational rule without supplied algorithmic source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but the detector merely combines two unsourced operational tests and has no inspectable algorithmic or implementation citation.

children.title: Usage Rebalancing Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Protective scheduling responses to separator portfolio imbalance.

knowledge_statements.title: Usage Rebalancing Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quota-and-cap controller that rebalances separator use without weakening cut-validity checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input imbalance flags, separator scores \(q_s\), resource shares \(p_s\), exploration floor \(\alpha>0\), and overuse cap \(\bar p<1\). At each eligible call, reserve at least an \(\alpha\)-fraction of portfolio opportunities for non-overused separators; exclude no separator solely because its recent utility is zero; and prevent an overused separator from receiving additional work while \(p_s>\bar p\), unless every alternative is ineligible. Apply the ordinary validity and numerical-acceptance tests to every generated cut. Stop rebalancing when all flags clear or the monitoring horizon ends.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reserve exploration for neglected separators and cap overused ones, while retaining all ordinary cut-validity and numerical-acceptance checks.
assumptions_latex: At least one separator is eligible at each controlled call.
Resource shares are updated after each invocation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_s\le\bar p\) is enforced for flagged overuse whenever an eligible alternative exists, while exploration mass is at least \(\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Current resource share of separator s.
Resource-share cap for an overused separator.

review_flags: Controller policy and safety guarantees require an implementation or algorithm source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for the leaf, but the exploration reservation, overuse cap, exception rule, and claimed enforcement behavior require a concrete algorithm or solver-policy source.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Bloat
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic failure boundary for relaxation growth with vanishing benefit per retained row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\supseteq P_1\supseteq\cdots\) be relaxations formed by retaining generated inequalities, let \(m_t\) be the retained-row count, and let \(z_t\) be the relaxation bound for a minimization problem. Relaxation bloat occurs along an infinite subsequence when \(m_t\to\infty\), solve cost \(C_t\to\infty\), and marginal bound gain per added row vanishes: \((z_t-z_{t-1})/(m_t-m_{t-1})\to0\) whenever \(m_t>m_{t-1}\). A finite-window diagnostic replaces these limits by configured size, cost, and marginal-gain thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation bloat is unbounded retained-row and solve-cost growth accompanied by vanishing bound improvement per added row.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem, so stronger relaxation bounds are nondecreasing.
\(C_t\) measures relaxation solution cost consistently across rounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_t\to\infty,\quad C_t\to\infty,\quad (z_t-z_{t-1})/(m_t-m_{t-1})\to0\) along the monitored subsequence.

notation.meaning: Number of retained relaxation rows after round t.
Relaxation lower bound after round t.
Cost of solving or reoptimizing the relaxation.

review_flags: Proposed asymptotic diagnostic requires cut-pool management sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is a suitable role, but the proposed asymptotic characterization is not a standard sourced definition. The meaning of all three limits holding along one subsequence and the handling of rounds with no added rows also need clarification.

children.title: User-Cut Semantics
children.top_down_role: Correctness role and relaxation scope of user-cut submissions.

knowledge_statements.title: User-Cut Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-interface semantics of a user cut relative to the declared integer-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_{\mathrm{LP}}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the declared continuous relaxation and \(X_I\subseteq X_{\mathrm{LP}}\) its declared integer-feasible set. An inequality \(a^\top x\le\beta\) has user-cut semantics when it is globally valid for every point of \(X_I\), but may exclude points of \(X_{\mathrm{LP}}\setminus\operatorname{conv}(X_I)\). Adding it strengthens the relaxation to \(X_{\mathrm{LP}}\cap\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\) without changing \(X_I\). It is therefore not a mechanism for introducing a missing constraint that excludes a declared integer-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A user cut may remove fractional relaxation points but must be valid for every integer-feasible solution of the declared model.
assumptions_latex: The declared integer-feasible set is well defined.
The inequality is interpreted with the solver's feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_I\subseteq\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\) and the declared integer-feasible set is unchanged.
review_flags: Solver callback documentation supporting user-cut semantics was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical distinction is plausible and the definition fits the leaf, but user-cut callback obligations are solver-interface semantics and require specific vendor documentation with a locator.

children.title: Lazy-Constraint Semantics
children.top_down_role: Correctness role and model-completeness scope of lazy-constraint submissions.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy-Constraint Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-interface semantics of an omitted defining constraint enforced on candidate integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_D\) be the integer-feasible set of the explicitly declared model and let the intended set be \(X_I=X_D\cap\bigcap_{j\in J}\{x:g_j(x)\le0\}\). A constraint \(g_j(x)\le0\) has lazy-constraint semantics when it is a defining condition of \(X_I\) intentionally omitted from the initial formulation and is enforced whenever a candidate integer solution violates it. Unlike a user cut, it need not be valid for every point of \(X_D\); its purpose is to remove candidates in \(X_D\setminus X_I\). Correct termination requires every accepted incumbent to satisfy all such constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lazy constraint is an omitted defining constraint checked on candidate integer solutions; it may exclude integer-feasible points of the explicit model.
assumptions_latex: The callback can identify every violated omitted constraint needed for an examined candidate.
Accepted incumbents are subjected to the prescribed lazy-constraint checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) may be accepted as intended-feasible only if \(x\in X_D\) and \(g_j(x)\le0\) for every \(j\in J\).

notation.meaning: Integer-feasible set of the explicitly declared model.
Intended integer-feasible set after omitted constraints are imposed.

review_flags: Solver callback documentation supporting lazy-constraint semantics was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but enforcement timing, candidate coverage, and incumbent acceptance guarantees vary by solver and require specific callback documentation.

children.title: User-Cut Misclassification
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by treating required lazy constraints as optional relaxation cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: User-Cut Misclassification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary crossed when a defining lazy constraint is submitted through a user-cut interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_D\) be the declared integer-feasible set and \(X_I\subsetneq X_D\) the intended set after imposing an omitted defining inequality \(a^\top x\le\beta\). Misclassification occurs when this inequality is submitted as a user cut although there exists \(\bar x\in X_D\) with \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\). The inequality then violates the user-cut validity obligation relative to \(X_D\). If it is not separately enforced through a mechanism that checks candidate integer solutions, the solver interface provides no valid certificate that returned incumbents belong to \(X_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A defining constraint is misclassified as a user cut when it excludes an integer-feasible point of the declared model, violating the user-cut contract.
assumptions_latex: \(X_I=X_D\cap\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\).
The user-cut interface requires validity for all of \(X_D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\bar x\in X_D:a^\top\bar x>\beta\), so the submitted inequality is not a valid user cut for \(X_D\).

notation.meaning: Declared-feasible point excluded by the omitted defining inequality.

review_flags: Exact consequences depend on solver callback guarantees and require vendor documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity violation is mathematically plausible and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but the claimed consequences for incumbent certification depend on the solver's user-cut and lazy-constraint guarantees and need vendor documentation.

children.title: Lazy-Constraint Misclassification
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by routing ordinary strengthening cuts through lazy-constraint enforcement.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n\) is the original mixed-integer domain and \(F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le 0\ \forall j\in J\}\) is the intended feasible set.
A callback labels a member of \(\{g_j(x)\le 0:j\in J\}\) as a user cut rather than as a lazy constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) need not equal the feasible set certified by the solver, and an incumbent in \(X\setminus F\) may be accepted.

notation.meaning: Intended feasible set including all deferred constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for treating feasibility-defining deferred constraints as relaxation-strengthening cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the original mixed-integer domain and let \(F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le 0\text{ for every }j\in J\}\). A lazy-constraint misclassification occurs when some feasibility-defining inequality \(g_j(x)\le 0\) is submitted only through an interface whose contract does not require enforcement at every candidate integer solution. If the solver may omit that inequality when certifying an incumbent, then it can accept \(\bar x\in X\) with \(g_j(\bar x)>0\). Consequently, the solver may optimize over a strict superset of \(F\), so incumbent feasibility and the reported objective bound need not be valid for the intended model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-defining deferred constraint submitted only as a user cut may be skipped at an incumbent, allowing an infeasible solution and invalid objective claims.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy-Constraint Misclassification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the infeasible-incumbent mechanism is plausible. However, no source establishes the solver-specific distinction between user cuts and lazy constraints. The claim that the reported objective bound itself may be invalid is also too broad: optimizing over a relaxation can preserve a valid dual bound while invalidating incumbent feasibility or an optimality claim.

assumptions_latex: A branch-and-cut node \(v\) has local domain \(D_v\), while an inequality \(a^Tx\le b\) is valid only on \(D_v\cap F\).
The inequality is installed at a node \(w\) for which \(D_w\nsubseteq D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global search may exclude feasible points in \(F\cap D_w\), invalidating completeness and possibly the reported optimum.

notation.meaning: Domain induced by branching decisions at node v.
Feasible set of the original model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scope failure when a node-local valid inequality is enforced outside its validity subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set and let \(D_v\) denote the domain defined by branching decisions at node \(v\). Suppose \(a^Tx\le b\) is valid for \(F\cap D_v\), but not necessarily for all of \(F\). Local-cut scope leakage occurs if this inequality is enforced at a node \(w\) with \(D_w\nsubseteq D_v\), or globally. If there exists \(x^*\in F\cap D_w\) satisfying \(a^Tx^*>b\), the leaked cut removes a feasible solution. The resulting tree no longer represents a valid partition or relaxation of the original problem, so pruning, optimality, and infeasibility conclusions derived from it may be incorrect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut valid only under one node's branching assumptions can delete feasible solutions if propagated globally or into an unrelated subtree.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Cut Scope Leakage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and conditional feasible-point deletion claim fit the leaf. A source is required for the branch-and-cut scope contract and the consequences of installing a local cut outside its valid subtree. The statement that the tree ceases to be a valid partition is imprecise; the branching domains may still partition the search space even though node relaxations or pruning certificates become invalid.

assumptions_latex: A presolve transformation \(T\) maps original variables \(x\) to presolved variables \(y=T(x)\) and admits a reconstruction map on feasible points.
A callback translates an original-space inequality \(a^Tx\le b\) into \(\tilde a^Ty\le\tilde b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A translation error can produce an invalid cut or fail to separate the intended violating point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for translating callback points and cuts across presolve transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let presolve map original variables \(x\) to presolved variables \(y=T(x)\), preserving the original feasible set through a valid reconstruction map. For an original-space inequality \(a^Tx\le b\), its presolved image \(\tilde a^Ty\le\tilde b\) must satisfy \(a^Tx\le b\) if and only if \(\tilde a^TT(x)\le\tilde b\) for every reconstructible feasible \(x\). A presolve mapping error is any violation of this equivalence, including incorrect indices, substitutions, scaling, or eliminated-variable constants. Such an error can make a submitted inequality invalid in presolved space or make it fail to cut the intended violating callback point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback translation is erroneous when a cut and its presolved image are not equivalent on reconstructible feasible points, causing invalid or ineffective separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Mapping Errors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general presolve section does not establish callback-space translation semantics or the asserted equivalence. Presolve commonly requires a reconstruction map from presolved to original space, so modeling it solely as y=T(x) may not cover eliminations and substitutions. Equivalence only on feasible original points also does not ensure separation of a relaxation callback point. In addition, \(\tilde a^TT(x)\) ambiguously encodes transpose notation.

assumptions_latex: A callback state \(s_k\) determines the cuts returned at invocation \(k\).
Two executions receive the same model, parameters, callback event, point, and declared random seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If their returned cut sets differ, the callback is not reproducible from its declared inputs and may induce different search trees or outcomes.

notation.meaning: Cut set returned by the callback.
Deterministic callback transition and output map.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reproducibility failure caused by callback state not determined by declared inputs and event history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Model a callback invocation by \((s_{k+1},C_k)=\Phi(s_k,e_k,z_k)\), where \(e_k\) is the solver event, \(z_k\) is the callback point, and \(C_k\) is the returned cut set. Callback state is nondeterministic when two executions with identical model data, parameters, declared seed, initial state, and identical ordered histories \((e_i,z_i)\) can produce different \(C_k\). Causes include unsynchronized shared mutation, dependence on thread scheduling, and unordered iteration with stateful tie-breaking. Because different valid cuts can alter node processing and termination paths, such nondeterminism defeats replay-based diagnosis and can expose latent state or interface errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback is nondeterministic when identical declared inputs and event histories can yield different cuts, often through shared mutable state or thread scheduling.
knowledge_statements.title: Nondeterministic Callback State

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the variables and deterministic transition model are introduced consistently. No source supports the assumed callback concurrency/replay contract, the role of ordered histories and seeds, or the stated operational consequences across solver implementations.

assumptions_latex: The intended set is \(F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le0\ \forall j\in J\}\), with some constraints enforced only by a callback.
The solver considers an integer candidate \(\bar x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the callback is not invoked or does not add every violated required constraint, \(\bar x\notin F\) may be accepted as feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for omitted checking or submission of deferred feasibility constraints at integer candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le0\text{ for all }j\in J\}\), where constraints indexed by \(J\) are omitted from the initial relaxation and must be enforced lazily. Correct enforcement requires that every candidate integer solution \(\bar x\in X\) be checked and, whenever \(g_j(\bar x)>0\), at least one violated feasibility-defining constraint be submitted before \(\bar x\) can be accepted. Missing lazy-constraint enforcement occurs when this check or submission is absent on any acceptance path. Then an integer point in \(X\setminus F\) may become an incumbent, and termination may report a solution or objective value that is invalid for the intended model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every integer candidate must be checked against deferred feasibility constraints; omitting any acceptance-path check can admit an infeasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Missing Lazy-Constraint Enforcement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf and the mathematical failure mechanism is coherent. An authoritative solver-interface source is required to establish which candidate-acceptance paths invoke lazy-constraint checks and what submission behavior prevents acceptance of a violating incumbent.

children.title: Failure Detection Controls
children.top_down_role: Monitoring controls for recognizing unreliable or counterproductive separation behavior.

assumptions_latex: Each separation invocation produces a candidate point \(x^k\), returned inequalities, and observable numerical and state metadata.
Validity and violation are evaluated using declared tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{val}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The control raises a typed failure whenever a returned cut is invalid, insufficiently violated, malformed, scope-inconsistent, or nonreproducible under replay.

notation.meaning: Candidate point at separation invocation k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable detection condition for mathematical, numerical, scope, and replay failures in separation callbacks.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Ease of detecting errors in the model p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each invocation \(k\), record the callback context, point \(x^k\), state digest, and every returned inequality \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\). A failure detector flags the invocation if any inequality violates a trusted validity test by more than \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{val}}\), has nonfinite coefficients, does not satisfy \(a_i^Tx^k>b_i+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}\) when separation is claimed, or is installed outside its declared scope. It also flags an integer candidate rejected without a recorded violated lazy constraint, and flags replay inconsistency when identical recorded inputs yield different normalized cut sets. Each flag must retain the triggering predicate and data needed for independent checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Log each callback and flag invalid, malformed, nonseparating, scope-inconsistent, unjustified incumbent rejection, or replay-inconsistent behavior using declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Detection Controls

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Ease of detecting errors in the model p. 37

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is a plausible role for checkable detection controls, but the cited textbook sections provide only generic model-error and branch-and-cut context. They do not support the detailed validity oracle, normalized-cut replay test, scope checks, lazy-rejection logging requirement, or tolerance predicates stated here. Those operational controls require a direct methodological or solver-interface source.

children.title: Safeguard Activation Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies governing when protective controls modify or suspend separation.

assumptions_latex: A detector emits a severity vector \(r_k\) from validity, numerical, stagnation, scope, and replay checks.
Available safeguards are ordered by increasing disruption and have declared activation thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy activates the least disruptive safeguard whose precondition covers \(r_k\), while any validity or scope breach triggers immediate quarantine.

notation.meaning: Ordered safeguards from least to most disruptive.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic policy mapping detected separation failures to minimally disruptive protective actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\) be the detector output at invocation \(k\), and order safeguards \((S_1,\ldots,S_m)\) from least to most disruptive. Each safeguard \(S_j\) has an activation predicate \(P_j(r_k,h_k)\), where \(h_k\) is the recorded failure history. If \(r_k\) reports a cut-validity or scope breach, quarantine the cut and suspend the responsible separator immediately. Otherwise choose the smallest \(j\) satisfying \(P_j(r_k,h_k)\), apply \(S_j\), and record its inputs and effect. If no predicate holds, continue unchanged. Repeated activation without restored progress increments severity, ensuring that safeguards do not cycle indefinitely without escalation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map each detected failure deterministically to the least disruptive applicable safeguard, but quarantine validity or scope breaches immediately and escalate repeated failures.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Activation Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits a policy that maps detector outputs to actions, and the notation is internally consistent. The ordering by disruption, immediate quarantine rule, and severity-escalation behavior are substantive design choices with no cited support; a source must establish or motivate this policy.

children.title: Recovery Escalation Paths
children.top_down_role: Escalating responses when initial separation safeguards do not restore reliable behavior.

assumptions_latex: Recovery levels \((R_0,\ldots,R_q)\) are ordered by increasing cost and decreasing reliance on the failing separator.
At each level, a measurable success predicate \(Q_j\) and finite retry budget \(B_j\) are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure either restores certified progress, terminates with a valid solver status, or emits an auditable unresolved-failure record.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite escalation protocol from local retry through separator disablement to certified termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given ordered recovery levels \((R_0,R_1,\ldots,R_q)\), begin at the least costly level compatible with the detected failure. At level \(j\), execute \(R_j\) for at most \(B_j\) attempts and evaluate the declared predicate \(Q_j\), which must require restored valid separation or another certified form of progress. If \(Q_j\) holds, resume search and retain the recovery record. Otherwise advance to \(R_{j+1}\). Levels may include recomputation at tighter tolerances, state reset, separator quarantine, fallback to a trusted formulation, and controlled termination. After level \(q\) fails, stop without claiming unsupported feasibility or optimality and emit the complete failure trace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try bounded recovery levels in order, escalating from recomputation to quarantine or trusted fallback; if all fail, terminate without unsupported correctness claims.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Escalation Paths

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the recovery-path leaf, and finite retry budgets make the escalation procedure well specified. The particular recovery levels, certified-progress requirement, fallback behavior, and terminal guarantees are unsupported design claims and require an authoritative source.
